* الشخير بكسر الشين والخاء مشددة # * الحكم بن عتيبة هو بتاء مثناة من فوق ثم مثناة من تحت ثم موحدة # * المحيى والممات الحياة والموت # * أوزعهم إلا ألههم # * حمدأ يوافي نعمة اي يصل إليها فيحصلها # * ويكافئ مزيده هو بهمزة آخر يكافئ ومعناه يقوم بشكر ما زادنا من النعم # * مجالد الراوي عن الشعبي بالجيم وكسر اللام # * الصيمري بفتح الصاد المهملة والميم وقيل بضم الميم وهو غريب # # وقد بسطت بيانه في تهذيب الأسماء واللغات فهذه أحرف وجيزة في ضبط مشكل ما وقع في هذا الكتاب وما بقي منها تركته لظهوره وما ذكرته من الظاهر قصدت بيانه لمن لا يخالط العلماء، فإنه ينتفع به إن شاء الله تعالى. # * * * # هذا آخر ما تيسر مهه هذا الكتاب، وهو نبذة مختصرة بالنسبة إلى آداب القراء. # ولكن حملني على اختصاره ما ذكرته في أول الكتاب. # وأنا أسأل الله العظيم أن ينفع به النفع العميم، لي ولأحبابي، وكل ناظر فيه وسائر المسلمين في الدارين. # والحمد الله رب العالمين حمدا يوافي نعمه ويكافي مزيده، وصلاته وسلامه الأكملان على سيدنا محمد، وعلى آل محمد، وأصحابه أجمعين والحمد الله رب العالمين. # اه. إلى هنا تم كتاب التبيان. # | الفوائد المزيدة على الكتاب | | لطيفة # # قال ابن الجوزي في كتاب " مناقب الامام أحمد بن حنبل " ص 434 في الباب الحادي والتسعين في ذكر المنامات التي رآها أحمد بن حنبل رضي الله تعالى عنه: أخبرنا عبد الملك بن أبي القاسم، قال: أنا عبد الله بن محمد الانصاري، قال: أنا محمد بن عبد الجليل بن أحمد، قال: أنا محمد بن أحمد بن إبراهيم، وأخبرنا ابن ناصر، قال: أنبأنا أبو علي الحسن بن أحمد، قال: أنا أبو محمد الخلال، قال: أنا عبيد الله بن عبد الرحمن الزهري، قالا: حدثنا أحمد بن محمد بن معثم، قال: سمعت عبد العزيز بن أحمد النهاوندي قال: سمعت عبد الله بن أحمد بن حنبل قال: سمعت أبي يقول: * رأيت رب العزة في المنام فقلت: يا رب ما أفضل ما تقرب به المتقربون إليك؟ * فقال: كلامي يا أحمد # * قال فقلت: يا رب بفهم أو بغير فهم؟ # # * قال: بفهم وبغير فهم. اه. # أنظر مناقب الامام أحمد، مطبعة دار الافاق الجديدة ط الثانية 1977 م. | | لطيفة # # عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أنه قال: ثمان أيات نزلت في سورة النساء خير لهذه الامة مما طلعت عليه الشمس: # * 1 -: (يريد الله ليبين لكم ويهديكم سنن الذين من قبلكم ويتوب عليكم) . # * 2 -: (والله يريد أن يتوب عليكم ويريد الذين يتبعون الشهوات أن تميلوا ميلا عظيما) . # ، 3 -: (يريد الله أن يخفف عنكم وخلق الانسان ضعيفا) . # * 4 -: (إن تجتنبوا كبائر ما تنهون عنه نكفر عنكم سيئاتكم وندخلكم مدخلا كريما) . # * 5 -: (إن الله لا يظلم مثقال ذرة وإن تك حسنة يضاعفها ويؤت من لدنه أجرا عظيما) . # * 6 -: (ومن يعمل سوءا أو يظلم نفسه ثم يستغفر الله يجد الله غفورا رحيما) . # * 7 -: (إن الله لا يغفر أن يشرك به ويغفر ما دون ذلك لمن يشاء) . # * 8 -: (والذين ءامنوا بالله ورسله، ولم يفرقوا بين أحد منهم # # أولئك سوف يؤتيهم أجورهم وكان الله غفورا رحيما) . # اه الاتقان 2 / 206 | لطيفة # * 1 -: إن أعظم آية في القرآن، (الله لا إله إلا هو الحي القيوم) . # * 2 -: وأعدل آية في القرآن، (إن الله يأمر بالعدل والاحسان وإيتائ ذى القربى) الاية ... * 3 -: وأخوف آية في القرآن، (فمن يعمل مثقال ذرة خيرا يره (7) ومن يعمل مثقال ذرة شرا يره) . # * 4 -: وأرجي آية في القرآن، (قل يعبادي الذين أسرفوا على أنفسهم لا تقنطوا من رحمة الله) الاية ... وقيل: (ولسوف يعطيك ربك فترضى) . # * 5 -: وأحزن آية في القرآن، (من يعمل سوءا يجزيه) . # * 6 -: وأشد آية في القرآن، - أي على أهل النار - (فذوقوا فلن نزيد كم إلا عذابا) . # * 7 -: وعن علي كرم الله وجهه: أحب آية إلى في القرآن، (إن الله لا يغفرأن يشرك به ويغفر ما دون ذلك لمن يشاء) . # * 8 -: وأفضل آية في القرآن، (وما أصابكم من مصيبة فبما كسبت أيديكم ويعفوا عن كثير) . # اه الاتقان 2 / 205 # | كلمة الختام # لقد تم - والحمد الله تعالى - تنقيح الطبعة الثالثة لكتاب التبيان، وإبرازها في ثوبها الجديد، وطباعتها الانيقة في المدينة المنورة، على ساكنها أفضل التحية، وأطيب الصلاة، وأتم التسليم، أيام هجرتي في أوائل الحرم في 1414 ه. # فالله أسأل أن ينظمني في سلك حملة القرآن، الذين يحلون حلاله، ويحرمون حرامه، ويرعون حدوده، ويجيدون تلاوته، وأن يميتني على حبهم، وأن يحشرني في زمرتهم وتحت لوائهم فأهل القرآن أهل الله، وسدنة كتابه، وأن يتقبل مني ما قدمت من عمل، وأن يمنحني حسن الختام عند انتهاء الاجل # نزيل المدينة المنورة # الفقير إليه تعالى # محمد محمود الحجار
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ض-ب-ط (ḍād-bā-ṭā)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To guard, preserve, retain firmly; to correct, to set right; the root denotes the act of grasping something firmly and protecting it from error or loss.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the context of scholarly transmission, it signifies the precise and meticulous preservation of textual wording, ensuring its accurate pronunciation and orthography.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal meaning is to bind or tie something tightly. Here it is used metaphorically for the intellectual "binding" of words to prevent them from straying or being corrupted.
- Sībawayh Rule: Chapter on the precision of nomenclature (bāb al-asmāʾ) — This chapter is a lexical appendix, where the author systematically defines and corrects the pronunciation of proper nouns, technical terms, and rare linguistic forms mentioned throughout the book, following the established conventions of Arabic philology.
chapters.translation:
I say: The tenth chapter concerns the correction of the wording of the names and linguistic forms mentioned in this book, arranged according to their order of occurrence. They are numerous, and a complete exposition of their correction, clarification, and elaboration would require a voluminous tome. However, I shall point to them with the most concise of indications and allude to their meanings with the briefest of expressions, confining myself to the most correct opinion in most cases.

The first of these occurs in the introduction.

**Al-Ḥamd** (الحمد): It is praise (al-thanāʾ) with beautiful attributes, and it is specific to God, may He be exalted, the Bestower of favors. It is also said to mean something else.

**Al-Mannān** (المنان): We have related from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may God honor his face, that its meaning is "The One who begins with bestowal before the asking."

**Al-Ṭawl** (الطول): It means wealth and abundance.

**Al-Hidāyah** (الهداية): It means divine guidance (al-tawfīq) and kindness (al-luṭf). It is said: "He guided us to faith (hadānā lil-īmān)," "He guided us in faith (hadānā al-īmān)," and "He guided us towards faith (hadānā ilā al-īmān)."

**Sāʾir** (سائر): It has the meaning of "the rest" or "the remaining."

**Our Prophet Muḥammad** (صلى الله عليه وسلم): He was named Muḥammad due to the abundance of his praiseworthy traits (khisāl ḥamīdah). This was stated by Ibn Fāris and others, meaning that God, may He be exalted, inspired his family with this name because of His knowledge of his beautiful attributes and the nobility of his character. May God increase him in honor and generosity.

**Taḥaddā** (تحدى): The people of language say: "So-and-so taḥaddā so-and-so" (يقال فلان يتحدى فلانا) when he vies with him and contends with him for victory.

**His saying "bi-ajmaʿihim"** (بأجمعهم): It is pronounced with a ḍammah on the mīm (بأجمعهم) and with a fatḥah (بأجمعهم); these are two well-known dialects, meaning "all of them."

**Afḥama** (أفحم): It means he silenced and overcame.

**Lā yakhluq** (لا يخلق): The lām is pronounced with a ḍammah (لا يخلق), and it is permissible to pronounce it with a fatḥah (لا يخلق). The yāʾ in both cases is pronounced with a fatḥah, and it is permissible to pronounce it with a ḍammah while the lām is pronounced with a kasrah. It is said: "khalaqa al-shayʾ" and "akhlaqa" (خلق الشيء وأخلق) when it becomes worn out. The intended meaning here is that its majesty and sweetness do not diminish.

**Istaẓharahu** (استظهره): He memorized it by heart (ḥafiẓahu ẓāhirā).

**Al-Wildān** (الولدان): The young boys (al-ṣibyān).

**Al-Ḥadathān** (الحدثان): With a fatḥah on the ḥāʾ and the dāl. It, along with al-ḥadath (الحدث), al-ḥādithah (الحادثة), and al-ḥudthā (الحدثى), all have the same meaning, which is the occurrence of something that was not.

**Al-Malawān** (الملوان): The night and the day.

**Al-Riḍwān** (الرضوان): With a kasrah on the rāʾ (الرضوان) and a ḍammah on it (الرضوان).

**Al-Anām** (الأنام): The creation (al-khalq), according to the chosen opinion. It is also said: "al-anīm" (الأنيم).

**Al-Dāmaghāt** (الدامغات): The breakers, the subjugators (al-qāhirāt).

**Al-Ṭaghām** (الطغام): With a fatḥah on the ṭāʾ and the ghayn, they are the rabble and the lowliest of people.

**Al-Amāthil** (الأماثل): The best and choicest; their singular is "amthal" (أمثل). It is said: "muthula al-rajul" (مثل الرجل), with a ḍammah on the thāʾ, meaning he became virtuous and choice.

**Al-Aʿlām** (الأعلام): The plural of "ʿalam" (علم), which is a mountain or other landmark by which one is guided on the road. The distinguished scholar is called by this name because he is one who is guided by him.

**Al-Nuhā** (النهى): The intellects (al-ʿuqūl); its singular is "nuhyah" (نهية), with a ḍammah on the nūn, because it forbids its possessor from indecencies. It is also said because its possessor arrives at (yantahī) his intellect and opinion. Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī said: It is permissible for "al-nuhā" to be a verbal noun (maṣdar) and to be a plural, like "al-ghuraf" (الغرف).

**Dimashq** (دمشق): With a kasrah on the dāl and a fatḥah on the mīm, according to the well-known pronunciation. The author of Maṭāliʿ al-Anwār related a kasrah on the mīm as well.

**Al-Mukhtaṣar** (المختصر): That which is brief in wording but abundant in meanings.

**Al-ʿAtīdah** (العتيدة): The present, the prepared (al-ḥāḍirah al-muʿaddah).

**Abtahel** (أبتهل): I supplicate with earnestness (ataḍarraʿ).

**Al-Tawfīq** (التوفيق): The creation of the ability for obedience.

**Ḥasbunā Allāh** (حسبنا الله): Meaning "God is sufficient for us" (kāfinā).

**Al-Wakīl** (الوكيل): The one entrusted with the affairs (al-muwakkal ilayhi). It is also said: the one entrusted with the management of His creation. It is also said: the one who undertakes the welfare of His creation. And it is said: the Protector (al-ḥāfiẓ).

**Ānāʾ al-Layl** (آناء الليل): Its hours. Its singular has four dialects: "anā" (أنى), "inā" (إنى) with a kasrah on the hamzah and a fatḥah on it, and "inī" (إني) and "inw" (إنو) with a yāʾ and a wāw, the hamzah being pronounced with a kasrah in both.

**Al-Ālāʾ** (الآلاء): The favors (al-niʿam). Its singular has the four dialects: "alā" (ألى), "ilā" (إلى), "alā" (ألا), and "alw" (ألو). Al-Wāḥidī related all of this.

**Al-Infāq** (الإنفاق) that is praised in the Sacred Law: The expenditure of wealth in obedience to God, may He be exalted.

**Tijāratan lan tabūr** (تجارة لن تبور): Meaning it will not perish or become corrupt.

**Al-Safarah** (السفرة): The angels, the scribes. **Al-Bararah** (البررة): The plural of "bārr" (بار), which is the obedient one.

**Yataʿtaʿu** (يتتعتع): Meaning he struggles and stumbles in his speech.

**Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī** (أبو موسى الأشعري): His name is ʿAbdullāh ibn Qays, attributed to al-Ashʿar, the ancestor of the tribe.

**Al-Utrunjah** (الأترجة): With a ḍammah on the hamzah and the rāʾ, it is well-known. Al-Jawharī said: Abū Zayd said: "turunjah" (ترنجة) is also said. In Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, in the Book of Foods, in this ḥadīth, it is mentioned as "al-utrunjah" (الأترنجة).

**Abū Umāmah al-Bāhilī** (أبو أمامة الباهلي): His name is Ṣudayy ibn ʿAjlān, attributed to Bāhilah, a well-known tribe.

**Al-Ḥasad** (الحسد): The desire for the removal of a blessing from another person. **Al-Ghibṭah** (الغبطة): It is similar to it, but without the removal of the blessing. Al-Ḥasad is forbidden, while al-ghibṭah in matters of good is praiseworthy and beloved. The meaning of his saying, peace and blessings be upon him, "There is no ḥasad except in two" is: there is no praiseworthy ghibṭah whose pursuit is emphasized except in two cases.

**Al-Tirmidhī** (الترمذي): Attributed to Tirmidh. Abū Saʿd al-Samʿānī said: It is an ancient town on the edge of Balkh, which is called Jayḥūn. The relative adjective is pronounced "Tirmidhī" (ترمذي) with a kasrah on the tāʾ and the mīm, and with a ḍammah on both, and with a fatḥah on the tāʾ with a kasrah on the mīm — three dialects related by al-Samʿānī.

**Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī** (أبو سعيد الخدري): His name is Saʿd ibn Mālik, attributed to the Banū Khudrah.

**Abū Dāwūd al-Sijistānī** (أبو داود السجستاني): His name is Sulaymān ibn al-Ashʿath.

**Al-Nasāʾī** (النسائي): He is Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān Aḥmad ibn Shuʿayb.

**Abū Masʿūd al-Badrī** (أبو مسعود البدري): His name is ʿUqbah ibn ʿAmr. The majority of scholars said he resided in Badr but did not witness the battle. Al-Zuhrī, al-Bukhārī, and others said he witnessed it with the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him.

**Al-Dārimī** (الدارمي): He is Abū Muḥammad ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, attributed to Dārim, the ancestor of a tribe.

**Shaʿāʾir Allāh** (شعائر الله): The rites and symbols of His religion; its singular is "shaʿīrah" (شعيرة). Al-Jawharī said: "shaʿārah" (شعارة) is also said for the singular.

**Al-Bazzār** (البزار): The author of the Musnad, with a rāʾ at the end.

**Laḥd al-Qabr** (لحد القبر): With a fatḥah on the lām and a ḍammah on it — two well-known dialects, the fatḥah being the more eloquent. It is the niche dug in the side of the grave facing the qiblah into which the deceased is placed. It is said: "laḥadta al-mayyit" (لحدت الميت) and "alḥadtuhu" (ألحدته).

**Abū Hurayrah** (أبو هريرة): His name is ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ṣakhr, according to the most correct of nearly thirty opinions. He was nicknamed with the kunyah of Abū Hurayrah because of a kitten (hurayrah) he had in his childhood, and he was the first to be called by this kunyah.

**Ādhananī bil-ḥarb** (آذنني بالحرب): He informed me (aʿlamanī), and its meaning is: He has shown that He will fight against me.

**Abū Ḥanīfah** (أبو حنيفة): He is al-Nuʿmān ibn Thābit ibn Zūṭā.

**Al-Imām al-Shāfiʿī** (الإمام الشافعي): He is Abū ʿAbdullāh Muḥammad ibn Idrīs ibn al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿUthmān ibn Shāfiʿ ibn al-Sāʾib ibn ʿUbayd ibn ʿAbd Yazīd ibn Hāshim ibn al-Muṭṭalib ibn ʿAbd Manāf ibn Quṣayy.

**Al-Thalb** (الثلب): With a fatḥah on the thāʾ and a sukūn on the lām, it means fault-finding and defamation (al-ʿayb).

**Ḥunafāʾ** (حنفاء): The plural of "ḥanīf" (حنيف), which is the one who is upright and inclined towards the truth, turning away from falsehood.

**Al-Marʿashī** (المرعشي): With a fatḥah on the mīm, a sukūn on the rāʾ, and a fatḥah on the ʿayn.

**Al-Tustarī** (التستري): With a ḍammah on the first tāʾ, a fatḥah on the second, and a sukūn on the sīn, attributed to Tustar, the well-known city.

**Al-Imām al-Muḥāsibī** (الإمام المحاسبي): With a ḍammah on the mīm. Al-Samʿānī said: He was called this because he used to take himself to account (yuḥāsib nafsahu). He was one who combined the knowledge of the outward and the inward.

**ʿArf al-Jannah** (عرف الجنة): With a fatḥah on the ʿayn, a sukūn on the rāʾ, and a fāʾ, meaning its fragrance.

**Falyatabawwaʾ maqʿadahu min al-nār** (فليتبوأ مقعده من النار): Meaning let him take up his seat in the Fire. It is also said: let him make it his abode. It is also said it is a supplication, and it is said it is an informative statement.

**Al-Dilālah** (الدلالة): With a fatḥah on the dāl and a kasrah on it. It is also said "dalwalah" (دلولة) with a ḍammah on the dāl and the lām.

**Al-Ṭawiyyah** (الطوية): With a fatḥah on the ṭāʾ and a kasrah on the wāw. The people of language say it is the conscience or inner thought (al-ḍamīr).

**Al-Tarāqī** (التراقي): The plural of "tarquwah" (ترقوة), which is the bone between the hollow of the collarbone and the shoulder.

**Yajlisūna ḥilaqan** (يجلسون حلقا): It is said with a fatḥah on the ḥāʾ and a kasrah on it — two dialects.

**Ibn Mājah** (ابن ماجه): He is Abū ʿAbdullāh Muḥammad ibn Yazīd.

**Abū al-Dardāʾ** (أبو الدرداء): His name is ʿUwaymir, and it is said ʿĀmir.

**Yaḥnū ʿalā al-ṭālib** (يحنو على الطالب): Meaning he is compassionate and kind towards him.

**Ayyūb al-Sakhtiyānī** (أيوب السختياني): With a fatḥah on the sīn and a kasrah on the tāʾ. Abū ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-Barr said: Ayyūb used to sell leather in Basra, and for this reason he was called al-Sakhtiyānī.

**Al-Barāʿah** (البراعة): A verbal noun from "baraʿa al-rajul" (برع الرجل) and "bariʿa" (برع), with a fatḥah on the rāʾ and a ḍammah on it, when he excels his companions.

**Ḥalqat al-ʿilm** (حلقة العلم): With a sukūn on the lām — this is the eloquent and well-known dialect. It is also said with a fatḥah on it, in a rare dialect related by Thaʿlab, al-Jawharī, and others.

**Al-Rifʿah** (الرفعة): With a ḍammah on the rāʾ and a kasrah on it — two dialects.

**Qiʿdat al-mutaʿallimīn** (قعدة المتعلمين): With a kasrah on the qāf.

**Al-Maʿshar** (المعشر): The group of people whose affair is one.

**His saying "wa yatafaqqadūnahā bil-nahār"** (ويتفقدونها بالنهار): Meaning they act upon what is in it.

**Abū Sulaymān al-Khaṭṭābī** (أبو سليمان الخطابي): Attributed to one of his ancestors named al-Khaṭṭāb. His name is Abū Sulaymān Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, and it is said his name was Aḥmad.

**Al-Zuhrī** (الزهري): He is Abū Bakr Muḥammad ibn Muslim ibn ʿUbaydillāh ibn ʿAbdillāh ibn Shihāb ibn ʿAbdillāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Zuhrah ibn Kilāb ibn Murrah ibn Kaʿb.

**Al-Baṣrī** (البصري): With a fatḥah on the bāʾ and a kasrah on it.

**Al-Shaʿbī** (الشعبي): With a fatḥah on the shīn. His name is ʿĀmir ibn Sharāḥīl, with a fatḥah on the shīn.

**Tamīm al-Dārī** (تميم الداري): Attributed to Dārīn, a place on the coast. It is also said "al-Dayrī" (الديري), attributed to a monastery (dayr) in which he used to worship. And it is said something else. I have clarified the difference of opinion regarding this at the beginning of my commentary on Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim.

**Sulaym ibn ʿItrah** (سليم بن عترة): With a kasrah on the ʿayn and a sukūn on the tāʾ.

**Al-Dūraqī** (الدورقي): With an important dāl, fatḥah, then a sukūn on the wāw, then a fatḥah on the rāʾ, then a qāf, then the yāʾ of attribution. It is said the attribution is to the tall caps called "al-dūra qiyyah" (الدورقية). It is also said his father was a devotee (nāsik), and in that time devotees were called "Dūraqī." And it is said it is an attribution to Dūraq, a town in Persia, or elsewhere.

**Manṣūr ibn Zādān** (منصور بن زاذان): With a zāy and a dhāl.

**His saying "yaḥtabī"** (يحتبي): Meaning he erects his shins and wraps his arms or a garment around the meeting point of his shins and thighs. "Al-ḥibwah" (الحبوة), with a ḍammah on the ḥāʾ and a kasrah on it — two dialects — is that action.

**Al-Hadharamah** (الهذرمة): With a dhāl, it is the rapidity of speech that is not distinct.

**Al-Ghazālī** (الغزالي): He is Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad. It is pronounced with a tashdīd on the zāy. It is related that he denied this and said: "I am only al-Ghazālī with a takhfīf on the zāy, attributed to a village in the districts of Ṭūs called Ghazālah."

**Ṭalḥah ibn Muṣarrif** (طلحة بن مصرف): With a ḍammah on the mīm, a fatḥah on the ṣād, and a kasrah on the rāʾ. It is said a fatḥah on the rāʾ is permissible, but this is nothing.

**Abū al-Aḥwaṣ** (أبو الأحوص): With an important ḥāʾ and ṣād. His name is ʿAwf ibn Mālik al-Jushamī, with a ḍammah on the jīm and a fatḥah on the shīn, attributed to Jusham, the ancestor of the tribe.

**Al-Fusṭāṭ** (الفسطاط): It has six dialects: "fusṭāṭ" (فسطاط) with a tāʾ instead of the ṭāʾ, and "fusāṭ" (فساط) with a tashdīd on the sīn. The fāʾ in all of them is pronounced with a ḍammah and a kasrah. The intended meaning is the tent and the dwelling.

**Al-Dawī** (الدوي): With a fatḥah on the dāl, a kasrah on the wāw, and a tashdīd on the yāʾ, it is an incomprehensible sound.

**Al-Nakhaʿī** (النخعي): With a fatḥah on the nūn and the khāʾ, attributed to Nakhaʿ, the ancestor of a tribe.

**Ḥalab shātin** (حلب شاة): With a fatḥah on the lām, and it is permissible to give it a sukūn in a rare dialect.

**Al-Raqāshī** (الرقاشي): With a fatḥah on the rāʾ and a takhfīf on the qāf.

**Al-Qadhāh** (القذاة): Like a small stick or a piece of cloth, and similar things that are swept out of the mosque.

**Sulaymān ibn Yasār** (سليمان بن يسار): With a mathannāh (tāʾ marbūṭah) then an important sīn.

**Abū Usayd** (أبو أسيد): With a ḍammah on the hamzah and a fatḥah on the sīn. His name is Mālik ibn Rabīʿah, and he witnessed Badr.

**Tanṭaḥunī** (تنطحني): With a kasrah on the ṭāʾ and a fatḥah on it.

**Muntashir jiddan** (منتشر جدا): With a kasrah on the jīm, and it is a verbal noun.

**Al-Ushnān** (الأشنان): With a ḍammah on the hamzah and a kasrah on it — two dialects mentioned by Abū ʿUbaydah. The hamzah of "ushnān" is original. Ibn al-Jawāliqī said it is a Persian word that has been Arabized, and in pure Arabic it is "ḥaraḍ" (حرض).

**Karāsī aḍrāsihi** (كراسي أضراسه): It is permissible to pronounce it with a tashdīd and a takhfīf.

**Al-Rūyānī** (الروياني): With a ḍammah on the rāʾ and a sukūn on the wāw, attributed to Rūyān.

**His saying "ʿalā ḥasbi ḥālihi"** (على حسب حاله): It is with a fatḥah on the sīn, meaning according to his capacity.

**Al-Ḥammām** (الحمام): It is well-known, and it is masculine according to the people of language.

**Al-Ḥushūsh** (الحشوش): The places prepared for excrement and urine; its singular is "ḥashsh" (حش), with a fatḥah on the ḥāʾ and a ḍammah on it — two dialects.

**Ḥijr al-insān** (حجر الانسان): With a fatḥah on the ḥāʾ and a kasrah on it.

**Al-Janāzah** (الجنازة): With a kasrah on the jīm and a fatḥah on it, from "janaza" (جنز), meaning to cover.

**Bahz ibn Ḥakīm** (بهز بن حكيم): With a fatḥah on the bāʾ, a sukūn on the hāʾ, and a zāy.

**Zurārah** (زرارة): With a ḍammah on the zāy.

**Aḥmad ibn Abī al-Ḥawārī** (أحمد بن أبي الحواري): With a fatḥah on the ḥāʾ and a kasrah on the rāʾ. Some pronounce the rāʾ with a fatḥah. Our teacher Abū al-Baqāʾ Khālid al-Nābulusī, may God have mercy on him, used to relate this and sometimes preferred it. He was the foremost scholar of his time in this art, with complete mastery of it. The name of Abū al-Ḥawārī is ʿAbdullāh ibn Maymūn ibn ʿAbbās ibn al-Ḥārith.

**Al-Jurʿī** (الجرعي): With a ḍammah on the jīm and the rāʾ.

**Abū al-Jawzāʾ** (أبو الجوزاء): With a fatḥah on the jīm and a zāy. His name is Aws ibn ʿAbdillāh, and it is said Aws ibn Khālid.

**Ḥabtar** (حبتر): With an important ḥāʾ, fatḥah, then a bāʾ, sukūn, then a tāʾ, fatḥah, then a rāʾ. It means the righteous man who upholds the rights of God and the rights of His servants. This is what al-Zajjāj, the author of al-Maṭāliʿ, and others said.

**Abū Dharr** (أبو ذر): His name is Jundub, and it is said Burayr, with a ḍammah on the bāʾ and a tashdīd on the rāʾ.

**Ijtaraḥū al-sayyiʾāt** (اجترحوا السيئات): They earned and acquired them.

**Al-ʿār** (العار): With a kasrah on the ʿayn, it is the mark or sign.

**Al-Shirāk** (الشراك): With a kasrah on the shīn, it is the thin strap that is on the top of the foot in the sandal.

**Umm Salamah** (أم سلمة): Her name is Hind, and it is said Ramlah, but this is nothing.

**ʿAbdullāh ibn Mughaffal** (عبد الله بن مغفل): With a ḍammah on the mīm, a fatḥah on the ghayn, and a fāʾ.

**Al-Laghṭ** (اللغط): With a fatḥah on the ghayn and a sukūn on it — two dialects. It is the confusion of voices.

**Al-Muʿawwidhatān** (المعوذتان): With a kasrah on the wāw.

**Al-Awzāʿī** (الأوزاعي): His name is ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAmr, the Imām of Syria in his time, attributed to a place at the Bāb al-Farādīs in Damascus called al-Awzāʿ. It is also said to an attribution to a tribe, and it is said something else.

**ʿUrazib** (عرزب): With an important ʿayn, fatḥah, then a rāʾ, sukūn, then a zāy, fatḥah, then a bāʾ.

**Buraydah ibn al-Ḥuṣayb** (بريدة بن الحصيب): With a ḍammah on the ḥāʾ and a fatḥah on the ṣād.

**Fuḍālah** (فضالة): With a fatḥah on the fāʾ.

**Lillāhi ashaddu adhanan** (لله أشد أذنا): With a fatḥah on the hamzah and the dhāl, meaning "more attentive listening."

**Al-Qaynah** (القينة): With a fatḥah on the qāf, the singing girl.

**Ṭūbā** (طوبى): Meaning goodness for them. This is what the people of language said.

**Al-Aʿmash** (الأعمش): He is Sulaymān ibn Mihrān.

**Abū al-ʿĀliyah** (أبو العالية): With an important ʿayn. His name is Rufayʿ, with a ḍammah on the rāʾ.

**Abū Lubābah al-Ṣaḥābī** (أبو لبابة الصحابي): With a ḍammah on the lām. His name is Bashīr, and it is said Rifāʿah ibn ʿAbd al-Mundhir.

**Al-Ghashmah** (الغشمة): The oppressors and tyrants.

**His saying "ʿaynāhu tadharfān"** (عيناه تذرفان): Meaning his tears flow. It is with a fatḥah on the tāʾ and a kasrah on the rāʾ.

**Fa-mā khaṭbukum** (فما خطبكم): Meaning what is your matter or affair.

**Al-Ayyām al-Maʿdūdāt** (الأيام المعدودات): The three days of Tashrīq, which follow the Day of Sacrifice.

**Tashmīt al-ʿāṭis** (تشميت العاطس): It is with a shīn and with a sīn. **Al-Qaffāl** mentioned here is al-Marwazī, ʿAbdullāh ibn Aḥmad. **Yuqran** (يقرن) is with a ḍammah on the rāʾ, according to the eloquent dialect, and in another dialect with a kasrah on it.

**Al-Baghawī** (البغوي): Attributed to Bagh, a city between Herāt and Marw, also called Baghshūr. His name is al-Ḥusayn ibn Masʿūd.

**Al-Āṣāl** (الآصال): The plural of "aṣīl" (أصيل), which is the end of the day. It is also said: what is between the ʿAṣr prayer and sunset.

**Zubayd ibn al-Ḥārith** (زبيد بن الحرث): With a ḍammah on the zāy, followed by a fatḥah on the bāʾ.

**Subbūḥ Quddūs** (سبوح قدوس): With a ḍammah on the first letter of each, and with a fatḥah — two well-known dialects.

**Abū Qilābah** (أبو قلابة): With a kasrah on the qāf, a fatḥah on the lām, and a takhfīf on it, and a bāʾ. His name is ʿAbdullāh ibn Zayd.

**Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb** (يحيى بن وثاب): With a thāʾ, tashdīd.

**Muʿādh ibn Rifāʿah** (معاذ بن رفاعة): With a ḍammah on the mīm and the ʿayn, and its end is a nūn.

**Al-Shakhīr** (الشخير): With a kasrah on the shīn and a tashdīd on the khāʾ.

**Al-Ḥakam ibn ʿUtaybah** (الحكم بن عتيبة): With a tāʾ, then a yāʾ, then a bāʾ.

**Al-Muḥyā wal-Mamāt** (المحيى والممات): Life and death.

**Awziʿhum** (أوزعهم): Meaning inspire them (alhimhum).

**Ḥamdan yuwāfī niʿamahu** (حمدا يوافي نعمة): Meaning it reaches His favors and attains them.

**Wa yukāfiʾ mazīdahu** (ويكافئ مزيده): It is with a hamzah at the end, "yukāfiʾ" (يكافئ), and its meaning is: he undertakes to give thanks for the favors He has increased upon us.

**Mujālid** (مجالد), the narrator from al-Shaʿbī: With a jīm and a kasrah on the lām.

**Al-Ṣaymarī** (الصيمري): With a fatḥah on the ṣād and the mīm. It is said with a ḍammah on the mīm, but this is strange.

I have elaborated on its explanation in Tahdhīb al-Asmāʾ wal-Lughāt. These are brief points on the correction of the problematic words that occur in

chapters.title_en: Section 3 — On the Veneration of the Qur'an and Its People, and the Etiquette of the Teacher and Learner
chapters.arabic_text:
الله تعالى (ذلك ومن يعظم حرمات الله فهو خير له عند ربه وقال تعالى (واخفض

جناحك لمن اتبعك من المؤمنين وقال تعالى (والذين يؤذون المؤمنين والمؤمنا ت

بغير ما اكتسبوا فقد احتملوا بهتانا وإثما مبينا
# 
# وفي الباب حديث أبي مسعود الأنصاري وحديث ابن عباس المتقدمان في الباب

الثاني وعن أبي موسى الأشعري رضي الله عنه قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه

وسلم: إن من إجلال الله تعالى إكرام ذي الشيبة المسلم وحامل القرآن غير

الغالي فيه والجافي عنه وإكرام ذي السلطان المقسط رواه أبو داود وهو حديث

حسن وعن عائشة رضي الله عنها قالت
# 
# [ ... ]
# 
# أمرنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: أن ننزل الناس منازلهم رواه أبو

داود في سننه والبزار في مسنده قال الحاكم أبو عبد الله
# في علوم الحديث هو حديث صحيح وعن جابر بن عبد الله رضي الله عنه أن النبي

ص: كان يجمع بين الرجلين من قتلى أحد ثم يقول أيهما أكثر أخذا للقرآن فإن

أشير إلى أحدهما قدمه في اللحد رواه البخاري وعن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن

النبي ص: إن الله عز وجل قال من آذى لي وليا فقد آذنته بالحرب رواه البخاري

وثبت في الصحيحين عنه صلى الله عليه وسلم: أنه قال من صلى الصبح فهو في ذمة

الله تعالى فلا يطلبنكم الله بشئ من ذمته وعن الإمامين الجليلين أبي حنيفة

والشافعي رضي الله عنهما قالا إن لم يكن العلماء أولياء الله فليس لله ولي

قال الإمام الحافظ أبو القاسم بن عساكر رحمه الله  اعلم يا أخي وفقنا الله

وإياك لمرضاته وجعلنا ممن يغشاه ويتقيه حق تقاته أن لحوم العلماء مسمومة

وعادة الله في هتك أستار
# 
# منتقصيهم معلومة وأن من أطلق لسانه في العلماء بالثلب ابتلاه الله تعالى

قبل موته بموت القلب فليحذر الذين يخالفون عن أمره أن تصيبهم فتنة أو

يصيبهم عذاب أليم
#

| الباب الرابع في آداب معلم القرآن ومتعلمه
# قال هذا الباب مع البابين بعده مقصود الكتاب وهو طويل منتشر جدا فإني

أشير إلى مقاصده مختصرة في فصول ليسهل حفظه وضبطه إن شاء الله تعالى [فضل]

أول ما ينبغي للمقرئ والقارئ أن يقصدا بذلك رضا الله تعالى قال الله تعالى

وما أمروا إلا ليعبدوا الله مخلصين له الدين حنفاء ويقيموا الصلاة ويؤتوا

الزكاة وذلك دين القيمة أي الملة المستقيمة وفي الصحيحين عن رسول الله صلى

الله عليه وسلم: إنما الأعمال بالنيات وإنما لكل امرئ ما نوى وهذا الحديث

من أصول الإسلام
# 
# وروينا عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال إنما يعطى الرجل على قدر نيته وعن

غيره إنما يعطى الناس على قدر نياتهم وروينا عن الأستاذ أبي القاسم القشيري

رحمه الله تعالى قال الإخلاص إفراد الحق في الطاعة بالقصد وهو أن يريد

بطاعته التقرب الى الله تعالى دون شئ آخر من تصنع لمخلوق أو اكتساب محمدة

عند الناس أو محبة أو مدح من الخلق أو معنى من المعاني سوى التقرب إلى الله

تعالى قال ويصح أن يقال
# الإخلاص تصفية الفعل عن ملاحظة المخلوقين وعن حذيفة المرعشي رحمه الله

تعالى الإخلاص استواء أفعال العبد في الظاهر والباطن وعن ذي النون رحمه

الله تعالى قال ثلاث من علامات الإخلاص 1 - استواء المدح والذم من العامة 2

- ونسيان رؤية العمل في الأعمال 3 - واقتضاء ثواب الأعمال في الآخرة وعن

الفضيل بن عياض رضي الله عنه قال ترك العمل لأجل الناس رياء والعمل لأجل

الناس شرك والإخلاص أن يعافيك الله منهما وعن سهل التستري رحمه الله تعالى

قال نظر الأكياس في تفسير الإخلاص فلم يجدوا غير  هذا أن تكون
# 
# حركته وسكونه في سره وعلانيته لله تعالى وحده لا يمازجه شئ لا نفس ولا

هوى ولا دنيا وعن السري رضي الله عنه قال لا تعمل للناس شيئا ولا تترك لهم

شيئا ولا تغط لهم شيئا ولا تكشف لهم شيئا وعن القشيري قال أفضل الصدق

استواء الصدق والعلانية وعن الحارث المحاسبي رحمه الله تعالى قال الصادق هو

الذي لا يبالي ولو خرج عن كل قدر له في قلوب
# الخلائق من أجل صلاح قلبه ولا يحب اطلاع الناس على مثاقيل الذر من حسن

عمله ولا يكره إطلاع الناس على السئ من عمله فإن كراهته لذلك دليل على أنه

يحب الزيادة عندهم وليس هذا من أخلاق الصديقين وعن غيره إذا طلبت الله

تعالى بالصدق أعطاك الله مرآة تبصر فيها كل شئ من عجائب الدنيا والآخرة

وأقاويل السلف في هذا كثيرة أشرنا إلى هذه الأحرف منها تنبيها على المطلوب

وقد ذكرت جملا من عن ذلك مع شرحها في أول شرح المهذب
# 
# وضممت إليها من آداب العالم والمتعلم والفقيه والمتفقه ما لا يستغني عنه

طالب العلم والله أعلم

| [فصل] وينبغي أن لا يقصد به توصلا إلى غرض من أغراض الدنيا
# من مال أو رياسة أو وجاهة أو ارتفاع على أقرانه أو ثناء عند الناس أو صرف

وجوه الناس إليه أو نحو ذلك * ولا يشوب المقرئ إقراءه بطمع في رفق يحصل له

من بعض من يقرأ عليه سواء كان الرفق مالا أو خدمة وإن قل ولو كان على صورة

الهدية التي لولا قراءته عليه لما أهداها إليه قال تعالى (من كان يريد حرث

الآخرة نزد له في حرثه ومن كان يريد حرث الدنيا نؤته منها وما له في الآخرة

من نصيب) وقال تعالى (من كان يريد العاجلة عجلنا له فيها ما نشاء لمن نريد)

الآية وعن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

من تعلم علما يبتغي به وجه الله تعالى لا يتعلمه إلا ليصيب به غرضا  من

الدنيا لم يجد عرف الجنة يوم القيامة رواه أبو داود بإسناد صحيح ومثله

أحاديث كثيرة وعن أنس وحذيفة وكعب بن مالك رضي الله عنهم أن رسول الله صلى

الله عليه وسلم: قال
# 
# من طلب العلم ليماري به السفهاء أو يكاثر به العلماء أو يصرف به وجوه
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ح ر م (ḥ-r-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of sacred inviolability; that which is protected and sanctified, entailing both prohibition and honor.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Theological nuance of *ḥurumāt* (sing. *ḥurma*) as the sanctities ordained by Allah, whose veneration is a mark of taqwā and whose violation incurs divine wrath.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense of physical sanctity (e.g., the Ka'bah); metaphorical extension to the honor due to believers, scholars, and bearers of the Qur'an.
- Sībawayh Rule: *ʿAṭf al-Bayān* (Appositional explicative) — The phrase "وذلك دين القيمة" employs an explicative apposition where "القيمة" (the straight) clarifies "الدين" (the religion), requiring precise nominal agreement.
chapters.translation:
Allah the Exalted said: {«ذلك ومن يعظم حرمات الله فهو خير له عند ربه»} ("That [is so]; and whoever venerates the sacred ordinances of Allah, it is better for him with his Lord"). And He said: {«واخفض جناحك لمن اتبعك من المؤمنين»} ("And lower your wing to the believers who follow you"). And He said: {«والذين يؤذون المؤمنين والمؤمنات بغير ما اكتسبوا فقد احتملوا بهتانا وإثما مبينا»} ("And those who harm believing men and believing women for something they have not committed — they have borne a slander and a manifest sin").

In this chapter [are cited] the hadith of Abū Masʿūd al-Anṣārī and the hadith of Ibn ʿAbbās already mentioned in the second chapter. And from Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Verily, from the veneration of Allah the Exalted is honoring the Muslim elder of advanced age, and the bearer of the Qur'an who is neither excessive in it nor neglectful of it, and honoring the just ruler." Narrated by Abū Dāwūd, and it is a ḥasan (good) hadith. And from ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: [The Prophet] commanded us to place people in their proper stations. Narrated by Abū Dāwūd in his *Sunan* and al-Bazzār in his *Musnad*; al-Ḥākim Abū ʿAbd Allāh said in *ʿUlūm al-Ḥadīth* that it is a ṣaḥīḥ (authentic) hadith. And from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet, peace be upon him, would pair two men among the martyrs of Uḥud [in one grave], then ask: "Which of the two had memorized more of the Qur'an?" If one of them was indicated, he would place him first in the niche (al-laḥd). Narrated by al-Bukhārī. And from Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet, peace be upon him: "Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: 'Whoever harms a friend (walī) of Mine, I have declared war upon him.'" Narrated by al-Bukhārī. And it is established in the Two Ṣaḥīḥs from him, peace be upon him, that he said: "Whoever prays the dawn prayer is under the protection (dhimmah) of Allah the Exalted; so let not Allah call you to account for any breach of His protection." And from the two venerable Imāms, Abū Ḥanīfah and al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah be pleased with them both, they said: "If the scholars are not the friends (awliyāʾ) of Allah, then Allah has no friend."

The Imām, the ḥāfiẓ, Abū al-Qāsim ibn ʿAsākir, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "Know, O my brother — may Allah grant us and you success in what pleases Him, and make us among those who frequent Him and fear Him with true piety — that the flesh of scholars is poisoned, and Allah's custom in exposing the veils of those who disparage them is well-known. And whoever unleashes his tongue against scholars with defamation, Allah the Exalted will afflict him before his death with the death of the heart. So let those who oppose his command beware, lest a trial befall them or a painful punishment strike them."

---

**Chapter Four: On the Etiquette of the Teacher of the Qur'an and Its Learner**

The author (Imam al-Nawawi) said: This chapter, along with the two chapters following it, is the very purpose of this book. It is lengthy and widely dispersed, so I shall point to its objectives in concise sections (fuṣūl) to facilitate its memorization and mastery, Allah willing.

**[Section on Sincerity (Ikhlāṣ)]**

The first thing incumbent upon the teacher (al-muqriʾ) and the learner (al-qāriʾ) is that they intend thereby the pleasure of Allah the Exalted. Allah the Exalted said: {«وما أمروا إلا ليعبدوا الله مخلصين له الدين حنفاء ويقيموا الصلاة ويؤتوا الزكاة وذلك دين القيمة»} ("And they were not commanded except to worship Allah, devoting religion sincerely to Him, as upright people, and to establish prayer and give zakāh — and that is the straight religion"). That is, the upright creed. And in the Two Ṣaḥīḥs, from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him: "Verily, deeds are but by intentions, and verily, every person shall have only what he intended." This hadith is among the foundational principles of Islam.

We have narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he said: "A man is given only according to his intention." And from another: "People are given only according to their intentions." And we have narrated from the master Abū al-Qāsim al-Qushayrī, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him, who said: "Sincerity (al-ikhlāṣ) is singling out the Truth (al-Ḥaqq) in obedience by one's intent — that one intends by his obedience to draw near to Allah the Exalted, and nothing else: neither showing off to a creature, nor seeking praise from people, nor love, nor commendation from creation, nor any other meaning besides drawing near to Allah the Exalted." He said: "And it may be said: sincerity is purifying the act from any regard for created beings."

And from Ḥudhayfah al-Marʿashī, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him: "Sincerity is the equality of the servant's acts in the outward and the inward." And from Dhū al-Nūn, may Allah have mercy on him, who said: "Three are among the signs of sincerity: (1) the equality of praise and blame from the common people; (2) forgetting the observation of the deed within one's deeds; (3) seeking the reward of deeds only in the Hereafter." And from al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "Abandoning an act for the sake of people is ostentation (riyāʾ); performing an act for the sake of people is polytheism (shirk); and sincerity is that Allah protects you from both." And from Sahl al-Tustarī, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him, who said: "The clever ones looked into the interpretation of sincerity and found nothing other than this: that one's movement and stillness, in secret and in public, be for Allah the Exalted alone, unmixed with anything — neither self, nor desire, nor worldly gain." And from al-Sarī, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "Do not do anything for people, do not abandon anything for them, do not conceal anything from them, and do not reveal anything to them." And from al-Qushayrī, who said: "The best of truthfulness is the equality of one's secret and public [states]." And from al-Ḥārith al-Muḥāsibī, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him, who said: "The truthful one is he who does not care even if he loses all standing in the hearts of creatures for the sake of his heart's rectitude; he does not love that people see the weight of an atom of his good deeds, nor does he dislike people seeing the evil of his deeds — for his dislike of that is evidence that he loves increase in their estimation, and this is not among the traits of the ṣiddīqīn (the utterly truthful)." And from another: "If you seek Allah the Exalted with truthfulness, Allah will give you a mirror through which you see every wonder of this world and the Hereafter."

The sayings of the Salaf on this matter are numerous; I have pointed to these few of them as an indication of what is sought. I have mentioned a collection of this, with its commentary, at the beginning of my *Sharḥ al-Muhadhdhab*, and I have appended to it the etiquettes of the scholar and the learner, the jurist and the student of jurisprudence, in what no seeker of knowledge can do without. And Allah knows best.

**[Section: On Not Seeking Worldly Aims]**

It is incumbent upon him not to intend thereby (i.e., learning and teaching the Qur'an) as a means to any worldly aim — whether wealth, leadership, prestige, elevation over one's peers, praise among people, turning people's faces toward oneself, or the like. Nor should the teacher (al-muqriʾ) mix his teaching with covetousness for any benefit (rifq) that might come to him from some of those who read under him — whether that benefit be money or service, however small, even if it takes the form of a gift that, were it not for his reading under him, would not have been given to him. Allah the Exalted said: {«من كان يريد حرث الآخرة نزد له في حرثه ومن كان يريد حرث الدنيا نؤته منها وما له في الآخرة من نصيب»} ("Whoever desires the harvest of the Hereafter, We increase for him in his harvest; and whoever desires the harvest of this world, We give him some of it, and he has no share in the Hereafter"). And He said: {«من كان يريد العاجلة عجلنا له فيها ما نشاء لمن نريد»} ("Whoever desires the immediate [life], We hasten for him therein what We will, for whom We intend") — the rest of the verse. And from Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Whoever learns knowledge by which the Face of Allah the Exalted is sought, and does not learn it except to attain thereby a worldly aim, he will not find the fragrance of Paradise on the Day of Resurrection." Narrated by Abū Dāwūd with an authentic chain (isnād ṣaḥīḥ). And there are many similar hadiths. And from Anas, Ḥudhayfah, and Kaʿb ibn Mālik, may Allah be pleased with them all, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Whoever seeks knowledge to argue with fools thereby, or to vie with scholars, or to turn people's faces [toward himself]..."

chapters.title_en: Section 4 — On the Teacher's Sincerity, Noble Character, and Kindness to Students
chapters.arabic_text:
الناس إليه فليتبوأ مقعده من النار رواه الترمذي من رواية كعب بن مالك وقال

أدخله النار
# إخلاص المعلم له

| [فصل] وليحذر كل الحذر من قصده التكثر بكثرة المشتغلين عليه
# والمختلفين إليه وليحذر من كراهته قراءة أصحابه على غيره ممن ينتفع به

وهذه مصيبة يبتلى بها بعض المعلمين الجاهلين وهي دلالة بينة من صاحبها على

سوء نيته وفساد طويته بل هي حجة فاطعة على عدم إرادته بتعليمه وجه الله

تعالى الكريم فإنه لو أراد الله بتعليمه لما كره ذلك بل قال لنفسه أنا أردت

الطاعة بتعليمه وقد حصلت وقد قصد بقراءته على غيري زيادة علم فلا عتب عليه
# 
# وقد روينا في مسند الإمام المجمع على حفظه وإمامته أبي محمد
# الدارمي رحمة الله عليه عن علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه أنه قال يا حملة

القرآن أو قال يا حملة العلم اعملوا به فإنما العلم من عمل بما علم ووافق

علمه عمله وسيكون أقوام يحملون العلم لا يجاوز تراقيهم يخالف عملهم علمهم

وتخالف سريرتهم علانيتهم يجلسون حلقا يباهي بعضهم بعضا حتى أن الرجل ليغضب

على جليسه أن يجلس إلى غيره ويدعه أولئك لا تصعد أعمالهم في مجالسهم تلك

إلى الله تعالى وقد صح عن الإمام الشافعي رضي الله عنه أنه قال وددت أن

الخلق تعلموا هذا العلم يعني علمه وكتبه أن لا ينسب إلي حرف منه
# 
# مكارم الاخلاق

| [فصل] وينبغي للمعلم أن يتخلق بالمحاسن التي ورد الشرع بها
# والخصال الحميدة والشيم المرضية التي أرشده الله إليها من الزهادة في

الدنيا والتقلل منها وعدم المبالاة بها وبأهلها والسخاء والجود ومكارم

الأخلاق وطلاقة الوجه من غير خروج إلى حد الخلاعة والحلم والصبر والتنزه عن

دنئ المكاسب  وملازمة الورع والخشوع والسكينة والوقار والتواضع والخضوع

واجتناب الضحك والإكثار من المزاح وملازمة الوظائف الشرعية كالتنظيف وتقليم

بإزالة الأوساخ والشعور التي ورد الشرع بإزالتها كقص الشارب وتقليم الظفر

وتسريح اللحية وإزالة الروائح الكريهة والملابس المكروهة
# 
# وليحذر كل الحذر من الحسد والرياء والعجب واحتقار غيره وإن كان دونه

وينبغي أن يستعمل الأحاديث الواردة في التسبيح والتهليل ونحوهما من الأذكار

والدعوات وأن يراقب الله تعالى في سره وعلانيته ويحافظ على ذلك وأن يكون

تعويله في جميع أموره على الله تعالى
# الاحسان للمتعلم

| [فصل] وينبغي له أن يرفق بمن يقرأ عليه
# وأن يرحب به ويحسن إليه بحسب حاله فقد روينا عن أبي هرون العبدي قال كنا

نأتي أبا سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه فيقول: مرحبا بوصية رسول الله صلى الله

عليه وسلم: إن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: قال إن الناس لكم تبع وإن رجالا

يأتونكم من أقطار الأرض يتفقهون في الدين فإذا أتوكم فاستوصوا بهم خيرا

رواه الترمذي وابن ماجه وغيرهما وروينا نحوه في مسند الدارمي عن أبي

الدرداء رضي الله عنه
# 
# إخلاص النصيحة له

| [فصل] وينبغي أن يبذل لهم النصيحة
# فإن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: قال الدين النصيحة لله ولكتابه

ولرسوله ولأئمة المسلمين وعامتهم رواه مسلم ومن النصيحة لله تعالى ولكتابه

إكرام قارئه وطالبه وإرشاده إلى مصلحته والرفق به ومساعدته على طلبه بما

أمكن وتأليف قلب الطالب وأن يكون سمحا بتعليمه في رفق متلطفا به ومحرضا له

على التعلم * وينبغي أن يذكره فضيلة ذلك ليكون سببا في نشاطه وزيادة في

رغبته ويزهده في الدنيا ويصرفه عن الركون إليها والإغترار بها
# 
# ويذكره فضيلة الإشتغال بالقرآن وسائر العلوم الشرعية وهو طريق العارفين

وعباد الله الصالحين وأن ذلك رتبة الأنبياء عليهم الصلاة والسلام * وينبغي

أن يشفق على الطالب ويعتني بمصالحه كاعتنائه بمصالح ولده ومصالح نفسه ويجري

المتعلم مجرى ولده في الشفقة عليه والصبر على جفائه وسوء أدبه ويعذره في

قلة أدبه في بعض الأحيان فإن الإنسان معرض للنقائص لا سيما إن كان  صغير

السن * وينبغي أن يحب له ما يحب لنفسه من الخير وأن يكره له ما يكره لنفسه

من النقص مطلقا فقد ثبت في الصحيحين عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: أنه

قال لا يؤمن أحدكم حتى يحب لأخيه ما يحب لنفسه وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

قال أكرم الناس على جليسي الذي يتخطى الناس حتى يجلس إلي لو استطعت أن لا

يقع الذباب على وجهه لفعلت وفي رواية إن الذباب ليقع عليه فيؤذيني وينبغي

أن لا يتعاظم على المتعلمين بل يلين لهم ويتواضع معهم
# فقد جاء في التواضع لآحاد الناس أشياء كثيرة معروفة فكيف بهؤلاء الذين هم

بمنزلة أولاده مع ما هم عليه من الاشتغال بالقرآن مع ما لهم عليه من حق

الصحبة وترددهم إليه وقد جاء عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: أنه قال

لينوا لمن تعلمون ولمن تتعلمون منه وعن أبي أيوب السختياني رحمه الله قال

ينبغي للعالم أن يضع التراب على رأسه تواضعا لله عز وجل
# 
# تأليف المتعلم

| [فصل] وينبغي أن يؤدب المتعلم على التدريج بالآداب السنية
# والشيم المرضية ورياضة نفسه بالدقائق الخفية ويعوده الصيانة في جميع

أموره الباطنة والجلية ويحرضه بأقواله وأفعاله المتكررات على الإخلاص

والصدق وحسن النيات ومراقبة الله تعالى في جميع اللحظات ويعرفه أن لذلك

تتفتح عليه أنوار المعارف وينشرح صدره ويتفجر من قلبه ينابيع الحكم

واللطائف ويبارك له في علمه وحاله ويوفق في أفعاله وأقواله
# حكم التعليم

| [فصل] تعليم المتعلمين فرض كفاية
# فإن لم يكن من يصلح إلا
# 
# واحد تعين وإن كان هناك جماعة يحصل التعليم ببعضهم فإن امتنعوا كلهم

أثموا وإن قام به بعضهم سقط الحرج عن الباقين وإن طلب من أحدهم وامتنع
chapters.anchors:
- Root: خ-ل-ص (khalasa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Purity, clarity, freedom from admixture; sincerity as the unalloyed essence of an act
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ikhlaṣ — directing an act solely toward Allah, stripping it of all worldly motives
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal purity of substance; metaphorically, the heart's purification from ostentation (riyāʾ)
- Root: ن-ص-ح (naṣaḥa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To be sincerely devoted, to advise faithfully; originally, to sew or mend — implying restoration of what is broken
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Naṣīḥah as comprehensive well-wishing — the advisor's desire for the advised one's true welfare in religion and world
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal mending of garments; metaphorically, the mending of hearts and rectifying their corruption
- Root: ر-ف-ق (rafaqa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Gentleness, kindness, leniency; the opposite of harshness (ʿunf)
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Rifq as a praiseworthy trait of the prophets — gentleness in teaching and guiding
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal smoothness of path; metaphorically, the gentle approach in dealing with people
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause with Implied Protasis (al-Sharṭ al-Muqaddar) — In "فإن لم يكن من يصلح إلا واحد تعين" the conditional structure implies a legal obligation contingent upon the absence of alternatives, requiring the apodosis to be read as a necessary consequence.
chapters.translation:
[Chapter] And let him be extremely wary of intending to increase his following by the multitude of those who study under him and those who come to him. And let him be wary of disliking his students' reading before others who may benefit them. This is a calamity by which some ignorant teachers are afflicted, and it is a clear indication from its possessor of his evil intention and the corruption of his inner disposition. Rather, it is a conclusive proof of his not intending by his teaching the Face of Allah, the Exalted, the Generous. For had he intended Allah by his teaching, he would not have disliked that. Rather, he would have said to himself: "I intended obedience to Allah by teaching him, and it has been attained. And he intended by his reading before someone else an increase in knowledge, so there is no blame upon him."

And we have related in the Musnad of the Imam whose preservation and imamate are unanimously agreed upon, Abū Muḥammad al-Dārimī (may Allah have mercy upon him), from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib (may Allah be pleased with him) that he said: "O bearers of the Qur'an" — or he said: "O bearers of knowledge — act upon it, for knowledge belongs only to him who acts upon what he knows, and whose action conforms to his knowledge. There will come people who bear knowledge that does not pass beyond their collarbones; their actions will contradict their knowledge, and their inner secrets will contradict their outward appearances. They will sit in circles, vying with one another in pride, until a man becomes angry at his companion for sitting with someone else and leaving him. Those — their deeds will not ascend from those gatherings of theirs to Allah, the Exalted." And it is authentically established from Imam al-Shāfiʿī (may Allah be pleased with him) that he said: "I wish that the people had learned this knowledge" — meaning his knowledge and his books — "so that not a single letter of it were attributed to me."

[Chapter] On Noble Character Traits

And it behooves the teacher to adorn himself with the excellences that the Sacred Law has brought, and the praiseworthy qualities and pleasing dispositions to which Allah has guided him — such as asceticism (zuhd) in this world, and taking little from it, and not caring about it or its people; and generosity, munificence, and noble character traits; and a cheerful countenance without exceeding into the limit of frivolity; and forbearance, patience, and abstention from base earnings; and adherence to scrupulous piety (waraʿ), humility, tranquility, and dignity; and humility and submissiveness; and avoiding laughter and excessive jesting; and adherence to the prescribed religious practices (al-waẓāʾif al-sharʿiyyah), such as cleanliness, and removing the filth and hairs whose removal the Sacred Law has commanded — like trimming the moustache, clipping the nails, combing the beard, and removing foul odors and disliked garments.

And let him be extremely wary of envy, ostentation (riyāʾ), self-admiration, and contempt for others, even if they be beneath him. And he should practice the supplications related concerning glorification (tasbīḥ), declaration of Allah's oneness (tahlīl), and similar remembrances (adhkār) and invocations (daʿawāt). And he should be mindful of Allah, the Exalted, in his secret and his public affairs, and preserve that, and his reliance in all his matters should be upon Allah, the Exalted.

[Chapter] On Kindness to the Student

And it behooves him to be gentle with the one who reads before him, and to welcome him and treat him well according to his condition. For we have related from Abū Hārūn al-ʿAbdī who said: "We used to come to Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī (may Allah be pleased with him), and he would say: 'Welcome to the testament of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him)!' For the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: {Indeed, the people are followers of you, and men will come to you from the corners of the earth to gain understanding in the religion. So when they come to you, treat them well.} Related by al-Tirmidhī and Ibn Mājah and others. And we have related something similar in the Musnad of al-Dārimī from Abū al-Dardāʾ (may Allah be pleased with him).

[Chapter] On Sincere Counsel to Him

And it behooves him to offer them sincere counsel (naṣīḥah), for the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: {Religion is sincere counsel — to Allah, to His Book, to His Messenger, and to the leaders of the Muslims and their common folk.} Related by Muslim. And from sincere counsel to Allah, the Exalted, and to His Book is honoring its reader and seeker, guiding him to his best interest, being gentle with him, assisting him in his pursuit as much as possible, and winning the heart of the student. And he should be generous in teaching him with gentleness, treating him with kindness, and urging him toward learning. And he should remind him of its virtue, so that this may be a cause for his vigor and an increase in his desire. And he should make him ascetic in this world and turn him away from relying upon it and being deluded by it.

And he should remind him of the virtue of occupying oneself with the Qur'an and the rest of the religious sciences — for that is the path of the knowers of Allah (al-ʿārifīn) and the righteous servants of Allah, and that it is the rank of the prophets (peace and blessings be upon them). And it behooves him to be compassionate toward the student and to attend to his interests as he attends to the interests of his own child and his own self. And he should treat the student like his own child in compassion toward him, and in patience with his harshness and ill manners, and excuse him for his lack of manners at times — for man is subject to deficiencies, especially if he is young in age. And he should love for him what he loves for himself of good, and dislike for him what he dislikes for himself of deficiency, absolutely. For it is established in the two Ṣaḥīḥs from the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) that he said: {None of you believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.} And from Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them both) who said: "The most generous of people to me is the one who steps over people until he sits with me. If I could prevent a fly from landing on his face, I would do so." And in another narration: "Indeed, a fly lands on him and harms me." And it behooves him not to hold himself in haughty superiority over the students, but rather to be gentle with them and humble before them.

For much has come concerning humility toward individual people, as is well known — so how much more so toward these who are in the position of his own children, along with their occupation with the Qur'an, and the right of companionship they have upon him, and their frequent coming to him? And it has come from the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) that he said: {Be gentle with those you teach and those from whom you learn.} And from Abū Ayyūb al-Sakhtiyānī (may Allah have mercy upon him) who said: "It behooves the scholar to place dust upon his head out of humility before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."

[Chapter] On Training the Student

And it behooves him to discipline the student gradually with the lofty etiquettes and pleasing dispositions, and to train his soul in the subtle refinements, and to accustom him to propriety in all his inner and outward affairs. And he should urge him, through his repeated words and deeds, toward sincerity (ikhlāṣ), truthfulness, good intentions, and mindfulness of Allah, the Exalted, in every glance. And he should inform him that through this, the lights of divine knowledge (anwār al-maʿārif) open upon him, his breast expands, and from his heart springs forth the fountains of wisdom and subtleties, and he is blessed in his knowledge and his state, and he is granted success in his deeds and his words.

[Chapter] On the Ruling of Teaching

Teaching students is a communal obligation (farḍ kifāyah). For if there is no one qualified except a single person, then it becomes personally incumbent upon him. And if there is a group by whom teaching can be accomplished through some of them, then if they all refuse, they all sin. And if some of them undertake it, the burden falls from the rest. And if one of them is asked and he refuses...

chapters.arabic_text: فأظهر الوجهين أنه لا يأثم لكن يكره له ذلك إن لم يكن عذر # إخلاص المعلم | [فصل] يستحب للمعلم أن يكون حريصا على تعليمهم # مؤثرا ذلك على مصالح نفسه الدنيوية التي ليست بضرورية # # وأن يفرغ قلبه في حال جلوسه لإقرائهم من من الأسباب الشاغلة كلها وهي كثيرة معروفة وأن يكون حريصا على تفهيمهم وأن يعطي كل إنسان منهم ما يليق به فلا يكثر على من لا يحتمل الإكثار ولا يقصر لمن يحتمل الزيادة ويأخذهم بإعادة محفوظاتهم ويثني على من ظهرت نجابته ما لم يخش عليه فتنة بإعجاب أو غيره ومن قصر عنفه تعنيفا لظيفا في ما لم يخش عليه تنفيره ولا يحسد أحدا منه لبراعة تظهر منه ولا يستكثر فيه ما أنعم الله به عليه فإن الحسد للأجانب حرام شديد التحريم فكيف للمتعلم الذي هو بمنزلة الولد ويعود من فضيلته إلى معلمه في الآخرة الثواب الجزيل وفي الدنيا الثناء الجميل والله الموفق | [فصل] ويقدم في تعليمهم إذا ازدحموا الأول فالأول # فإن رضي الأول بتقديم غيره قدمه وينبغي أن يظهر لهم البشر وطلاقة الوجه ويتفقد أحوالهم ويسأل عمن غاب منهم # [فصل] قال العلماء رضي الله عنهم ولا يمتنع من تعليم أحد لكونه غير صحيح النية فقد قال سفيان وغيره طلبهم للعلم نية وقالوا طلبنا العلم لغير الله فأبى أن يكون إلا لله معناه كانت غايته أن صار لله تعالى # # أدب المعلم | | [فصل] ومن آدابه المتأكدة # وما يعتنى به أن يصون يديه في حال الإقراء عن العبث وعينيه عن تفريق نظرهما من غير حاجة ويقعد على طهارة مستقبل القبلة ويجلس بوقار وتكون ثيابه بيضا نظيفة وإذا وصل إلى موضع جلوسه صلى ركعتين قبل الجلوس سواء كان الموضع مسجدا أو غيره فإن كان مسجدا كان آكد فيه فإنه يكره الجلوس فيه قبل أن يصلي ركعتين ويجلس متربعا إن شاء أو غير متربع روى أبو بكر بن أبي داود السجستاني باسناده عن عبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله عنه كان يقرئ الناس في المسجد جاثيا على ركبتيه # [فصل] ومن آدابه المتأكدة وما يعتني بحفظه أن لا يذل العلم فيذهب إلى مكان ينسب إلى من يتعلم منه ليتعلم منه فيه وأن كان المتعلم خليفة فمن دونه بل يصون العلم عن ذلك كما صانه عنه السلف رضي الله عنهم وحكاياتهم في هذا كثيرة مشهورة | [فصل] وينبغي أن يكون مجلسه واسعا # ليتمكن جلساؤه فيه ففي الحديث عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: # خير المجالس أوسعها رواه أبو داود في سنته في أوائل كتاب الآداب بإسناد صحيح من # # رواية أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه في آداب المتعلم | [فصل] جميع ما ذكرناه من آداب المعلم في نفسه آداب للمتعلم # # ومن آدابه أن يجتنب الأسباب الشاغلة عن التحصيل إلا سببا لا بد منه للحاجة وينبغي أن يطهر قلبه من الأدناس ليصلح لقبول القرآن وحفظه واستثماره فقد صح عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: أنه قال ألا إن في الجسد مضغة إذا صلحت صلح الجسد كله وإذا فسدت فسد الجسد كله ألا وهي القلب وقد أحسن القائل بقوله يطيب القلب للعلم كما تطيب الأرض للزراعة وينبغي أن يتواضع لمعلمه ويتأدب معه وأن كان أصغر منه سنا وأقل شهرة ونسبا وصلاحا وغير ذلك ويتواضع للعلم فبتواضعه يدركه وقد قالوا نظما العلم حرب للفتى المتعالي * بن كالسيل حرب للمكان العالي * # # وينبغي أن ينقاد لمعلمه ويشاوره في أموره ويقبل قوله كالمريض العاقل يقبل قول الطبيب الناصح الحاذق وهذا أولى | [فصل] ولا يتعلم إلا ممن تكلمت أهليته وظهرت ديانته # وتحققت معرفته واشتهرت صيانته فقد قال محمد بن سيرين ومالك بن أنس وغيرهما من السلف هذا العلم دين فانظروا عمن تأخذون دينكم وعليه أن ينظر معلمه بعين الاحترام ويعتقد كمال أهليته ورجحانه على طبقته فإنه أقرب إلى انتفاعه به وكان بعض المتقدمين إذا ذهب إلى معلمه تصدق بشئ وقال اللهم استر عيب معلمي عني ولا تذهب بركة علمه مني وقال الربيع صاحب الشافعي رحمهما الله ما اجترأت أن أشرب الماء والشافعي ينظر إلي هيبة له وروينا عن أمير المؤمنين علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه قال من حق المعلم عليك أن تسلم على الناس عامة وتخصه دونهم بتحية وأن تجلس أمامه ولا تشيرن عنده بيدك ولا تغمزن بعينيك ولا تقولن قال فلان خلاف ما تقول ولا تغتابن عنده أحدا ولا تشاور جليسك في مجلسه ولا تأخذ بثوبه إذا قام ولا تلح عليه إذا كسل ولا تعرض أي تشبع من طول صحبته وينبغي أن يتأدب بهذه الخصال التي أرشد إليها علي كرم الله وجهه وأن يرد غيبة شيخه إن قدر فإن تعذر عليه ردها فارق ذلك المجلس اه. # | [فصل] ويدخل على الشيخ كامل الخصال # متصفا بما ذكرناه في المعلم متطهرا مستعملا للسواك فارغ القلب من الأمور الشاغلة # * وأن لا يدخل بغير استئذان إذا كان الشيخ في مكان يحتاج فيه إلى * استئذان وأن يسلم على الحاضرين إذا دخل ويخصه دونهم بالتحية * وأن يسلم عليه وعليهم إذا انصرف كما جاء في الحديث فليست * الأولى أحق من الثانية ولا يتخطى رقاب الناس بل يجلس حيث ينتهي به المجلس إلا أن يأذن له الشيخ في التقدم أو يعلم من حالهم إيثار ذلك ولا يقيم أحدا من موضعه فإن آثره غيره لم يقبل اقتداء بابن عمر رضي الله عنهما إلا أن يكون في تقديمه مصلحة للحاضرين أو أمره الشيخ بذلك ولا يجلس في وسط الحلقة إلا لضرورة * ولا يجلس بين صاحبين بغير إذنهما وإن فسحا له قعد وضم نفسه # أدبه مع رفاقه | [فصل] وينبغي أيضا أن يتأدب مع رفقته # وحاضري مجلس الشيخ فإن ذلك تأدب مع الشيخ وصيانة لمجلسه ويقعد بين يدي الشيخ قعدة المتعلمين لا قعدة # # المعلمين ولا يرفع صوته رفعا بليغا من غير حاجة ولا يضحك ولا يكثر الكلام
chapters.anchors:
- Root: خ-ل-ص (khalasa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Purity, clarity, freedom from admixture; sincerity as the unalloyed essence of an act.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ikhlaṣ (sincerity) as the purification of intention (niyyah) so that the act is solely for Allah, the theological precondition for valid worship and learning.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — pure gold free of dross; metaphorical (majāz) — an act stripped of all worldly motives.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ) — "فإن رضي الأول بتقديم غيره قدمه" (If the first is pleased with another's precedence, he gives precedence): the protasis (sharṭ) governs the apodosis (jawāb), indicating a contingent ethical obligation, not an absolute one.
chapters.translation:
I say: The more apparent of the two positions is that he does not sin, but it is disliked (makrūh) for him to do so if there is no excuse.

# Chapter: On the Teacher's Sincerity

[Section] It is recommended (mustaḥabb) for the teacher to be eager in teaching them, preferring that over his own worldly interests which are not necessary. He should empty his heart, while seated to instruct them, of all distracting causes — and these are many and well-known. He should be keen to make them understand, and give each person what befits him: not overloading one who cannot bear much, nor holding back from one who can bear more. He should make them repeat what they have memorized, and praise the one whose excellence appears — as long as he does not fear for him a trial (fitnah) of self-admiration or otherwise. The one who falls short he should admonish with gentle reproof, as long as he does not fear driving him away. He should not envy any of them for brilliance that appears from him, nor regard as excessive what Allah has bestowed upon him. For envy of strangers is severely forbidden — how then [is it] toward a student who is like a son, and from whose virtue returns to his teacher, in the Hereafter, abundant reward, and in this world, beautiful praise? Allah is the Granter of success.

[Section] When they crowd [upon him], he gives precedence in teaching to the first, then the next. If the first is pleased to give precedence to another, he gives him precedence. He should show them cheerfulness and a smiling face, inquire about their conditions, and ask about those who are absent among them.

[Section] The scholars — may Allah be pleased with them — said: He should not refuse to teach anyone merely because his intention is not sound. For Sufyān and others said: "Their seeking of knowledge is itself an intention," and they said: "We sought knowledge for other than Allah, but it refused to be except for Allah" — meaning its ultimate end became that it was for Allah, the Exalted.

# Etiquette of the Teacher

[Section] Among his emphasized etiquettes, and what he should attend to, is that he keep his hands, while instructing, from fidgeting; his eyes from wandering without need; he sits in a state of purity (ṭahārah), facing the qiblah, with dignity; his garments white and clean. When he reaches his place of sitting, he prays two rakʿahs before sitting — whether the place is a mosque or otherwise. If it is a mosque, it is more emphatic, for it is disliked to sit in it before praying two rakʿahs. He may sit cross-legged if he wishes, or otherwise. Abū Bakr ibn Abī Dāwūd al-Sijistānī narrated with his chain from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd — may Allah be pleased with him — that he used to instruct the people in the mosque kneeling on his knees.

[Section] Among his emphasized etiquettes, and what he should be careful to preserve, is that he not debase knowledge by going to a place attributed to one from whom he learns, to learn from him there — even if the learner is a caliph or one below him. Rather, he preserves knowledge from that, just as the Salaf — may Allah be pleased with them — preserved it from that. Their stories in this regard are many and well-known.

[Section] His gathering place should be spacious, so that his companions can be comfortable in it. For in the ḥadīth from the Prophet — may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him: {«خير المجالس أوسعها»} ("The best of gatherings is the most spacious of them") — narrated by Abū Dāwūd in his Sunan, at the beginning of the Book of Etiquette, with a sound chain (isnād ṣaḥīḥ) from the narration of Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī — may Allah be pleased with him.

# On the Etiquette of the Student

[Section] All that we have mentioned of the teacher's etiquette regarding himself is also etiquette for the student. Among his etiquettes is that he avoid the causes that distract from acquisition, except a cause that is unavoidable due to need. He should purify his heart of filth, so that it becomes fit for receiving the Qur'an, memorizing it, and deriving fruit from it. For it is authentically established from the Messenger of Allah — may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him — that he said: {«ألا إن في الجسد مضغة إذا صلحت صلح الجسد كله وإذا فسدت فسد الجسد كله ألا وهي القلب»} ("Truly, in the body there is a lump of flesh; if it is sound, the whole body is sound, and if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt — truly, it is the heart.") And excellent is the saying of the one who said: "The heart becomes good for knowledge just as the earth becomes good for cultivation."

He should humble himself before his teacher and conduct himself with propriety toward him, even if the teacher is younger in age, lesser in fame, lineage, righteousness, or otherwise. He should humble himself before knowledge, for by his humility he attains it. They have said in verse: "Knowledge is war against the youth who is haughty, * like the flood is war against the high place."

He should yield to his teacher, consult him in his affairs, and accept his word — like a sensible patient accepts the word of a sincere, skillful physician. This is more fitting.

[Section] He should not learn except from one whose competence has been attested, whose religiosity has appeared, whose knowledge has been verified, and whose integrity has become well-known. For Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn, Mālik ibn Anas, and others of the Salaf said: "This knowledge is religion — so look to whom you take your religion from." He must regard his teacher with an eye of respect, and believe in the completeness of his competence and his preeminence over his peers — for that is more conducive to his benefiting from him. Some of the early scholars, when going to their teacher, would give charity and say: "O Allah, conceal the fault of my teacher from me, and do not take away the blessing of his knowledge from me." Al-Rabīʿ, the companion of al-Shāfiʿī — may Allah have mercy on them both — said: "I never dared to drink water while al-Shāfiʿī was looking at me, out of awe of him." And we have narrated from the Commander of the Believers, ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib — may Allah be pleased with him — that he said: "Of the right of the teacher upon you is that you greet the people generally, and single him out with a special salutation; that you sit before him; that you do not gesture at him with your hand, nor wink with your eyes; that you do not say, 'So-and-so said contrary to what you say'; that you do not backbite anyone in his presence; that you do not consult your companion in his gathering; that you do not take hold of his garment when he stands; that you do not importune him when he is weary; and that you do not become bored — i.e., satiated — from the length of his companionship." He should conduct himself according to these traits that ʿAlī — may Allah honor his face — guided to, and he should repel the backbiting of his shaykh if he is able. If repelling it becomes impossible for him, he leaves that gathering. End.

[Section] He enters upon the shaykh with complete qualities, characterized by what we have mentioned regarding the teacher: purified, using the toothstick (siwāk), his heart empty of distracting matters. He should not enter without permission if the shaykh is in a place requiring permission. He greets those present upon entering, and singles him out with a special salutation. He greets him and them upon departing, as came in the ḥadīth: the first greeting is not more deserving than the second. He does not step over people's necks, but sits where the gathering ends for him — unless the shaykh permits him to advance, or he knows from their state that they prefer that. He does not remove anyone from his place; and if another yields his place to him, he does not accept it — following the example of Ibn ʿUmar — may Allah be pleased with them both — unless there is in his advancement a benefit for those present, or the shaykh commands him to do so. He does not sit in the middle of the circle except for necessity. He does not sit between two companions without their permission; and if they make room for him, he sits and makes himself compact.

# His Etiquette with His Companions

[Section] He should also conduct himself with propriety toward his companions and those present in the shaykh's gathering — for that is propriety toward the shaykh and protection of his gathering. He sits before the shaykh in the sitting posture of students, not that of teachers. He does not raise his voice excessively without need, does not laugh, and does not speak much.

chapters.arabic_text:
من غير حاجة ولا يعبث بيده ولا بغيرها ولا يلتفت يمينا ولا شمالا من غير

حاجة بل يكون متوجها إلى الشيخ مصغيا إلى كلامه أدبه مع شيخه

| [فصل] ومما يتأكد الاعتناء به أن لا يقرأ على الشيخ في حال شغل قلب الشيخ
# وملله واستيفازه سنة وروعه وغمه وفرحه وعطشه ونعاسه وقلقه ونحو ذلك مما

يشق عليه أو يمنعه من كمال حضور القلب والنشاط وأن يغتنم أوقات نشاطه ومن

آدابه أن يتحمل جفوة الشيخ وسوء خلقه ولا يصده ذلك عن ملازمته واعتقاد

كماله ويتأول لأفعاله  وأقواله التي ظاهرها الفساد تأويلات صحيحة فما يعجز

عن ذلك إلا قليل التوفيق أو عديمه وأن جفاه الشيخ ابتدأ هو بالاعتذار إلى

الشيخ وأظهر أن الذنب له والعتب عليه فذلك أنفع له في الدنيا والآخرة وأنقى

لقلب الشيخ
# 
# وقد قالوا من لم يصبر على ذل التعليم بقي عمره في عماية الجهالة ومن صبر

عليه آل أمره إلى عز الاخرة والدنيا ومنه الأثر المشهور عن ابن عباس رضي

الله عنهما ذللت طالبا فعززت مطلوبا وقد أحسن من قال
# من لم يذق طعم المذلة ساعة * قطع الزمان بأسره مذلولا
# حرصه على العلم

| [فصل] ومن آدابه المتأكدة أن يكون حريصا على التعلم
# مواظبا عليه في جميع الأوقات التي يتمكن منه فيها ولا يقنع بالقليل مع

تمكنه من الكثير ولا يحمل نفسه ما لا يطيق مخافة من الملل وضياع ما حصل

وهذا يختلف باختلاف الناس والأحوال وإذا جاء إلى مجلس الشيخ فلم يجده انتظر

ولازم بابه ولا يفوت وظيفته إلا أن يخاف كراهة الشيخ لذلك بأن يعلم من حاله

الإقراء في وقت بعينه وأنه لا يقرئ في غيره وإذا وجد الشيخ نائما أو مشتغلا

بمهم لم يستأذن عليه بل يصبر إلى استيقاظه أو فراغه أو ينصرف والصبر أولى

كما كان ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما وغيره يفعلون وينبغي أن يأخذ نفسه

بالإجتهاد في التحصيل في وقت الفراغ والنشاط وقوة البدن ونباهة الخاطر وقلة

الشاغلات قبل عوارض البطالة وارتفاع المنزلة فقد قال أمير المؤمنين عمر بن

الخطاب رضي الله عنه تفقهوا قبل أن تسودوا
# 
# معناه اجتهدوا في كمال أهليتكم قبل وأنتم أتباع قبل أن تصيروا سادة فإنكم

إذا صرتم سادة متبوعين امتنعتم من التعلم لارتفاع منزلتكم وكثرة شغلكم وهذا

معنى قول الإمام الشافعي رضي الله عنه تفقه قبل أن ترأس فإذا رأست فلا سبيل

إلى التفقه

| [فصل] وينبغي أن يبكر بقراءته على الشيخ أول النهار
# لحديث النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: اللهم بارك لأمتي في بكورها وينبغي أن

يحافظ على قراءة محفوظه وينبغي أن لا  يؤثر بنوبته غيره فإن الإيثار مكروه

في القرب بخلاف الإيثار بحظوظ النفس فإنه محبوب فإن رأى الشيخ المصلحة في

الإيثار في بعض الأوقات لمعنى
# 
# شرعي فأشار عليه بذلك امتثل أمره ومما يجب عليه ويتأكد الوصية به ألا

يحسد أحدا من رفقته أو غيرهم على فضيلة رزقه الله إياها وأن لا يعجب بنفسه

بما خصه الله وقد قدمنا ايضاح هذا في آداب الشيخ وطريقه في نفي العجب أن

يذكر نفسه أنه لم يحصل ما حصله بحوله وقوته وإنما هو فضل من الله ولا ينبغي

أن يعجب بشئ لم يخترعه بل أودعه الله تعالى فيه وطريقه في نفي الحسد أن

يعلم أن حكمة الله تعالى اقتضت جعل هذه الفضيلة في هذا
# 
# فينبغي أن لا يعترض عليها ولا يكره حكمة أرادها الله تعالى ولم يكرهها
#

| الباب الخامس في آداب حامل القرآن
# قد تقدم جمل منه في الباب الذي قبل هذا ومن آدابه أن يكون على أكمل

الأحوال وأكرم الشمائل وأن يرفع نفسه عن كل ما نهى القرآن عنه إجلالا

للقرآن وأن يكون مصونا عن دنئ الاكتساب شريف النفس مرتفعا على الجبابرة

والجفاة من أهل الدنيا متواضعا للصالحين وأهل الخير والمساكين وأن يكون

متخشعا ذا سكينة ووقار * فقد جاء عن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه أنه قال يا

معشر القراء ارفعوا رؤوسكم فقد وضح لكم الطريق فاستبقوا الخيرات لا تكونوا

عيالا على الناس
# وعن عبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله عنه قال ينبغي لحامل القرآن أن يعرف

بليله إذا الناس نائمون وبنهاره إذا الناس مفطرون وبحزنه إذا الناس يفرحون

وببكائه إذا الناس يضحكون وبصحته إذا الناس يخوضون، ويخسوعه إذا الناس

يختالون وعن الحسن بن علي رضي الله عنه قال إن من كان قبلكم رأوا القرآن

رسائل من ربهم فكانوا يتدبرونها بالليل ويتفقدونها في النهار
# 
# وعن الفضيل بن عياض قال ينبغي لحامل القرآن أن لا تكون له حاجة إلى أحد

من الخلفاء فمن دونهم وعنه أيضا قال حامل القرآن حامل راية الإسلام لا

ينبغي  أن يلهو مع من يلهو ولا يسهو مع من يسهو ولا يلغو مع من يلغو تعظيما

لحق القرآن
# بعده عن التكسب به

| [فصل] ومن أهم ما يؤمر به أن يحذر كل الحذر من اتخاذ القرآن معيشة يكتسب بها
# 
# فقد جاء عن عبد الرحمن بن شبيل رضي الله عنه قال قال رسول الله صلى الله

عليه وسلم: اقرؤوا القرآن ولا تأكلوا به ولا تجفوا عنه ولا تغلوا فيه وعن

جابر رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: اقرؤوا القرآن من قبل أن

يأتي قوم يقيمونه إقامة القدح يتعجلونه
# ولا يتأجلونه رواه بمعناه من رواية سهل بن سعد معناه يتعجلون أجره إما

بمال وإما سمعة ونحوها
# 
# وعن فضيل بن عمرو رضي الله عنه قال دخل رجلان من أصحاب رسول الله صلى

الله عليه وسلم: مسجدا فلما سلم الإمام قام رجل فتلا آيات من القرآن ثم سأل

فقال أحدهما إنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

يقول سيجئ قوم يسألون بالقرآن فمن سأل بالقرآن فلا تعطوه وهذا الإسناد

منقطع فإن الفضل بن عمرو لم يسمع الصحابة وأما أخذ الأجرة على تعليم القرآن

فقد اختلف العلماء فيه فحكى الإمام أبو سليمان الخطابي منع أخذ الأجرة عليه

- Root: و-ج-ه (w-j-h)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Face, direction, orientation; turning one's countenance toward something.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Intentional orientation of the heart and body toward the object of veneration, as in devotional focus (tawajjuh).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal physical turning (Ḥaqīqah) vs. metaphorical attentiveness of the heart (Majāz); here both converge.
- Sībawayh Rule: Ḥāl Clause (الْحَال) — The circumstantial accusatives (e.g., "mutawajjihan," "muṣghiyan") describe the subject's state during the main verb, requiring simultaneous occurrence.

- Root: ص-ب-ر (ṣ-b-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Restraint, endurance, steadfastness under hardship.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Retention of the soul within its divinely ordained bounds; patience as a prerequisite for knowledge acquisition.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal forbearance vs. metaphorical "digesting" of humiliation (dhull) as a means to honor (ʿizz).
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (الشَّرْط) — "Man lam yaṣbir... āla amruhu" (whoever does not endure... his affair ends) demonstrates the protasis-apodosis structure with perfective verbs for universal truths.

- Root: ح-ر-ص (ḥ-r-ṣ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Intense desire, eager craving for something.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Commendable zeal when directed toward knowledge and obedience; blameworthy greed when worldly.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal covetousness vs. metaphorical "hunger" for learning that never satiates.
- Sībawayh Rule: Emphasis (التَّوْكِيد) — "ḥarīṣan" as a predicate of "yakūna" with the particle "an" (obligation), reinforcing the mandatory nature of the trait.

- Root: ب-ك-ر (b-k-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Early morning, the first part of the day.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The blessed time for spiritual and intellectual endeavors, as the Prophet ﷺ supplicated for blessing in it.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal dawn-time vs. metaphorical "beginning" of any undertaking.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf Bayān (عَطْف الْبَيَان) — Appositional clarification in "bukūrihā" (its early morning) specifying the exact temporal scope.
