- Root: س-م-ع (s-m-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Auditory perception; receiving sound waves through the ear.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Hearing with comprehension; in legal context, the act of listening to divine speech (kalām Allāh) as a means of daʿwah.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical hearing; metaphorical (majāz) for obedience (samʿan wa ṭāʿatan).
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-sharṭ wa al-jawāb) — The protasis "in kāna lā yurjā islāmuhu" governs the apodosis "lam yajuz taʿlīmuhu," establishing a legal causality.
chapters.translation:
I say: One says "the sunnah of so-and-so" and "the recitation of so-and-so," and the correct view is what we have already presented.

# Ruling on an Unbeliever Hearing the Quran

| [Section] An unbeliever is not prevented from hearing the Quran, due to the saying of Allah the Exalted: {«وَإِنْ أَحَدٌ مِّنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ اسْتَجَارَكَ فَأَجِرْهُ حَتَّىٰ يَسْمَعَ كَلَامَ اللَّهِ»} ("And if any of the polytheists seeks your protection, then grant him protection so that he may hear the word of Allah") [Quran 9:6].

But he is prevented from touching the muṣḥaf (physical copy of the Quran). As for teaching him the Quran, our companions (the Shāfiʿīs) said: If his conversion to Islam is not hoped for, it is not permissible to teach him. If his conversion is hoped for, there are two views (wajhān): The more correct of the two is that it is permissible, hoping for his conversion. The second view is that it is not permissible, just as it is not permissible to sell him a muṣḥaf even if his conversion is hoped for. However, if we see him learning (on his own), there are two views on whether he should be prevented.

# Ruling on Writing the Quran on Vessels

| [Section] The scholars differed regarding writing the Quran in a vessel, then washing it and giving the water to a sick person to drink. Al-Ḥasan (al-Baṣrī), Mujāhid, Abū Qilābah, and al-Awzāʿī said: There is no harm in it. Al-Nakhaʿī disapproved of it. Qāḍī Ḥusayn, al-Baghawī, and others among our companions said: If one writes the Quran on sweets (ḥalwā) and other foods, there is no harm in eating them. Qāḍī (Ḥusayn) said: If it were on a piece of wood, he disapproved of burning it.

# Ruling on Writing Letters (al-Ḥurūf)

| [Section] Our school (madhhab) holds that it is disapproved (makrūh) to engrave walls and garments with the Quran and with the names of Allah the Exalted. ʿAṭāʾ said: There is no harm in writing the Quran on the qiblah of the mosque. As for writing amulets (ḥurūz) from the Quran, Mālik said: There is no harm in it if it is in a reed tube or leather, and stitched over it. Some of our companions said: If one writes in an amulet the Quran along with other things, it is not unlawful (ḥarām), but it is better to leave it, because it is carried during states of ritual impurity (ḥadath). And if it is written, it should be protected as stated by Imām Mālik, may Allah have mercy on him. And this is the fatwā given by Shaykh Abū ʿAmr ibn al-Ṣalāḥ, may Allah have mercy on him.

# [Section] On Blowing (al-Nafth) with the Quran for Ruqyah (Incantation)

Ibn Abī Dāwūd narrated from Abū Juḥayfah the Companion, may Allah be pleased with him — his name being Wahb ibn ʿAbd Allāh, and it was also said other than that — and from al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī and Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī that they disapproved of that. But the chosen view (al-mukhtār) is that this is not disapproved; rather, it is a recommended sunnah (sunnah mustaḥabbah). For it is authentically established from ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, when he retired to his bed every night, would cup his palms together, then blow into them, and recite into them {«قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ»} ("Say: He is Allah, the One") and {«قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ الْفَلَقِ»} ("Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the dawn") and {«قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ النَّاسِ»} ("Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind"), then wipe with them as much of his body as he could, starting with his head, face, and the front of his body, doing this three times. Narrated by al-Bukhārī and Muslim in their two Ṣaḥīḥs. In some narrations in the two Ṣaḥīḥs there is additional content beyond this. In some of them, ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: "When he fell ill, he would order me to do that for him." In some of them: "The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would blow over himself during the illness in which he died with the muʿawwidhat (the two or three refuge-seeking surahs)." ʿĀʾishah said: "When he became heavy (with illness), I would blow over him with them and wipe with his own hand for its blessing." In some of them: "When he was ill, he would recite over himself the muʿawwidhat and blow." The linguists said: Al-nafth is a gentle blowing without saliva. And Allah knows best.

# Chapter Eight: On the Verses and Surahs Recommended at Specific Times and Circumstances

Know that this chapter is extremely vast and cannot be fully encompassed due to the abundance of what has been reported concerning it. But we will point to most of it, or much of it, with concise expressions. For most of what we mention in it is known to the elite and the common folk alike, and for this reason I do not mention the evidences for most of it. Among that is the great care for reciting the Quran in the month of Ramaḍān — and in the last ten days (of it) more emphatically, and in the odd nights (layālī al-witr) of it even more emphatically. And among that is the first ten days of Dhū al-Ḥijjah, the Day of ʿArafah, the Day of Friday, after the dawn prayer, and in the night. And one should consistently recite Sūrat Yāsīn, al-Wāqiʿah, and Tabārak al-Mulk.

# The Sunnah Recitations (al-Qirāʾāt al-Masnūnah)

| [Section] It is the sunnah to recite in the dawn prayer (ṣalāt al-ṣubḥ) on Friday, after the Fātiḥah, in the first rakʿah Sūrat {«الم تَنزِيلُ»} (Alif Lām Mīm, the Revelation — i.e., al-Sajdah) in its entirety, and in the second rakʿah {«هَلْ أَتَىٰ عَلَى الْإِنسَانِ»} ("Has there come upon man...") in its entirety. And one should not do what many imams of mosques do — restricting themselves to some verses from each of them while elongating the recitation (tamṭīṭ). Rather, one should recite both of them in full, and he should moderate his recitation (yudrij qirāʾatahu) with proper pacing (tartīl). And it is the sunnah to recite in the Friday prayer (ṣalāt al-jumuʿah) in the first rakʿah Sūrat al-Jumuʿah in its entirety, or if he wishes {«سَبِّحِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ الْأَعْلَىٰ»} ("Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High"), and in the second rakʿah {«هَلْ أَتَاكَ حَدِيثُ الْغَاشِيَةِ»} ("Has there reached you the narration of the Overwhelming?") — for both are authentically reported from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. And he should avoid restricting himself to part (of them) and should do what we have presented. And it is the sunnah in the Eid prayer (ṣalāt al-ʿīd) to recite in the first rakʿah Sūrat Qāf, and in the second rakʿah Sūrat al-Sāʿah (i.e., al-Ghāshiyah) in its entirety, or if he wishes {«سَبِّحِ»} and {«هَلْ أَتَاكَ»} — for both are authentically reported from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. And he should avoid restricting himself to part (of them).

| [Section] And in the two rakʿahs of the sunnah of the dawn prayer (sunnat al-fajr), after the Fātiḥah, one recites in the first {«قُلْ يَا أَيُّهَا الْكَافِرُونَ»} ("Say: O disbelievers") and in the second {«قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ»} ("Say: He is Allah, the One"). And if he wishes, he may recite in the first {«قُولُوا آمَنَّا بِاللَّهِ وَمَا أُنزِلَ إِلَيْنَا»} ("Say: We believe in Allah and what has been revealed to us") — the verse — and in the second {«قُلْ يَا أَهْلَ الْكِتَابِ تَعَالَوْا إِلَىٰ كَلِمَةٍ سَوَاءٍ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَكُمْ»} ("Say: O People of the Scripture, come to a word common between us and you"). And in the sunnah of the Maghrib prayer, one recites {«قُلْ يَا أَيُّهَا الْكَافِرُونَ»} and {«قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ»}. And one recites these two as well in the two rakʿahs of the ṭawāf (circumambulation) and the two rakʿahs of the istikhārah (prayer for guidance).

And whoever prays witr with three rakʿahs recites in the first rakʿah {«سَبِّحِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ الْأَعْلَىٰ»}, in the second {«قُلْ يَا أَيُّهَا الْكَافِرُونَ»}, and in the third {«قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ»} and the muʿawwidhatayn (al-Falaq and al-Nās).

| [Section] It is recommended to recite Sūrat al-Kahf on Friday, due to the hadith of Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, may Allah be pleased with him, and others concerning it. Imām al-Shāfiʿī said in al-Umm: It is also recommended to recite it on the night of Friday. The evidence for this is what Abū Muḥammad al-Dārimī narrated with his chain from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "Whoever recites Sūrat al-Kahf on the night of Friday, a light will shine for him between him and the Ancient House (al-Bayt al-ʿAtīq, i.e., the Kaʿbah)." And al-Dārimī mentioned a hadith on the recommendation of reciting Sūrat Hūd on Friday. And from Makḥūl, the venerable Tābiʿī, (it is reported) the recommendation of reciting Āl ʿImrān on Friday.

| [Section] It is recommended to recite abundantly Āyat al-Kursī in all places, and to recite it every night when retiring to bed, and to recite the muʿawwidhatayn after every prayer. For it is authentically established from ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, commanded me to recite the muʿawwidhatayn after every prayer." Narrated by Abū Dāwūd, al-Tirmidhī, and al-Nasāʾī. Al-Tirmidhī said: A ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith.

# What is Recited at Sleep

| [Section] It is recommended to recite at sleep: Āyat al-Kursī, {«قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ»}, the muʿawwidhatayn, and the end of Sūrat al-Baqarah. For this is among the matters that one should be diligent about.

chapters.title_en: Section 24 — Nightly and Occasional Recitations: At Sleep, Upon Waking, at the Sickbed, and at the Deceased; and the Compilation and Veneration of the Muṣḥaf
chapters.arabic_text: له ويتأكد الاعتناء به فقد ثبت فيه أحاديث صحيحة عن أبي مسعود البدري رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: قال # # الآيتان من آخر سورة البقرة من قرأ بهما في ليلة كفتاه قال جماعة من أهل العلم كفتاه عن قيام الليل وقال آخرون كفتاه المكروه في ليلته # وعن عائشة رضي الله عنها أن النبي صلى الله علية وسلم: كان كل ليلة يقرأ قل هو الله أحد والمعوذتين وقد قدمناه في فصل النفث بالقرآن وروى عن أبي داود باسناده عن علي كرم الله وجهه قال ما كنت أرى أحدا يعقل دخل في الاسلام ينام حتى يقرأ آية الكرسي * وعن علي كرم الله وجهه أيضا قال ما كنت أرى أحدا يعقل ينام قبل أن يقرأ الآيات الثلاث الأواخر من سورة البقرة اسناده صحيح على شرط البخاري ومسلم * وعن عقبة بن عامر رضي الله عنه قال قال لي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: لا تمر بك ليلة إلا قرأت فيها قل هو الله أحد والمعوذتين فما أتت علي ليلة إلا وأنا أقرؤهن * فإن وعن إبراهيم النخعي قال كانوا يستحبون أن يقرؤوا هذه السور كل ليلة ثلاث مرات قل هو الله أحد والمعوذتين إسناده صحيح على شرط مسلم * وعن إبراهيم أيضا كانوا يعلمونهم إذا أووا إلى فراشهم أن يقرؤوا المعوذتين # # * وعن عائشة رضي الله عنها كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: لا ينام حتى يقرأ الزمر وبني اسرائيل رواه الترمذي وقال حسن * ويستحب أن يقرأ إذا استيقظ من النوم كل ليلة آخر آل عمران من قوله تعالى إن في خلق السماوات والأرض إلى أخرها فقد ثبت في الصحيحين أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: كان يقرأ خواتيم آل عمران إذا استيقظ # | | [فصل] فيما يقرأ عند المريض # يستحب أن يقرأ عند المريض بالفاتحة لقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم: في الحديث الصحيح فيها وما أدراك أنها رقية * ويستحب أن يقرأ عنده قل هو الله أحد وقل أعوذ برب الفلق وقل أعوذ برب الناس مع النفث في اليدين فقد ثبت في الصحيحين من فعل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: وقد تقدم بيانه في فصل النفث في آخر الباب الذي قبل هذا وعن طلحة بن مطرف قال كان المريض إذا قرئ عنده القرآن وجد لذلك خفة فدخلت على خيمته وهو مريض فقلت إني أراك اليوم صالحا فقال إني قرئ عندي القرآن وروى الخطيب أبو بكر البغدادي رحمه الله باسناده أن الرمادي رضي الله عنه كان إذا اشتكى شيئا قال هاتوا أصحاب الا حديث فإذا حضروا قال اقرؤوا على الحديث فهذا في الحديث فالقرآن أولى # | [فصل] فيما يقرأ عند الميت # قال العلماء من أصحابنا وغيرهم يستحب أن تقرأ عنده يس لحديث معقل بن يسار رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: قال اقرؤوا يس على موتاكم رواه أبو داود والنسائي في عمل اليوم والليلة وابن ماجه باسناد ضعيف وروى مجالد عن الشعبي قال كانت الأنصار إذا حضروا عند الميت قرؤوا سورة البقرة ومجالد ضعيف والله أعلم # | الباب التاسع في كتابة القرآن وإكرام المصحف # اعلم أن القرآن العزيز كان مؤلفا في زمن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: على ما هو في المصاحف اليوم ولكن لم يكن مجموعا في مصحف بل كان محفوظا في صدور الرجال فكان طوائف من الصحابة يحفظونه كله وطوائف يحفظون أبعاضا منه فلما كان زمن أبي بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه وقتل كثير من حملة # # القرآن خاف موتهم واختلاف من بعدهم فيه فاستشار الصحابة رضي الله عنهم في جمعه في مصحف فأشاروا بذلك فكتبه في مصحف وجعله في بيت حفصة أم المؤمنين رضي الله عنها فلما كان في زمن عثمان رضي الله عنه وانتشر الاسلام خاف عثمان وقوع الاختلاف المؤدي إلى ترك شئ من القرآن أو الزيادة فيه فنسخ من ذلك المجموع الذي عند حفصة الذي أجمعت الصحابة علية مصاحف وبعث بها إلى البلدان وأمر باتلاف ما خالفها وكان فعله هذا باتفاق منه ومن على بن أبي طالب وسائر الصحابة وغيرهم رضي الله عنهم وإنما لم يجعله النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: في مصحف واحد لما كان يتوقع من زيادته ونسخ بعض المتلو ولم يزل ذلك التوقع الى وفاته صلى الله عليه وسلم: فلما أمن أبو بكر وسائر أصحابه ذلك التوقع واقتضت المصلحة جمعه فعلوه رضي الله عنهم واختلفوا في عدد المصاحف التي بعث بها عثمان فقال الامام أبو عمرو الداني أكثر العلماء على أن عثمان كتب أربع نسخ 1 - فبعث إلى البصرة إحداهن 2 - وإلى الكوفة أخرى 3 - والى الشام أخرى 4 - وحبس عنده أخرى وقال أبو حاتم السجستاني كتب عثمان سبعة مصاحف # # * بعث واحدا إلى مكة * وآخر إلى الشام * وآخر إلى اليمن * وآخر إلى البحرين * وآخر إلى البصرة * وآخر إلى الكوفة * وحبس بالمدينة واحدا وهذا مختصر ما يتعلق بأول جمع المصحف وفيه أحاديث كثيرة في الصحيح وفي المصحف ثلاث لغات ضم الميم وكسرها وفتحها فالضم والكسر مشهورتان والفتح ذكرها أبو جعفر النحاس وغيره # # [ ... ] # # البدعة الحسنة | [فصل] اتفق العلماء على استحباب كتابة المصاحف # وتحسين كتابتها وتبيينها وإيضاحها وتحقق الخط دون مشقة وتعليقة قال العلماء ويستحب نقط المصحف وشكله فانه صيانة من اللحن فيه وتصحيفه وأما كراهة الشعبي والنخعي النقط فانما كرهاه في ذلك الزمان خوفا من التغيير فيه وقد أمن ذلك اليوم فلا منع ولا يمتنع من ذلك لكونه محدثا فانه من المحدثات الحسنة فلم يمنع # # منه كنظائره مثل تصنيف العلم وبناء المدارس والرباطات وغير ذلك # والله أعلم | [فصل] لا تجوز كتابة القرآن بشئ نجس وتكره كتابته على الجدران # عندنا وفيه مذهب عطاء الذي قدمناه وقد قدمنا أنه إذا كتب على الاطعمة فلا بأس بأكلها وأنه إذا كتب على خشبة كره إحراقها # القيام له
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ك-ف-ي (k-f-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Sufficiency, adequacy; to spare one from need or harm.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, denotes divine sufficiency that exempts the servant from what would otherwise burden or afflict him.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally here (ḥaqīqah) — the two verses suffice in place of something else; no metaphorical extension.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — the phrase "الآيتان من آخر سورة البقرة" is governed by the preceding verb "قال," with the predicate "كفتاه" completing the nominal sentence.
chapters.translation:
I say: And attention to it is strongly emphasized, for authentic ḥadīths have been established concerning it. Abū Masʿūd al-Badrī, may Allah be pleased with him, reported that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: {«الآيتان من آخر سورة البقرة من قرأ بهما في ليلة كفتاه»} — "The two verses at the end of Sūrat al-Baqarah — whoever recites them in a night, they suffice him." A group of the people of knowledge said: They suffice him in place of the night prayer (qiyām al-layl). Others said: They suffice him against the disliked (makrūh) in his night.

And it is reported from ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to recite every night {«قل هو الله أحد والمعوذتين»} — "Say: He is Allah, the One" and the two Muʿawwidhatān (the two chapters of seeking refuge). We have already presented this in the section on blowing (nafth) with the Qurʾān. It is also narrated by Abū Dāwūd with his chain of transmission from ʿAlī, may Allah honor his face, who said: "I did not consider anyone of understanding who had entered into Islam to sleep until he recited the Āyat al-Kursī." And likewise from ʿAlī, may Allah honor his face, who said: "I did not consider anyone of understanding to sleep before reciting the three final verses of Sūrat al-Baqarah." Its chain is authentic (ṣaḥīḥ) upon the condition of al-Bukhārī and Muslim.

And it is reported from ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to me: "No night passes over you but that you recite therein {«قل هو الله أحد والمعوذتين»}." So no night came upon me except that I recited them. And it is reported from Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī that he said: They used to deem it commendable (yastaḥibbūn) to recite these sūrahs every night three times: {«قل هو الله أحد والمعوذتين»}. Its chain is authentic upon the condition of Muslim. And likewise from Ibrāhīm: They used to teach them, when they retired to their beds, to recite the two Muʿawwidhatān.

And it is reported from ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would not sleep until he recited Sūrat al-Zumar and Sūrat Banī Isrāʾīl. Al-Tirmidhī narrated it and declared it ḥasan (good). And it is commendable to recite, upon waking from sleep every night, the end of Sūrat Āl ʿImrān, from His saying, the Exalted: {«إن في خلق السماوات والأرض»} — "Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth" — to its conclusion. For it is established in the two Ṣaḥīḥs that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to recite the concluding verses of Āl ʿImrān when he woke.

[Section] Concerning what is recited at the sick person:
It is commendable to recite at the sick person Sūrat al-Fātiḥah, due to his saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in the authentic ḥadīth concerning it: {«وما أدراك أنها رقية»} — "And what makes you know that it is a ruqyah (incantation of healing)?" And it is commendable to recite at him {«قل هو الله أحد»} and {«قل أعوذ برب الفلق»} and {«قل أعوذ برب الناس»} with blowing (nafth) into the hands. For it is established in the two Ṣaḥīḥs from the action of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Its explanation has already preceded in the section on blowing at the end of the chapter before this one. And it is reported from Ṭalḥah ibn Muṭarrif who said: When the Qurʾān was recited at a sick person, he would find lightness from that. So I entered upon his tent while he was sick and said: "I see you today in good condition." He said: "Indeed, the Qurʾān was recited at me." And al-Khaṭīb Abū Bakr al-Baghdādī, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated with his chain that al-Ramādī, may Allah be pleased with him, when he complained of something, would say: "Bring the people of ḥadīth." When they attended, he would say: "Recite upon me the ḥadīth." So if this is [done] with ḥadīth, then the Qurʾān is more worthy.

[Section] Concerning what is recited at the deceased:
The scholars among our companions and others said: It is commendable to recite at him Sūrat Yā Sīn, due to the ḥadīth of Maʿqil ibn Yasār, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: {«اقرؤوا يس على موتاكم»} — "Recite Yā Sīn upon your dead." Abū Dāwūd, al-Nasāʾī in ʿAmal al-Yawm wa al-Laylah, and Ibn Mājah narrated it with a weak (ḍaʿīf) chain. And Mujālid narrated from al-Shaʿbī who said: The Anṣār, when they attended a deceased person, used to recite Sūrat al-Baqarah. And Mujālid is weak. And Allah knows best.

Chapter Nine: On the Writing of the Qurʾān and the Veneration of the Muṣḥaf:
Know that the Noble Qurʾān was compiled (muʾallaf) in the time of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in the manner it is in the muṣḥafs today. However, it was not gathered into a single muṣḥaf; rather, it was preserved in the breasts of men. Thus, groups of the Companions memorized all of it, and groups memorized portions of it. When the era of Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, may Allah be pleased with him, came, and many of the bearers of the Qurʾān were killed, he feared their death and the divergence of those after them concerning it. So he consulted the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, about gathering it into a muṣḥaf, and they advised him to do so. So he wrote it in a muṣḥaf and placed it in the house of Ḥafṣah, the Mother of the Believers, may Allah be pleased with her. Then, when the era of ʿUthmān, may Allah be pleased with him, came, and Islam spread, ʿUthmān feared the occurrence of divergence leading to the abandonment of something of the Qurʾān or addition to it. So he copied from that gathered collection which was with Ḥafṣah — upon which the Companions had reached consensus — muṣḥafs, and sent them to the provinces, and ordered the destruction of what contradicted them. His action was by agreement of him, ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, and the rest of the Companions and others, may Allah be pleased with them all. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, did not place it in a single muṣḥaf only because he anticipated additions to it and the abrogation (naskh) of some of what was recited, and that anticipation continued until his death, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. When Abū Bakr and the rest of his Companions were secure from that anticipation, and the public interest (maṣlaḥah) necessitated its gathering, they did so, may Allah be pleased with them.

They differed concerning the number of muṣḥafs that ʿUthmān sent. Imām Abū ʿAmr al-Dānī said: The majority of scholars hold that ʿUthmān wrote four copies: 1) He sent one to Baṣrah, 2) another to Kūfah, 3) another to al-Shām, and 4) he retained one with himself. And Abū Ḥātim al-Sijistānī said: ʿUthmān wrote seven muṣḥafs: he sent one to Mecca, another to al-Shām, another to Yemen, another to Bahrain, another to Baṣrah, another to Kūfah, and retained one in Medina. This is a summary of what pertains to the first gathering of the muṣḥaf, and there are many ḥadīths concerning it in the Ṣaḥīḥ. In the word "muṣḥaf" there are three dialects: ḍamm of the mīm, kasr of it, and fatḥ of it. The ḍamm and kasr are well-known, and the fatḥ was mentioned by Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās and others.

[Section] The Commendable Innovation (al-Bidʿah al-Ḥasanah):
The scholars have agreed upon the commendability of writing the muṣḥafs, beautifying their writing, clarifying and elucidating them, and perfecting the script without hardship or suspension. The scholars said: It is commendable to dot the muṣḥaf and to vocalize it (shakl), for that is a safeguard against error (laḥn) in it and textual corruption (taṣḥīf). As for the disapproval of dotting by al-Shaʿbī and al-Nakhaʿī, they only disapproved it in that era out of fear of alteration in it. Today that fear is removed, so there is no prohibition, and it is not forbidden due to its being an innovation (muḥdath), for it is among the commendable innovations (al-muḥdathāt al-ḥasanah). Thus it is not prohibited, like its analogues, such as the codification of knowledge (taṣnīf al-ʿilm), the building of schools (madāris) and hospices (ribāṭāt), and other such things. And Allah knows best.

[Section] It is not permissible to write the Qurʾān with anything impure (najis), and it is disapproved (makrūh) to write it on walls:
This is our school (madhhab), and in it there is the position of ʿAṭāʾ which we have already presented. And we have already stated that if it is written on foods, there is no harm in eating them, and that if it is written on wood, it is disapproved to burn it. Standing for it [is not required].

| [فصل] أجمع المسلمون على وجوب صيانة المصحف
# واحترامه قال أصحابنا وغيرهم ولو ألقاه مسلم في القاذورة والعياذ بالله

تعالى صار الملقي كافرا
# 
# قالوا ويحرم توسده بل توسد آحاد كتب العلم حرام ويستحب أن يقوم للمصحف

إذا قدم به عليه لأن القيام مستحب للفضلاء من العلماء والأخيار فالمصحف

أولى وقد قررت دلائل استحباب القيام في الجزء الذي جمعته فيه وروينا في

مسند الدارمي باسناد صحيح عن ابن أبي مليكة أن عكرمة بن أبي جهل رضي الله

عنه كان يضع المصحف على وجهه ويقول كتاب ربي اه.
# بيعه مهمة غير المسلم

| [فصل] تحرم المسافرة بالمصحف إلى أرض العدو إذا خيف وقوعه في أيديهم
# للحديث المشهور في الصحيحين أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: نهى أن

يسافر بالقرآن إلى أرض العدو ويحرم بيع المصحف من الذمي فان باعه ففي صحة

البيع قولان للشافعي
# * 1 - أصحهما لا يصح * 2 - والثاني يصح ويؤمر في الحال بأزالة ملكه عنه

ويمنع المجنون والصبي الذي لا يميز من مس المصحف مخافة من انتهاك حرمته

وهذا المنع واجب على الولي وغيره ممن رآه يتعرض لحمله
# 
# مس المصحف وحمله

| [فصل] يحرم على المحدث  مس المصحف وحمله
# سواء حمله بعلاقته أو بغيرها سواء مس نفس الكتابة أو الحواشي أو الجلد

ويحرم مس الخريطة والغلاف والصندوق إذا كان فيهن المصحف هذا هو المذهب

المختار وقيل لا تحرم هذه الثلاثة وهو ضعيف ولو كتب القرآن في لوح فحكمه

حكم المصحف سواء قل المكتوب أو كثر حتى لو كان بعض آية كتب للدراسة حرم مس

اللوح
# 
# قلبه بعود

| [فصل] إذا تصفح المحدث أو الجنب أو الحائض أوراق المصحف بعود أو شبهه
# ففي جوازه وجهان لأصحابنا 1 - أظهرهما جوازه وبه قطع العراقيون من

أصحابنا لأنه غير ماس ولا حامل 2 - والثاني تحريمه لأنه يعد حاملا للورقة

والورقة كالجميع وأما إذا لف كمه على يده وقلب الورقة فحرام بلا خلاف وغلط

بعض أصحابنا فحكى فيه وجهين والصواب القطع بالتحريم لأن القلب يقع باليد لا

بالكم
# كتب المحدث له

| [فصل] إذا كتب الجنب أو المحدث
# مصحكان يحمل الورقة أو جسها حال الكتابة فحرام وان لم يحملها ولم يمسها

ففيه ثلاثة أوجه * 1 - الصحيح جوازه * 2 - والثاني تحريمه * 3 - والثالث

يجوز للمحدث ويحرم على الجنب
# 
# حمله مع غيره

| [فصل] إذا مس المحدث أو الجنب أو الحائض أو حمل كتابا
# من كتب الفقه أو غيره من العلوم وفيه آيات من القرآن أو ثوبا مطرزا

بالقرآن أو دراهم أو دنانير منقوشة به أو حمل متاعا في جملته مصحف أو لمس

الجدار أو الحلوى أو الخبز المنقوش به فالمذهب الصحيح جواز هذا كله لأنه

ليس بمصحف وفيه وجه أنه حرام وقال أقضى القضاة أبو حسن الماوردي في كتابه

الحاوي يجوز مس الثياب المطرزة بالقرآن ولا يجوز لبسها بلا خلاف لأن

المقصود بلبسها التبرك بالقرآن وهذا الذي ذكره أو قاله ضعيف لم يوافقه أحد

عليه فيما رأيته بل صرح الشيخ أبو محمد الجويني وغيره بجواز لبسها وهذا هو

الصواب والله أعلم وأما كتب تفسير القرآن فان كان القرآن فيها أكثر من غيره

حرم مسها وحملها وان كان غيره أكثر كما هو الغالب ففيها ثلاثة أوجه  * 1 -

أصحها لا يحرم * 2 - والثاني يحرم * 3 - والثالث إن كان القرآن بخط متميز

بغلظ أو حمرة أو غيرها حرم وان لم يتميز لم يحرم قلت ويحرم المس إذا استويا

قال صاحب التتمة من أصحابنا واذا قلنا لا يحرم فهو مكروه
# 
# وأما كتب حديث رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: فان لم يكن فيها آيات من

القرآن لم يحرم مسها والأولى أن لا تمس إلا على طهارة وان كان فيها آيات من

القرآن لم يحرم على المذهب وفيه وجه أنه يحرم وهو الذي في كتب الفقه وأما

المنسوخ تلاوته كالشيخ والشيخة إذا زنيا فارجموهما البتة وغير ذلك فلا يحرم

مسه ولا حمله قال أصحابنا وكذلك التوراة والإنجيل

| [فصل] إذا كان في موضع من بدن المتطهر نجاسة غير معفو عنها
# حرم عليه مس المصحف بموضع النجاسة بلا خلاف ولا يحرم بغيره على المذهب

الصحيح المشهور الذي قاله جماهير أصحابنا وغيرهم من العلماء وقال أبو

القاسم الصيمري من أصحابنا يحرم وغلطه أصحابنا في هذا قال القاضي أبو الطيب

هذا الذي قاله مردود بالاجماع ثم على المشهور قال بعض أصحابنا انه مكروه

والمختار أنه ليس بمكروه
# فروع

| [فصل] من لم يجد ماء فتيمم
# حيث يجوز التيمم له مس المصحف سواء كان تيممه للصلاة أو لغيرها مما يجوز

التيمم له
#

المصحف لأنه محدث جوزنا له الصلاة للضرورة ولو كان معه مصحف ولم يجد من

يودعه عنده وعجز عن الوضوء جاز له حمله للضرورة قال القاضي أبو الطيب ولا

كان محدثا للضرورة

# واللوح اللذين يقرأ فيهما فيه وجهان مشهوران اصحهما عند الأصحاب لا يجب

للمشقة

- Root: ص-و-ن (ṣ-w-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to preserve, guard, protect from harm or defilement" — implies active custodianship, not mere possession.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, ṣiyānah of the Qur'an denotes protecting its inviolability (ḥurmah) as an act of veneration (taʿẓīm) reflecting the divine origin of the speech.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is physical protection; metaphorical extension applies to safeguarding honor and sanctity, as here with the Mushaf.
- Root: م-س-س (m-s-s)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: "To touch, feel, handle directly with the skin" — implies direct contact, distinguishing it from indirect manipulation.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal-theological context, mass is the physical contact that triggers purity requirements (ṭahārah), tied to the verse {«لَا يَمَسُّهُ إِلَّا الْمُطَهَّرُونَ»} (56:79).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal touch vs. metaphorical "touch" (e.g., affliction); here strictly literal, as the ruling hinges on physical contact.
- Root: ح-م-ل (ḥ-m-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: "To carry, bear, transport" — includes both lifting and conveying, whether directly or via an intermediary.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Carrying the Mushaf is an act of service (khidmah) to the divine word; its prohibition for the impure underscores the need for ritual purity in all forms of engagement.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal carrying; the metaphorical sense of "bearing responsibility" is not operative here, but the physical act is treated with legal rigor.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-Sharṭ wa al-Istithnāʾ) — The text frequently uses "إذا" (idhā) for conditional clauses and "إلا" (illā) for exceptions, requiring precise parsing to distinguish general rulings from specific exemptions (e.g., "لا يحرم مسه إلا على طهارة").
chapters.translation:
I say: The Muslims are unanimously agreed upon the obligation of safeguarding the Mushaf and venerating it. Our companions (the Shāfiʿīs) and others said: If a Muslim were to cast it into a filthy place — and Allah forbid — the one who casts it becomes a disbeliever.

They said: It is unlawful to use it as a pillow; rather, even using individual books of knowledge as pillows is unlawful. It is recommended (mustaḥabb) to stand for the Mushaf when it is brought forward, because standing is recommended for virtuous scholars and righteous people, so the Mushaf is even more deserving. I have established the evidences for the recommendation of standing in the treatise I compiled on this matter. We narrated in the Musnad of al-Dārimī with a sound chain from Ibn Abī Mulaykah that ʿIkrimah ibn Abī Jahl — may Allah be pleased with him — used to place the Mushaf on his face and say: "The Book of my Lord."

[Section] — On the Prohibition of Traveling with the Mushaf and Selling It to a Non-Muslim

Traveling with the Mushaf to the land of the enemy is unlawful if there is fear that it will fall into their hands, due to the well-known hadith in the two Ṣaḥīḥs that the Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — forbade traveling with the Qur'an to the land of the enemy. It is also unlawful to sell the Mushaf to a dhimmī (non-Muslim under Muslim protection). If one sells it, there are two opinions (qawlān) attributed to al-Shāfiʿī regarding the validity of the sale:
1. The more correct of the two is that it is not valid.
2. The second is that it is valid, but the seller is immediately ordered to remove his ownership of it.

The insane person and the child who lacks discernment (tamyīz) are to be prevented from touching the Mushaf, out of fear of violating its sanctity. This prevention is obligatory upon the guardian (walī) and upon anyone else who sees them attempting to handle it.

[Section] — On Touching and Carrying the Mushaf

It is unlawful for the one in a state of minor impurity (muḥdith) to touch the Mushaf or carry it, whether he carries it by its strap or otherwise, and whether he touches the actual script, the margins, or the binding. It is likewise unlawful to touch the case (kharīṭah), the cover (ghilāf), or the box (ṣundūq) if the Mushaf is inside them. This is the chosen school (al-madhhab al-mukhtār). It was said that these three are not unlawful, but this is weak. If the Qur'an is written on a tablet (lawḥ), its ruling is the same as that of the Mushaf, whether the written portion is little or much — even if it is part of a verse written for study, touching the tablet is unlawful.

[Section] — On Turning Its Pages with a Stick

If the one in minor impurity, the junub (one in major impurity), or the menstruating woman turns the pages of the Mushaf with a stick or similar object, there are two faces (wajhān) among our companions:
1. The more apparent of the two is its permissibility, and this is what the Iraqis among our companions definitively held, because he is neither touching nor carrying it.
2. The second is its unlawfulness, because he is deemed to be carrying the page, and the page is like the whole.

As for wrapping his sleeve over his hand and turning the page, this is unlawful without dispute. Some of our companions erred by narrating two faces in this matter; the correct view is the definitive ruling of unlawfulness, because the turning is effected by the hand, not by the sleeve.

[Section] — On the Impure Person Writing the Mushaf

If the junub or the muḥdith writes a Mushaf, and he carries the page or touches it during the writing, it is unlawful. If he does not carry it and does not touch it, there are three faces:
1. The sound (ṣaḥīḥ) view is its permissibility.
2. The second is its unlawfulness.
3. The third is that it is permissible for the muḥdith but unlawful for the junub.

[Section] — On Carrying It Along with Other Things

If the muḥdith, junub, or menstruating woman touches or carries a book of jurisprudence (fiqh) or other sciences that contains verses of the Qur'an, or a garment embroidered with the Qur'an, or dirhams or dīnārs stamped with it, or carries baggage in which a Mushaf is included, or touches a wall, sweetmeat, or bread inscribed with it — the sound school (al-madhhab al-ṣaḥīḥ) is that all of this is permissible, because it is not a Mushaf. There is a face that it is unlawful. The Chief Judge Abū al-Ḥasan al-Māwardī said in his book al-Ḥāwī: "It is permissible to touch garments embroidered with the Qur'an, but it is not permissible to wear them without dispute, because the intent in wearing them is to seek blessing (tabarruk) from the Qur'an." What he mentioned or said is weak; no one has agreed with him on it, as far as I have seen. Rather, Shaykh Abū Muḥammad al-Juwaynī and others explicitly stated the permissibility of wearing them, and this is the correct view. And Allah knows best.

As for books of Qur'anic exegesis (tafsīr), if the Qur'an in them is more than the other content, touching and carrying them is unlawful. If the other content is more — as is usually the case — there are three faces:
1. The most correct is that it is not unlawful.
2. The second is that it is unlawful.
3. The third is that if the Qur'an is written in a distinct script, such as boldness, redness, or otherwise, it is unlawful; if it is not distinct, it is not unlawful.

I say: It is unlawful to touch if the two are equal. The author of al-Tatimmah among our companions said: If we say it is not unlawful, then it is disliked (makrūh).

As for the books of the hadith of the Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — if they contain no verses of the Qur'an, touching them is not unlawful, though it is preferable not to touch them except in a state of purity. If they contain verses of the Qur'an, touching them is not unlawful according to the school, though there is a face that it is unlawful, and this is what is found in the books of jurisprudence. As for what has been abrogated in its recitation (mansūkh al-tilāwah), such as the verse of stoning — "The elderly man and the elderly woman, if they commit adultery, stone them both outright" — and similar cases, touching and carrying it is not unlawful. Our companions said: Likewise for the Torah and the Gospel.

[Section] — On Touching with a Spot of Impurity

If there is on a part of the body of one who is purified a ritual impurity (najāsah) that is not excused, it is unlawful for him to touch the Mushaf with that spot of impurity, without dispute. It is not unlawful with other parts of the body, according to the sound and well-known school held by the majority of our companions and other scholars. Abū al-Qāsim al-Ṣaymarī among our companions said it is unlawful, but our companions refuted him in this. Judge Abū al-Ṭayyib said: What he said is rejected by consensus (ijmāʿ). Then, on the well-known view, some of our companions said it is disliked; the chosen view is that it is not disliked.

[Section] — Subsidiary Rulings (Furūʿ)

For one who finds no water and performs tayammum (dry ablution) where it is permissible, he may touch the Mushaf, whether his tayammum was for prayer or for other purposes for which tayammum is permissible.

As for one who finds neither water nor earth, he prays according to his state, but he is not permitted to touch the Mushaf, because he is in a state of impurity (muḥdith); we permitted him prayer only out of necessity. If he has a Mushaf with him and finds no one to entrust it to, and he is unable to perform ablution, it is permissible for him to carry it out of necessity. Judge Abū al-Ṭayyib said: He is not obligated to perform tayammum. There is consideration (naẓar) in what he said; rather, he should be obligated to perform tayammum. However, if he fears for the Mushaf from burning, drowning, falling into impurity, or falling into the hands of a disbeliever, he may take it even if he is impure, out of necessity.

[Section] — On the Obligation of the Guardian and Teacher to Require Purity from a Discriminating Child

Regarding whether the guardian and teacher are obligated to require the discerning child (ṣabī mumayyiz) to perform purification for carrying the Mushaf and the tablet on which he reads, there are two well-known faces. The more correct of the two among the companions is that it is not obligatory, due to hardship (mashaqqah).

[Section] — On Selling and Buying the Mushaf

The sale and purchase of the Mushaf are valid, and there is no dislike in buying it. Regarding the dislike of selling it, there are two faces among our companions. The more correct of them — and it is the explicit text (naṣṣ) of al-Shāfiʿī — is that it is disliked. Those who said selling and buying it are not disliked include al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, ʿIkrimah, and al-Ḥakam ibn ʿUyaynah, and this is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās. A group of scholars disliked both selling and buying it; Ibn al-Mundhir narrated this from ʿAlqamah, Ibn Sīrīn, al-Nakhaʿī, Shurayḥ, Masrūq, and ʿAbdullāh ibn Zayd. Severity in selling it is narrated from ʿUmar and Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī. Another group held the view of permitting purchase while disliking sale; Ibn al-Mundhir narrated this from Ibn ʿAbbās and Saʿīd ibn [al-Musayyib].

- Root: ض-ب-ط (ḍ-b-ṭ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To bind firmly, to guard precisely, to retain with exactness
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Intellectual mastery and preservation of knowledge against error
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense of physical binding; metaphorical sense of scholarly precision
- Root: ل-غ-ز (l-gh-z) [from "أرمز"]
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To gesture obliquely, to signal cryptically
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Concise allusion conveying meaning without full exposition
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: enigma; here metaphorical: brief indication
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — For listing variant readings (e.g., "بضم الميم وفتحها"), each is syntactically independent but semantically coordinate.
