I say — and God knows best — [this section continues from the preceding discussion of Jubayr, Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, and Isḥāq ibn Rāhawayh].

# Chapter Ten: On the Precise Fixing of the Names and Linguistic Expressions Mentioned in This Book, According to the Order of Their Occurrence

Know that these are numerous, and the complete fixing, clarification, and expansion of them would require a massive volume. However, I shall point to them with the briefest of indications, and gesture toward their intended meanings with the most concise of expressions, restricting myself to the most correct [opinion] in the majority of cases.

The first of that [occurs] in the Khutbah (Introduction):

- **Al-Ḥamd** (الحمد): i.e., praise (al-thanāʾ) with beautiful attributes — [this is] the generous [meaning] concerning the attributes of God Most High, the Bestower of favors. And other [interpretations] have been stated.

- **Al-Mannān** (المنان): We have related from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib (may God honor his face) that its meaning is: the One who begins with bestowal before the asking.

- **Al-Ṭawl** (الطول): Sufficiency and abundance.

- **Al-Hidāyah** (الهداية): Divine enabling (al-tawfīq) and gentleness (al-luṭf). It is said: "He guided us to faith" (hadānā lil-īmān), and "He guided us [in] faith" (hadānā al-īmān), and "He guided us unto faith" (hadānā ilā al-īmān).

- **Sāʾir** (سائر): In the sense of "the remaining" (al-bāqī).

- **Our Prophet Muḥammad** (peace and blessings be upon him) **was so named**: due to the abundance of his praiseworthy traits (al-khiṣāl al-maḥmūdah). Ibn Fāris and others said this — i.e., God Most High inspired his family with that [name] because of what He knew of his beautiful attributes and the nobility of his character. May God increase him in honor and generosity.

- **Taḥaddā** (تحدى): The people of language said: one says "so-and-so taḥaddā so-and-so" when he vies with him and contends with him for victory.

- **His saying "bi-ajmaʿihim"** (بأجمعهم): With ḍammah on the mīm and with fatḥah on it — two well-known variant readings, meaning "all of them."

- **Afḥama** (أفحم): i.e., silenced and overcame.

- **Lā yakhluq** (لا يخلق): With ḍammah on the lām, and fatḥah on it is permissible; the yāʾ in both cases is fatḥah, and ḍammah on it is permissible with kasrah on the lām. One says "khaliqa al-shayʾ" and "akhlaqa" when it becomes worn out. The intended meaning here: its majesty and sweetness do not pass away.

- **Istaẓharahu** (استظهره): He memorized it outwardly (ḥafiẓahu ẓāhirā).

- **Al-Wildān** (الولدان): Young boys (al-ṣibyān).

- **Al-Ḥadathān** (الحدثان): With fatḥah on the ḥāʾ and the dāl — it, along with al-ḥadath, al-ḥādithah, and al-ḥudthā, are all of one meaning: the occurrence of that which was not [previously].

- **Al-Malawān** (الملوان): The night and the day.

- **Al-Riḍwān** (الرضوان): With kasrah on the rāʾ and with ḍammah on it [both permissible].

- **Al-Anām** (الأنام): The creation (al-khalq), according to the preferred opinion; and "al-anīm" is also said.

- **Al-Dāmaghāt** (الدامغات): The breakers, the subjugators (al-qāhirāt).

- **Al-Ṭughām** (الطغام): With fatḥah on the ṭāʾ (unpointed) and the ghayn (pointed) — they are the base rabble of the people (awghād al-nās).

- **Al-Amāthil** (الأماثل): The best ones (al-khiyār); their singular is "amthal." And it is said "mathula al-rajul" (with ḍammah on the thāʾ): he became virtuous and excellent.

- **Al-Aʿlām** (الأعلام): Plural of "ʿalam," which is that by which one is guided on the road — from a mountain or otherwise. The distinguished scholar is called by this [term] because guidance is sought through him.

- **Al-Nuhā** (النهى): The intellects (al-ʿuqūl); their singular is "nuhyah" (with ḍammah on the nūn) — because they restrain (tanhā) their possessor from base deeds. And it is said: because their possessor arrives at (yantahī ilā) his intellect and his opinion.

- **Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī said**: It is permissible that "al-nuhy" be a verbal noun (maṣdar) and that it be a plural — like "al-ghuruf."

- **Dimashq** (دمشق): With kasrah on the dāl and fatḥah on the mīm, according to the well-known [pronunciation]. The author of Maṭāliʿ al-Anwār related kasrah on the mīm as well.

- **Al-Mukhtaṣar** (المختصر): That whose wording is little but whose meanings are many.

- **Al-ʿAtīdah** (العتيدة): The present, the prepared (al-ḥāḍirah al-muʿaddah).

- **Abtahelu** (أبتهل): I humble myself in supplication (ataḍarraʿ).

- **Al-Tawfīq** (التوفيق): The creation of the capacity for obedience (khalq qudrat al-ṭāʿah).

- **Ḥasbunā Allāh** (حسبنا الله): i.e., "Sufficient for us is God" (kāfinā).

- **Al-Wakīl** (الوكيل): The one entrusted with the matter (al-muwakkal ilayhi). And it is said: the one entrusted with the governance of His creation. And it is said: the one who undertakes the welfare of His creation. And it is said: the Protector (al-ḥāfiẓ).

- **Ānāʾ al-Layl** (آناء الليل): The hours of the night. Regarding its singular, there are four variant forms: "anā," "inā" (with kasrah on the hamzah and fatḥah on it), "inī" and "inw" (with yāʾ and wāw, the hamzah kasrah in both).

- **Ālāʾ** (الآلاء): The favors (al-niʿam). Regarding its singular, the four variant forms: "alā," "ilā," "alā," and "alw" — al-Wāḥidī related all of this.

- **Al-Infāq** (الانفاق) **praised in the Sacred Law**: The expenditure of wealth in obedience to God Most High.

- **Tijāratan lan tabūr** (تجارة لن تبور): i.e., a commerce that will not perish nor become corrupt.

- **Al-Safarah** (السفرة): The angels, the scribes, the righteous ones (al-bararah) — plural of "bārr," which is the obedient one.

- **Yataʿtaʿu** (يتتعتع): i.e., it becomes severe and difficult (yashtadd wa yaʿtaṣiru).

- **Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī**: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Qays, attributed to al-Ashʿar, the ancestor of the tribe.

[ ... ]

- **Al-Utrunjah** (الأترجة): With ḍammah on the hamzah and the rāʾ — it is well-known. Al-Jawharī said: Abū Zayd said: "turunjah" is also said. In Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, in the Book of Foods, in this ḥadīth: "like the utrunjah" (al-utrunjah).

- **Abū Umāmah al-Bāhilī**: His name is Ṣudayy ibn ʿAjlān, attributed to Bāhilah, a well-known tribe.

- **Al-Ḥasad** (الحسد): The wishing for the removal of a blessing from another.

- **Al-Ghibṭah** (الغبطة): Like it, but without its removal [being wished].

- **Al-Ḥasad is forbidden** (ḥarām), and **al-ghibṭah in good things is praiseworthy and beloved**. The meaning of his saying (peace and blessings be upon him): "There is no ḥasad except in two [things]" — i.e., there is no praiseworthy ghibṭah whose pursuit is emphasized except in two [cases].

- **Al-Tirmidhī**: Attributed to Tirmidh. Abū Saʿīd al-Samʿānī said: It is an ancient town on the edge of Balkh, at [the river] called Jayḥūn. Regarding the relative attribution to it, one says "Tirmidhī" with kasrah on the tāʾ and the mīm, with ḍammah on both, and with fatḥah on the tāʾ with kasrah on the mīm — three forms, related by al-Samʿānī.

- **Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī**: His name is Saʿd ibn Mālik, attributed to the Banū Khudrah.

- **Abū Dāwūd al-Sijistānī**: His name is Sulaymān ibn al-Ashʿath.

- **Al-Nasāʾī**: He is Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān Aḥmad ibn Shuʿayb.

- **Abū Masʿūd al-Badrī**: His name is ʿUqbah ibn ʿAmr. The majority of scholars said: he resided in Badr but did not witness [the battle]. Al-Zuhrī, al-Bukhārī, and others said: he witnessed it with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him).

- **Al-Dārimī**: He is Abū Muḥammad ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, attributed to Dārim, the ancestor of a tribe.

- **Shaʿāʾir Allāh** (شعائر الله تعالى): The landmarks of His religion (maʿālim dīnihi); their singular is "shaʿīrah." Al-Jawharī said: "shaʿārah" is also said for the singular.

- **Al-Bazzār** (البزار): The author of the Musnad — with rāʾ at its end.

- **Laḥd al-Qabr** (لحد القبر): With fatḥah on the lām and ḍammah on it — two well-known variant readings; the fatḥah is the more eloquent. It is the niche in its qiblī side into which the deceased is placed. One says "laḥadtu al-mayyit" and "alḥadtuhu."

- **Abū Hurayrah**: His name is ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ṣakhr, according to the most correct of roughly thirty opinions. He was nicknamed with "Hurayrah" — a kitten he had in his childhood — and he was the first to be nicknamed by this.

- **Ādhananī bil-ḥarb** (آذنني بالحرب): He informed me [of war] (aʿlamanī); its meaning: he manifested his warfare against me.

- **Abū Ḥanīfah**: al-Nuʿmān ibn Thābit ibn Zūṭī.

- **Al-Imām al-Shāfiʿī**: Abū ʿAbd Allāh Muḥammad ibn Idrīs ibn al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿUthmān ibn Shāfiʿ ibn al-Sāʾib ibn ʿUbayd ibn ʿAbd Yazīd ibn Hāshim ibn al-Muṭṭalib ibn ʿAbd Manāf ibn Quṣayy.

- **Al-Thalb** (الثلب): With fatḥah on the thāʾ (with three dots) and sukūn on the lām — it is the fault/defect (al-ʿayb).

- **Ḥunafāʾ** (حنفاء): Plural of "ḥanīf," which is the upright one (al-mustaqīm). And it is said: the one inclined to the truth, turning away from falsehood.

- **Al-Marʿashī** (المرعشي): With fatḥah on the mīm, sukūn on the rāʾ, and fatḥah on the ʿayn (unpointed).

- **Al-Tustarī** (التستري): With ḍammah on the first tāʾ, fatḥah on the second, and sukūn on the sīn (unpointed) — attributed to Tustar, the well-known city.

- **Al-Imām al-Muḥāsibī** (المحاسبي): With ḍammah on the mīm. Al-Samʿānī said: He was called this because he used to hold himself to account (yuḥāsib) [in his soul].

chapters.title_en: Section 27 — Clarification of Unfamiliar Terms and Proper Names in the Chapter on Etiquette with the Quran
chapters.arabic_text:
نفسه وهو ممن جمع له علم الظاهر والباطن
# * عرف الجنة بفتح العين وإسكان الراء وبالفاء ريحها
# * فليتبوا مقعده من النار أي فلينزله وقيل فليتخذه وقيل هو دعاء وقيل خبر
# * الدلالة بفتح الدال وكسرها ويقال دلولة عنه بضم الدال واللام
# * الطوية بفتح الطاء وكسر الواو قال أهل اللغة هي الضمير
# * التراقي جمع ترقوة وهو العظم الذي بين نقرة النحر والعاتق
# 
# * يجلسون حلقا يقال بفتح الحاء وكسرها  لغتان
# * ابن ماجه هو أبو عبد الله بن محمد بن يزيد
# * أبو الدرداء اسمه عويمر وقيل عامر
# 
# * يحنو على الطالب أي يعطف عليه ويشفق
# * أيوب السختياني بفتح السين وكسر التاء قال أبو عمر بن عبد البر كان

أيوب يبيع الجلود بالبصرة ولهذا قيل السختياني
# 
# [ ... ]
# 
# * البراعة مصدر برع الرجل وبرع بفتح الراء وضمها إذا فاق أصحابه
# * حلقة العلم ونحوها باسكان اللام هذه هي اللغة الفصيحة المشهورة ويقال

بفتحها في لغة قليلة حكاها ثعلب والجوهري وغيرهما
# * الرفعة بضم الراء وكسرها لغتان
# * قعدة المتعلمين بكسر القاف
# * المعشر الجماعة الذين أمرهم واحد
# * قوله ويتفقدونها بالنهار أي يعملون بما فيها
# * أبو سليمان الخطابي منسوب إلى جد من إجداده اسمه الخطاب واسم ابي

سليمان محمد بن محمد بن ابراهيم بن الخطاب وقيل اسمه أحمد
# * الزهري هو أبو بكر محمد بن مسلم بن عبيد الله بن عبد الله بن شهاب بن

عبد الله بن الحارث بن زهرة بن كلاب بن مرة بن كعب
# * البصري بفتح الباء وكسرها
# * الشعبي بفتح الشين اسمه عامر بن شراحيل بفتح الشين
# 
# * تميم الداري منسوب إلى دارين موضع بالساحل ويقال تميم الديري نسبة إلى

دير كان يتعبد فيه وقيل غير ذلك وقد أوضحت الخلاف فيه في أول شرح صحيح مسلم
# * سليم بن عترة بكسر العين المهملة وإسكان التاء المثناة فوق
# * الدورقي بدال مهملة مفتوحة ثم واو ساكنة ثم راء مفتوحة ثم قاف ثم ياء

النسب قيل إنها نسبة إلى القلانس الطوال التي تسمى الدورقية وقيل كان أبونا

ناسكا أي عابدأ وكان في ذلك الزمن يسمون الناسك دورقيا وقيل نسبة الى دورق

بلدة بفارس أو غيرها
# * منصور بن زاذان بالزاي والذال المعجمة
# * قوله يحتبي أي ينصب ساقيه ويحتوي على ملتقى ساقيه وفخذيه بيديه أو بثوب

والحبوة بضم الحاء وكسرها لغتان هي ذلك الفعل
# * الهذرمة بالذال المعجمة سرعة الكلام الخفي
# * الغزالي هو محمد بن محمد بن محمد بن أحمد وهكذا يقال بتشديد الزاي وقد

روي عنه أنه أنكر هذا وقال إنما أنا الغزالي بتخفيف الزاي  منسوب إلى قرية

من قرى طوس يقال لها غزالة
# 
# * طلحة بن مصرف بضم الميم وفتح الصاد وكسر الراء وقيل يجوز فتح الراء

وليس بشئ
# * أبو الأحوص بالحاء والصاد المهملتين واسمه عوف بن مالك الجشمي بضم

الجيم وفتح الشين المعجمة منسوب إلى جشم جد القبيلة
# * الفسطاط فيه ست لغات فستاط بالتاء بدل الطاء وفساط بتشديد السين والفاء

فيهن مضمومة ومكسورة والمراد به الخيمة والمنزل
# * الدوي بفتح الدال وكسر الواو وتشديد الياء صوت لا يفهم
# * النخعي بفتح النون والخاء منسوب الى النخعي جد قبيلة
# * حلب شاة بفتح اللام ويجوز اسكانها في لغة قليلة
# * الرقاشي بفتح الراء وتخفيف القاف
# * القذاة كالعود وفتات الخرق ونحوها مما يكنس المسجد منه
# * سليمان بن يسار بالمثناة ثم السين المهملة
# 
# * أبو أسيد بضم الهمزة وفتح السين اسمه مالك بن ربيعة شهد بدرا
# * تنطحني بكسر الطاء وفتحها
# * منتشر جدا بكسر الجيم وهو مصدر
# * الأشنان بضم الهمزة وكسرها لغتان ذكرهما أبو عبيدة وهمزة أشنان: أصلية.
# * وابن الجواليقي هو فارسي معرب وهو بالعربية المحضة حرض
# * كراسي أضراسه يجوز فيه التشديد والتخفيف
# * والروياني بضم الراء وإسكان الواو منسوب إلى رويان
# * قوله على حسب حاله هو بفتح السين اي على قدر طاقته
# * الحمام معروف وهو مذكر عند أهل اللغة
# 
# * الحشوش مواضع العذرة والبول المتخذة له واحدها حش بفتح الحاء وضمها

لغتان
# * حجر الانسان بفتح الحاء وكسرها
# * الجنازة بكسر الجيم وفتحها من جنز إذا ستر
# * بهز بن حكيم هو بفتح الباء واسكان الهاء وبالزاي
# * زرارة بضم الزاي
# * أحمد بن أبي الحواري بفتح الحاء وكسر الراء ومنهم من يفتح الراء وكان

شيخنا أبو البقاء خالد النابلسي رحمه الله يحكيه وربما اختاره وكان علامة

وقته في هذا الفن مع كمال تحقيقة فيه واسم أبي
# * الحواري عبد الله بن ميمون بن عباس بن الحرث
# * الجرعي بضم الجيم والراء
# * أبو الجوزاء بفتح الجيم وبالزاي اسمه أوس بن عبد الله وقيل أوس بن خالد
# * حبتر بحاء مهملة مفتوحة ثم باء موحدة ساكنة ثم تاء مثناة من فوق مفتوحة

ثم  راء الرجل الصالح هو القائم بحقوق الله تعالى وحقوق العباد كذا قاله

الزجاج وصاحب المطالع وغيرهما
# 
# * أبو ذر اسمه جندب وقيل برير بضم الموحدة وتكرير الراء
# * اجترحوا السيئات اكتسبوها
# * العار بكسر الشين العلامة
# 
# * الشراك بكسر الشين هو السير الرقيق الذي يكون في النعل ظهر القدم
# * أم سلمة اسمها هند وقيل رملة وليس بشئ
# * عبد الله بن مغفل بضم الميم وفتح الغين المعجمة والفاء
# 
# * اللغط بفتح الغين وإسكانها لغتان هو اختلاط الأصوات
# * المعوذتان بكسر الواو
# * الأوزاعي اسمه عبد الرحمن بن عمر إمام الشام في عصره منسوب الى موضع
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع ر ف (ʿarafa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Knowledge and perception; the core sense is the recognition of a thing by its trace or scent.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, ʿirfān denotes experiential or intuitive knowledge, distinct from mere transmitted report.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: to know; metaphorical: to perceive by scent, as in the fragrance of Paradise.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Vocalization Variants (Lughāt) — When multiple vowellings are cited for a single word, each is a legitimate dialectal or tribal pronunciation, and the translator must preserve the author's enumeration without preferring one over the other.
chapters.translation:
I say: And he is one for whom both the outward and inward sciences have been gathered.

- "ʿArf al-Jannah" (عرف الجنة) — with the opening of the ʿayn (fatḥah) and the stillness of the rāʾ, and with the fāʾ — means its fragrance.

- "Falyatabawwaʾ maqʿadahu min al-Nār" (فليتبوا مقعده من النار) — meaning let him take it as his abode. And it was said: let him adopt it. And it was said: it is a supplication. And it was said: it is an informative statement.

- "Al-Dilālah" (الدلالة) — with the opening of the dāl and its kasrah. And it is said: "dalwalah" (دلولة) with the ḍammah of the dāl and the lām.

- "Al-Ṭawiyyah" (الطوية) — with the opening of the ṭāʾ and the kasrah of the wāw. The people of language said: it is the inner conscience (al-ḍamīr).

- "Al-Tarāqī" (التراقي) — the plural of "turquwwah" (ترقوة), which is the bone between the hollow of the collarbone (naḥr) and the shoulder (ʿātiq).

- "Yajlisūna ḥilaqan" (يجلسون حلقا) — it is said with the opening of the ḥāʾ and its kasrah; these are two dialects.

- "Ibn Mājah" (ابن ماجه) — he is Abū ʿAbd Allāh Muḥammad ibn Yazīd.

- "Abū al-Dardāʾ" (أبو الدرداء) — his name is ʿUwaymir, and it was said: ʿĀmir.

- "Yaḥnū ʿalā al-ṭālib" (يحنو على الطالب) — meaning he inclines toward him with compassion and shows him tenderness.

- "Ayyūb al-Sakhtiyānī" (أيوب السختياني) — with the opening of the sīn and the kasrah of the tāʾ. Abū ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-Barr said: Ayyūb used to sell leather in Baṣrah, and for this reason he was called al-Sakhtiyānī.

[ ... ]

- "Al-Barāʿah" (البراعة) — the verbal noun of "baraʿa al-rajul" (برع الرجل) and "bariʿa" (برع) — with the opening of the rāʾ and its ḍammah — when he surpasses his companions.

- "Ḥalqat al-ʿilm" (حلقة العلم) and the like — with the sukūn of the lām; this is the eloquent and well-known dialect. And it is said with its fatḥah in a rare dialect, narrated by Thaʿlab, al-Jawharī, and others.

- "Al-Rifʿah" (الرفعة) — with the ḍammah of the rāʾ and its kasrah; two dialects.

- "Qiʿdat al-mutaʿallimīn" (قعدة المتعلمين) — with the kasrah of the qāf.

- "Al-Maʿshar" (المعشر) — the group of people whose affair is one.

- His saying: "Wa yatafaqqadūnahā bil-nahār" (ويتفقدونها بالنهار) — meaning they act upon what is in it.

- "Abū Sulaymān al-Khaṭṭābī" (أبو سليمان الخطابي) — attributed to one of his forefathers whose name was al-Khaṭṭāb. The name of Abū Sulaymān is Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, and it was said: his name is Aḥmad.

- "Al-Zuhrī" (الزهري) — he is Abū Bakr Muḥammad ibn Muslim ibn ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shihāb ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Zuhrah ibn Kilāb ibn Murrah ibn Kaʿb.

- "Al-Baṣrī" (البصري) — with the opening of the bāʾ and its kasrah.

- "Al-Shaʿbī" (الشعبي) — with the opening of the shīn. His name is ʿĀmir ibn Sharāḥīl — with the opening of the shīn.

- "Tamīm al-Dārī" (تميم الداري) — attributed to Dārīn, a place on the coast. And it is said: Tamīm al-Dayrī, attributed to a monastery (dayr) in which he used to worship. And it was said: other than that. I have already clarified the disagreement concerning it at the beginning of my commentary on Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim.

- "Sulaym ibn ʿItrah" (سليم بن عترة) — with the kasrah of the unpointed ʿayn and the sukūn of the tāʾ with two points above.

- "Al-Dūraqī" (الدورقي) — with an unpointed dāl, opened, then a wāw, still, then a rāʾ, opened, then a qāf, then the yāʾ of attribution. It was said: it is an attribution to the tall conical caps (qalānis) called "Dūra qiyyah." And it was said: our father was a devotee (nāsik), i.e., a worshiper, and in that era the devotees were called "Dūraqī." And it was said: it is an attribution to Dūraq, a town in Persia, or other than it.

- "Manṣūr ibn Zādān" (منصور بن زاذان) — with the zāy and the pointed dhāl.

- His saying: "Yaḥtabī" (يحتبي) — meaning he erects his two shins and wraps his arms or a garment around the meeting point of his shins and thighs. "Al-ḥubwah" (الحبوة) — with the ḍammah of the ḥāʾ and its kasrah; two dialects — is that very act.

- "Al-Hadharamah" (الهذرمة) — with the pointed dhāl — is the rapidity of speech that is indistinct.

- "Al-Ghazālī" (الغزالي) — he is Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad. Thus it is said with the tashdīd of the zāy. And it has been narrated from him that he denied this and said: "I am only al-Ghazālī with the takhfīf of the zāy, attributed to a village among the villages of Ṭūs called Ghazālah."

- "Ṭalḥah ibn Muṣarrif" (طلحة بن مصرف) — with the ḍammah of the mīm, the fatḥah of the ṣād, and the kasrah of the rāʾ. And it was said: the opening of the rāʾ is permissible, but it is nothing.

- "Abū al-Aḥwaṣ" (أبو الأحوص) — with the unpointed ḥāʾ and the unpointed ṣād. His name is ʿAwf ibn Mālik al-Jushamī — with the ḍammah of the jīm and the fatḥah of the pointed shīn — attributed to Jusham, the forefather of the tribe.

- "Al-Fusṭāṭ" (الفسطاط) — it has six dialects: "fisṭāṭ" (فسطاط) with tāʾ instead of ṭāʾ, and "fasṣāṭ" (فساط) with the tashdīd of the sīn. The fāʾ in all of them is with ḍammah and kasrah. The intended meaning is the tent and the dwelling.

- "Al-Dawī" (الدوي) — with the fatḥah of the dāl, the kasrah of the wāw, and the tashdīd of the yāʾ — is a sound that is not understood.

- "Al-Nakhaʿī" (النخعي) — with the fatḥah of the nūn and the khāʾ — attributed to Nakhaʿ, the forefather of a tribe.

- "Ḥalaba shātan" (حلب شاة) — with the fatḥah of the lām, and its sukūn is permissible in a rare dialect.

- "Al-Riqāshī" (الرقاشي) — with the fatḥah of the rāʾ and the takhfīf of the qāf.

- "Al-Qadhāh" (القذاة) — like the stick, the fragment of a garment, and similar things with which the mosque is swept clean.

- "Sulaymān ibn Yasār" (سليمان بن يسار) — with the mathnāh (tāʾ) then the unpointed sīn.

- "Abū Usayd" (أبو أسيد) — with the ḍammah of the hamzah and the fatḥah of the sīn. His name is Mālik ibn Rabīʿah. He witnessed Badr.

- "Tanṭaḥunī" (تنطحني) — with the kasrah of the ṭāʾ and its fatḥah.

- "Muntashir jiddan" (منتشر جدا) — with the kasrah of the jīm, and it is a verbal noun.

- "Al-Ushnān" (الأشنان) — with the ḍammah of the hamzah and its kasrah; two dialects, mentioned by Abū ʿUbaydah. The hamzah of "ushnān" is original. And Ibn al-Jawālīqī said: it is a Persian word arabicized, and in pure Arabic it is "ḥuraḍ" (حرض).

- "Karāsī aḍrāsihi" (كراسي أضراسه) — both tashdīd and takhfīf are permissible in it.

- "Al-Rūyānī" (الروياني) — with the ḍammah of the rāʾ and the sukūn of the wāw — attributed to Rūyān.

- His saying: "ʿAlā ḥasbi ḥālihi" (على حسب حاله) — it is with the fatḥah of the sīn, meaning according to the measure of his capacity.

- "Al-Ḥammām" (الحمام) — well known, and it is masculine according to the people of language.

- "Al-Ḥushūsh" (الحشوش) — the places of filth and urine prepared for that purpose; its singular is "ḥashsh" (حش) — with the fatḥah of the ḥāʾ and its ḍammah; two dialects.

- "Ḥajar al-insān" (حجر الانسان) — with the fatḥah of the ḥāʾ and its kasrah.

- "Al-Janāzah" (الجنازة) — with the kasrah of the jīm and its fatḥah, from "janaza" (جنز), meaning to cover.

- "Bahz ibn Ḥakīm" (بهز بن حكيم) — with the fatḥah of the bāʾ, the sukūn of the hāʾ, and with the zāy.

- "Zurārah" (زرارة) — with the ḍammah of the zāy.

- "Aḥmad ibn Abī al-Ḥawārī" (أحمد بن أبي الحواري) — with the fatḥah of the ḥāʾ and the kasrah of the rāʾ. And among them is one who opens the rāʾ. Our teacher Abū al-Baqāʾ Khālid al-Nābulusī, may God have mercy on him, used to narrate it and perhaps preferred it; he was the foremost scholar of his time in this art, with complete mastery in it. The name of Abū al-Ḥawārī is ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maymūn ibn ʿAbbās ibn al-Ḥārith.

- "Al-Jurʿī" (الجرعي) — with the ḍammah of the jīm and the rāʾ.

- "Abū al-Jawzāʾ" (أبو الجوزاء) — with the fatḥah of the jīm and with the zāy. His name is Aws ibn ʿAbd Allāh, and it was said: Aws ibn Khālid.

- "Ḥabtar" (حبتر) — with an unpointed ḥāʾ, opened, then a single bāʾ, still, then a tāʾ with two points above, opened, then a rāʾ. The righteous man (al-rajul al-ṣāliḥ) is the one who upholds the rights of God, may He be exalted, and the rights of the servants. Thus said al-Zajjāj, the author of al-Maṭāliʿ, and others.

- "Abū Dharr" (أبو ذر) — his name is Jundab, and it was said: Burayr — with the ḍammah of the bāʾ and the repetition of the rāʾ.

- "Ijtaraḥū al-sayyiʾāt" (اجترحوا السيئات) — they earned them.

- "Al-ʿār" (العار) — with the kasrah of the shīn — is the mark.

- "Al-Shirāk" (الشراك) — with the kasrah of the shīn — is the thin strap that is on the instep of the foot in the sandal.

- "Umm Salamah" (أم سلمة) — her name is Hind, and it was said: Ramlah, but that is nothing.

- "ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mughaffal" (عبد الله بن مغفل) — with the ḍammah of the mīm, the fatḥah of the pointed ghayn, and the fāʾ.

- "Al-Laghṭ" (اللغط) — with the fatḥah of the ghayn and its sukūn; two dialects — is the mixing of voices.

- "Al-Muʿawwidhatān" (المعوذتان) — with the kasrah of the wāw.

- "Al-Awzāʿī" (الأوزاعي) — his name is ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAmr, the Imām of Syria in his era, attributed to a place.

chapters.title_en: Section 28 — Clarification of Problematic Words and Concluding Supplications
chapters.arabic_text: بباب الفراديس من دمشق يقال له الأوزاع وقيل إلى قبيلة وقيل غير ذلك # * عرزب بعين مهملة مفتوحة ثم راء ساكنة ثم زاي مفتوحة ثم باء موحدة # * بريدة بن الحصيب بضم الحاء وفتح الصاد المهملتين # * فضالة بفتح الفاء # # * لله أشد أذنا بفتح الهمزة والذال أي استماعا # * القينة بفتح القاف المغنية # * طوبى أي خير لهم كذا قاله أهل اللغة # * الأعمش سليمان بن مهران # * أبو العالية بالعين المهملة اسمه رفيع بضم الراء # * أبو لبابة الصحابي بضم اللام اسمه بشير وقيل رفاعة بن عبد المنذر # * الغشمة الظلمة # * قوله عيناه تذرفان أي ينصب دمعهما وهو بفتح التاء المثناة من فوق وكسر الراء # * فما خطبكم أي شأنكم # * الأيام المعدودات أيام التشريق الثلاثة بعد يوم النحر # # تشميت العاطس هو بالشين وبالسين القفال المذكور هنا المروزي عبد الله بن أحمد يقرن بضم الراء على اللغة الفصيحة وفي لغة بكسرها # * البغوي منسوب الى بغ مدينة بين هراة ومرو ويقال لها أيضا بغشور واسمه الحسين بن مسعود # * الآصال جمع أصيل وهو آخر النهار وقيل ما بين العصر وغروب الشمس # * زبيد بن الحرث بضم الزاي وبعدها موحدة مفتوحة # * سبوح قدوس بضم أولهما وبالفتح لغتان مشهورتان # * أبو قلابة بكسر القاف وفتح اللام وتخفيفها وبالياء الموحدة اسمة عبد الله بن زيد # # * يحيى بن وثاب بثاء مثلثة مشددة # * معان بن رفاعة بضم الميم والعين وآخره نون # * الشخير بكسر الشين والخاء مشددة # * الحكم بن عتيبة هو بتاء مثناة من فوق ثم مثناة من تحت ثم موحدة # * المحيى والممات الحياة والموت # * أوزعهم إلا ألههم # * حمدأ يوافي نعمة اي يصل إليها فيحصلها # * ويكافئ مزيده هو بهمزة آخر يكافئ ومعناه يقوم بشكر ما زادنا من النعم # * مجالد الراوي عن الشعبي بالجيم وكسر اللام # * الصيمري بفتح الصاد المهملة والميم وقيل بضم الميم وهو غريب # # وقد بسطت بيانه في تهذيب الأسماء واللغات فهذه أحرف وجيزة في ضبط مشكل ما وقع في هذا الكتاب وما بقي منها تركته لظهوره وما ذكرته من الظاهر قصدت بيانه لمن لا يخالط العلماء، فإنه ينتفع به إن شاء الله تعالى. # * * * # هذا آخر ما تيسر مهه هذا الكتاب، وهو نبذة مختصرة بالنسبة إلى آداب القراء. # ولكن حملني على اختصاره ما ذكرته في أول الكتاب. # وأنا أسأل الله العظيم أن ينفع به النفع العميم، لي ولأحبابي، وكل ناظر فيه وسائر المسلمين في الدارين. # والحمد الله رب العالمين حمدا يوافي نعمه ويكافي مزيده، وصلاته وسلامه الأكملان على سيدنا محمد، وعلى آل محمد، وأصحابه أجمعين والحمد الله رب العالمين. # اه. إلى هنا تم كتاب التبيان. # | الفوائد المزيدة على الكتاب | | لطيفة # # قال ابن الجوزي في كتاب " مناقب الامام أحمد بن حنبل " ص 434 في الباب الحادي والتسعين في ذكر المنامات التي رآها أحمد بن حنبل رضي الله تعالى عنه: أخبرنا عبد الملك بن أبي القاسم، قال: أنا عبد الله بن محمد الانصاري، قال: أنا محمد بن عبد الجليل بن أحمد، قال: أنا محمد بن أحمد بن إبراهيم، وأخبرنا ابن ناصر، قال: أنبأنا أبو علي الحسن بن أحمد، قال: أنا أبو محمد الخلال، قال: أنا عبيد الله بن عبد الرحمن الزهري، قالا: حدثنا أحمد بن محمد بن معثم، قال: سمعت عبد العزيز بن أحمد النهاوندي قال: سمعت عبد الله بن أحمد بن حنبل قال: سمعت أبي يقول: * رأيت رب العزة في المنام فقلت: يا رب ما أفضل ما تقرب به المتقربون إليك؟ * فقال: كلامي يا أحمد # * قال فقلت: يا رب بفهم أو بغير فهم؟ # # * قال: بفهم وبغير فهم. اه. # أنظر مناقب الامام أحمد، مطبعة دار الافاق الجديدة ط الثانية 1977 م. | | لطيفة # # عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أنه قال: ثمان أيات نزلت في سورة النساء خير لهذه الامة مما طلعت عليه الشمس: # * 1 -: (يريد الله ليبين لكم ويهديكم سنن الذين من قبلكم ويتوب عليكم) . # * 2 -: (والله يريد أن يتوب عليكم ويريد الذين يتبعون الشهوات أن تميلوا ميلا عظيما) . # ، 3 -: (يريد الله أن يخفف عنكم وخلق الانسان ضعيفا) . # * 4 -: (إن تجتنبوا كبائر ما تنهون عنه نكفر عنكم سيئاتكم وندخلكم مدخلا كريما) . # * 5 -: (إن الله لا يظلم مثقال ذرة وإن تك حسنة يضاعفها ويؤت من لدنه أجرا عظيما) . # * 6 -: (ومن يعمل سوءا أو يظلم نفسه ثم يستغفر الله يجد الله غفورا رحيما) . # * 7 -: (إن الله لا يغفر أن يشرك به ويغفر ما دون ذلك لمن يشاء) . # * 8 -: (والذين ءامنوا بالله ورسله، ولم يفرقوا بين أحد منهم # # أولئك سوف يؤتيهم أجورهم وكان الله غفورا رحيما) . # اه الاتقان 2 / 206 | لطيفة # * 1 -: إن أعظم آية في القرآن، (الله لا إله إلا هو الحي القيوم) . # * 2 -: وأعدل آية في القرآن، (إن الله يأمر بالعدل والاحسان وإيتائ ذى القربى) الاية ... * 3 -: وأخوف آية في القرآن، (فمن يعمل مثقال ذرة خيرا يره (7) ومن يعمل مثقال ذرة شرا يره) . # * 4 -: وأرجي آية في القرآن، (قل يعبادي الذين أسرفوا على أنفسهم لا تقنطوا من رحمة الله) الاية ... وقيل: (ولسوف يعطيك ربك فترضى) . # * 5 -: وأحزن آية في القرآن، (من يعمل سوءا يجزيه) . # * 6 -: وأشد آية في القرآن، - أي على أهل النار - (فذوقوا فلن نزيد كم إلا عذابا) . # * 7 -: وعن علي كرم الله وجهه: أحب آية إلى في القرآن، (إن الله لا يغفرأن يشرك به ويغفر ما دون ذلك لمن يشاء) . # * 8 -: وأفضل آية في القرآن، (وما أصابكم من مصيبة فبما كسبت أيديكم ويعفوا عن كثير) . # اه الاتقان 2 / 205 #
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-ر-ز-ب (ʿ-r-z-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A proper noun (place name); the diacritical marks are given for correct vocalization.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Not a theological term; purely lexical identification.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal designation of a location; no metaphorical extension.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Vocalization (Ḍabṭ) — precise vowel marking to prevent misreading in transmission.
chapters.translation:
I say: [The place] at the gate of the Firdaws quarter of Damascus is called al-Awzāʿ; it is also said [it is named] after a tribe, and other opinions exist.

- ʿArzab: with an unpointed ʿayn (fathah), then a silent rāʾ, then an open zāy, then a single bāʾ.
- Buraydah ibn al-Ḥuṣayb: with ḍammah on the ḥāʾ and fathah on the ṣād (both unpointed).
- Fuḍālah: with fathah on the fāʾ.

- "Allah is more attentive in hearing" (ashaddu udhunan): with fathah on the hamzah and dhāl, meaning "more [intense] in listening."
- Al-Qaynah: with fathah on the qāf — the singing girl.
- Ṭūbā: meaning "goodness for them" — thus said the lexicographers.
- Al-Aʿmash: Sulaymān ibn Mihrān.
- Abū al-ʿĀliyah: with unpointed ʿayn; his name is Rufayʿ, with ḍammah on the rāʾ.
- Abū Lubābah the Companion: with ḍammah on the lām; his name is Bashīr, and it is said Rifāʿah ibn ʿAbd al-Mundhir.
- Al-Ghashmah: darkness.
- His saying {«ʿaynāhu tadhrifān»} — i.e., his tears flow; it is with fathah on the tāʾ (the second letter from above) and kasrah on the rāʾ.
- "What is your affair?" (fa-mā khaṭbukum): i.e., what is your matter.
- "The numbered days" (al-ayyām al-maʿdūdāt): the three days of Tashrīq following the Day of Sacrifice.

- "Tashmīt al-ʿāṭis" (blessing the sneezer): it is with shīn and with sīn. Al-Qaffāl mentioned here is al-Marwazī, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad, with ḍammah on the rāʾ in the eloquent language, and in another dialect with kasrah.
- Al-Baghawī: attributed to Bagh, a city between Herat and Marw, also called Baghshūr; his name is al-Ḥusayn ibn Masʿūd.
- Al-Āṣāl: plural of aṣīl, which is the end of the day; it is also said [it is] the period between ʿAṣr and sunset.
- Zubayd ibn al-Ḥārith: with ḍammah on the zāy, followed by an open bāʾ.
- Subbūḥ Quddūs: with ḍammah on the first letter of each; with fathah [on the first letter] are two well-known variant readings.
- Abū Qilābah: with kasrah on the qāf, fathah on the lām, and its lightening; with a final yāʾ (single letter); his name is ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zayd.

- Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb: with a shaddah on the thāʾ (a three-pointed letter).
- Muʿān ibn Rifāʿah: with ḍammah on the mīm and ʿayn, and its final letter is nūn.
- Al-Shakhīr: with kasrah on the shīn and shaddah on the khāʾ.
- Al-Ḥakam ibn ʿUtaybah: it is with a tāʾ (two points from above), then a tāʾ (two points from below), then a single bāʾ.
- Al-Muḥyī and al-Mumāt: life and death.
- "Awziʿhum" — i.e., "make them incline" (alihhum).
- "Ḥamdan yuwāfī niʿamah": i.e., [praise] that reaches His blessings and obtains them.
- "Wa-yukāfiʾ mazīdah": it is with a hamzah at the end — yukāfiʾ — meaning: he undertakes to thank what He has increased upon us of blessings.
- Mujālid, the narrator from al-Shaʿbī: with jīm and kasrah on the lām.
- Al-Ṣaymarī: with fathah on the unpointed ṣād and the mīm; it is also said with ḍammah on the mīm, and this is uncommon.

I have expanded its explanation in Tahdhīb al-Asmāʾ wa al-Lughāt. These are brief notes on the problematic [words] occurring in this book; what remains of them I have left due to its obviousness. What I have mentioned of the apparent [meanings], I intended to clarify for one who does not mix with scholars, for he will benefit from it, if Allah the Exalted wills.

* * *

This is the end of what has been facilitated of this book — a concise excerpt relative to the etiquette of Qurʾān reciters. But what compelled me to abbreviate it is what I mentioned at the beginning of the book. I ask Allah the Magnificent to grant benefit through it — abundant benefit — for me, for my beloved ones, for every reader of it, and for the rest of the Muslims in both abodes. And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds — praise that reaches His blessings and compensates His increase — and His most complete prayers and peace be upon our master Muḥammad, upon the family of Muḥammad, and upon all his Companions. And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds. End. Here concludes the book al-Tibyān.

---

ADDITIONAL BENEFITS APPENDED TO THE BOOK

---

A Subtle Point:
Ibn al-Jawzī said in his book "Manāqib al-Imām Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal" (p. 434), in the ninety-first chapter, concerning the dreams seen by Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal (may Allah be pleased with him): ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Abī al-Qāsim informed us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad al-Anṣārī told us, saying: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jalīl ibn Aḥmad told us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Ibrāhīm told us — and Ibn Nāṣir informed us, saying: Abū ʿAlī al-Ḥasan ibn Aḥmad told us, saying: Abū Muḥammad al-Khallāl told us, saying: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Zuhrī told us — they both said: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Maʿtham narrated to us, saying: I heard ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Aḥmad al-Nahāwandī say: I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal say: I heard my father say: *I saw the Lord of Might in a dream, and I said: "O Lord, what is the most excellent thing by which those who draw near draw near to You?"* He said: *"My speech, O Aḥmad."* He said: I said: "O Lord, with understanding or without understanding?" He said: *"With understanding and without understanding."* End. See Manāqib al-Imām Aḥmad, Dār al-Āfāq al-Jadīdah Press, 2nd ed., 1977 CE.

---

A Subtle Point:
From Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them both) that he said: Eight verses revealed in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ are better for this ummah than what the sun has risen upon:
1. {«Yurīdu Allāhu li-yubayyina lakum wa-yahdiyakum sunana alladhīna min qablikum wa-yatūba ʿalaykum»} (Allah desires to make clear to you and guide you to the ways of those before you and to turn to you in mercy).
2. {«Wa-Allāhu yurīdu an yatūba ʿalaykum wa-yurīdu alladhīna yattabiʿūna al-shahawāti an tamīlū maylan ʿaẓīmā»} (And Allah desires to turn to you in mercy, but those who follow lusts desire that you deviate with great deviation).
3. {«Yurīdu Allāhu an yukhaffifa ʿankum wa-khuliqa al-insānu ḍaʿīfā»} (Allah desires to lighten [burdens] for you, and man was created weak).
4. {«In tajtanibū kabāʾira mā tunhawna ʿanhu nukaffir ʿankum sayyiʾātikum wa-nudkhilkum mudkhalan karīmā»} (If you avoid the major sins which you are forbidden, We will expiate from you your misdeeds and admit you to a noble entrance).
5. {«Inna Allāha lā yaẓlimu mithqāla dharratin wa-in taku ḥasanatan yuḍāʿifhā wa-yuʾti min ladunhu ajran ʿaẓīmā»} (Indeed, Allah does not wrong [anyone] even the weight of an atom; and if there is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward).
6. {«Wa-man yaʿmal sūʾan aw yaẓlim nafsahu thumma yastaghfiri Allāha yajidi Allāha ghafūran raḥīmā»} (And whoever does evil or wrongs himself, then seeks forgiveness from Allah, will find Allah Forgiving, Merciful).
7. {«Inna Allāha lā yaghfiru an yushraka bihi wa-yaghfiru mā dūna dhālika li-man yashāʾ»} (Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills).
8. {«Wa-alladhīna āmanū bi-Allāhi wa-rusulihi wa-lam yufarriqū bayna aḥadin minhum ulāʾika sawfa yuʾtīhim ujūrahum wa-kāna Allāhu ghafūran raḥīmā»} (And those who believe in Allah and His messengers and do not differentiate between any of them — those He will give their rewards, and Allah is Forgiving, Merciful).
End. [From] al-Itqān 2/206.

---

A Subtle Point:
1. The greatest verse in the Qurʾān: {«Allāhu lā ilāha illā huwa al-ḥayyu al-qayyūm»} (Allah — there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining).
2. The most just verse in the Qurʾān: {«Inna Allāha yaʾmuru bi-al-ʿadli wa-al-iḥsāni wa-ītāʾi dhī al-qurbā»} (Indeed, Allah commands justice, excellence, and giving to near relatives) — the verse.
3. The most fear-inducing verse in the Qurʾān: {«Fa-man yaʿmal mithqāla dharratin khayran yarah (7) wa-man yaʿmal mithqāla dharratin sharran yarah»} (So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it).
4. The most hope-inspiring verse in the Qurʾān: {«Qul yā ʿibādi alladhīna asrafū ʿalā anfusihim lā taqnaṭū min raḥmati Allāh»} (Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah) — the verse. And it is said: {«Wa-la-sawfa yuʿṭīka rabbuka fa-tarḍā»} (And your Lord is going to give you, and you will be satisfied).
5. The most sorrowful verse in the Qurʾān: {«Man yaʿmal sūʾan yujzā bihi»} (Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it).
6. The most severe verse in the Qurʾān — i.e., upon the people of the Fire: {«Fa-dhūqū fa-lan nazīdakum illā ʿadhābā»} (So taste [the punishment], for We will not increase you except in torment).
7. And from ʿAlī (may Allah honor his face): The most beloved verse to me in the Qurʾān: {«Inna Allāha lā yaghfiru an yushraka bihi wa-yaghfiru mā dūna dhālika li-man yashāʾ»} (Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills).
8. And the most virtuous verse in the Qurʾān: {«Wa-mā aṣābakum min muṣībatin fa-bi-mā kasabat aydīkum wa-yaʿfū ʿan kathīr»} (And whatever misfortune strikes you is due to what your hands have earned, and He pardons much).
End. [From] al-Itqān 2/205.

chapters.title_en: Concluding Word — The Third Revised Edition of *Al-Tibyān*
chapters.arabic_text:
| كلمة الختام
# لقد تم - والحمد الله تعالى - تنقيح الطبعة الثالثة لكتاب التبيان،

وإبرازها في ثوبها الجديد، وطباعتها الانيقة في المدينة المنورة، على

ساكنها أفضل التحية، وأطيب الصلاة، وأتم التسليم، أيام هجرتي في أوائل

الحرم في 1414 ه.
# فالله أسأل أن ينظمني في سلك حملة القرآن، الذين يحلون حلاله، ويحرمون

حرامه، ويرعون حدوده، ويجيدون تلاوته، وأن يميتني على حبهم، وأن يحشرني في

زمرتهم وتحت لوائهم فأهل القرآن أهل الله، وسدنة كتابه، وأن يتقبل مني ما

قدمت من عمل، وأن يمنحني حسن الختام عند انتهاء الاجل
# نزيل المدينة المنورة
# الفقير إليه تعالى
# محمد محمود الحجار
chapters.anchors:
- Root: خ-ت-م (kh-t-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Sealing, concluding, imprinting a final mark upon a thing; the end that encloses and completes.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, *khatm* signifies the final seal of a matter—whether of revelation (seal of prophets) or of one's life (seal of deeds, *khatm al-ʿamal*).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: physical sealing (e.g., sealing a vessel). Metaphorical: concluding a discourse or a book, as here—the closing word (*kalimat al-khitām*).
- Sībawayh Rule: *Al-ʿAṭf bi-lā Takrār* (Coordination without repetition) — The series of verbs and nouns joined by *wa* (e.g., "يحلون... ويحرمون... ويرعون... ويجيدون") maintains a single governing syntactic frame, each clause sharing the same subject (*ḥamalat al-Qurʾān*), with no need for resumptive pronouns beyond the implicit ones.
chapters.translation:
I say: The third edition of the book *Al-Tibyān* has been completed—praise be to God Most High—and brought forth in its new garb, printed with elegance in the illuminated city of Madīnah, upon whose dweller be the best of greetings, the purest of prayers, and the most complete of salutations, during the days of my emigration in the early days of the sacred precinct, in the year 1414 AH (1993 CE).

I ask God to enroll me in the ranks of the bearers of the Qurʾān—those who deem lawful its lawful, deem unlawful its unlawful, observe its boundaries, and perfect its recitation—and to cause me to die upon love of them, and to gather me in their company and beneath their banner, for the people of the Qurʾān are the people of God and the custodians of His Book. And I ask Him to accept from me the work I have presented, and to grant me a goodly end (*ḥusn al-khitām*) at the termination of my appointed term.

— The resident of the illuminated Madīnah,
The one in need of Him Most High,
Muḥammad Maḥmūd al-Ḥajjār.

chapters.title_en: Section 30 — Clarification of Names, Terms, and Linguistic Variants in the Book
chapters.arabic_text:
وسلم
# 
# * الدارمي هو أبو محمد عبد الله بن عبد الرحمن منسوب الى دارم جد قبيلة
# * شعائر الله تعالى معالم دينه واحدتها شعيرة قال الجوهري ويقال في

الواحدة شعارة
# * البزار صاحب المسند بالراء في آخره
# * لحد القبر بفتح اللام وضمها لغتان مشهورتان والفتح أفصح وهو شق في

جانبه القبلي يدخل فيه الميت يقال لحدت الميت وألحدته
# * أبو هريرة اسمه عبد الرحمن بن صخر على الأصح من نحو ثلاثين قولا كني

بهريرة وسلم كانت له في صغره وهو أول من كني بهذا
# 
# * آذنني بالحرب أعلمني ومعناه أظهر محاربتي
# *أبو حنيفة بن النعمان بن ثابت بن زوطي الامام الشافعي
# *أبو عبد الله محمد بن ادريس بن العباس بن عثمان بن شافع بن السائب بن

عبيد بن عبد يزيد بن يزيد بن هاشم بن المطلب بن عبد مناف بن قصي
# * الثلب بفتح الثاء المثلثة واسكان اللام هو العيب
# * حنفاء جمع حنيف وهو المستقيم وقيل المائل الى الحق المعرض عن الباطل
# *المرعشي بفتح الميم وإسكان الراء وفتح العين المهملة
# 
# * التستري بضم التاء الأولى وفتح الثانية وإسكان السين المهملة منسوب إلى

تستر المدينة المعروفة
# * الإمام المحاسبي بضم الميم قال السمعاني قيل له ذلك لانه كان يحاسب

نفسه وهو ممن جمع له علم الظاهر والباطن
# * عرف الجنة بفتح العين وإسكان الراء وبالفاء ريحها
# * فليتبوا مقعده من النار أي فلينزله وقيل فليتخذه وقيل هو دعاء وقيل خبر
# * الدلالة بفتح الدال وكسرها ويقال دلولة عنه بضم الدال واللام
# * الطوية بفتح الطاء وكسر الواو قال أهل اللغة هي الضمير
# * التراقي جمع ترقوة وهو العظم الذي بين نقرة النحر والعاتق
# 
# * يجلسون حلقا يقال بفتح الحاء وكسرها  لغتان
# * ابن ماجه هو أبو عبد الله بن محمد بن يزيد
# * أبو الدرداء اسمه عويمر وقيل عامر
# 
# * يحنو على الطالب أي يعطف عليه ويشفق
# * أيوب السختياني بفتح السين وكسر التاء قال أبو عمر بن عبد البر كان

أيوب يبيع الجلود بالبصرة ولهذا قيل السختياني
# 
# [ ... ]
# 
# * البراعة مصدر برع الرجل وبرع بفتح الراء وضمها إذا فاق أصحابه
# * حلقة العلم ونحوها باسكان اللام هذه هي اللغة الفصيحة المشهورة ويقال

بفتحها في لغة قليلة حكاها ثعلب والجوهري وغيرهما
# * الرفعة بضم الراء وكسرها لغتان
# * قعدة المتعلمين بكسر القاف
# * المعشر الجماعة الذين أمرهم واحد
# * قوله ويتفقدونها بالنهار أي يعملون بما فيها
# * أبو سليمان الخطابي منسوب إلى جد من إجداده اسمه الخطاب واسم ابي

سليمان محمد بن محمد بن ابراهيم بن الخطاب وقيل اسمه أحمد
# * الزهري هو أبو بكر محمد بن مسلم بن عبيد الله بن عبد الله بن شهاب بن

عبد الله بن الحارث بن زهرة بن كلاب بن مرة بن كعب
# * البصري بفتح الباء وكسرها
# * الشعبي بفتح الشين اسمه عامر بن شراحيل بفتح الشين
# 
# * تميم الداري منسوب إلى دارين موضع بالساحل ويقال تميم الديري نسبة إلى

دير كان يتعبد فيه وقيل غير ذلك وقد أوضحت الخلاف فيه في أول شرح صحيح مسلم
# * سليم بن عترة بكسر العين المهملة وإسكان التاء المثناة فوق
# * الدورقي بدال مهملة مفتوحة ثم واو ساكنة ثم راء مفتوحة ثم قاف ثم ياء

النسب قيل إنها نسبة إلى القلانس الطوال التي تسمى الدورقية وقيل كان أبونا

ناسكا أي عابدأ وكان في ذلك الزمن يسمون الناسك دورقيا وقيل نسبة الى دورق

بلدة بفارس أو غيرها
# * منصور بن زاذان بالزاي والذال المعجمة
# * قوله يحتبي أي ينصب ساقيه ويحتوي على ملتقى ساقيه وفخذيه بيديه أو بثوب

والحبوة بضم الحاء وكسرها لغتان هي ذلك الفعل
# * الهذرمة بالذال المعجمة سرعة الكلام الخفي
# * الغزالي هو محمد بن محمد بن محمد بن أحمد وهكذا يقال بتشديد الزاي وقد

روي عنه أنه أنكر هذا وقال إنما أنا الغزالي بتخفيف الزاي  منسوب إلى قرية

من قرى طوس يقال لها غزالة
# 
# * طلحة بن مصرف بضم الميم وفتح الصاد وكسر الراء وقيل يجوز فتح الراء

وليس بشئ
# * أبو الأحوص بالحاء والصاد المهملتين واسمه عوف بن مالك الجشمي بضم

الجيم وفتح الشين المعجمة منسوب إلى جشم جد القبيلة
# * الفسطاط فيه ست لغات فستاط بالتاء بدل الطاء وفساط بتشديد السين والفاء
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Knowledge, sign, marker; a thing by which something else is known.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, ʿalam denotes a distinguishing sign of divine commands or rites (shaʿāʾir).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: a physical mark; metaphorical: any indicator of religious obligation or identity.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — Proper nouns and epithets are clarified by apposition, as in genealogical chains (e.g., "Abū ʿAbd Allāh Muḥammad ibn Idrīs...").
chapters.translation:
I say — and success is from God alone:

The Dārimī is Abū Muḥammad ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, attributed to Dārim, the ancestor of a tribe.

The shaʿāʾir of God — may He be exalted — are the landmarks of His religion; the singular is shaʿīrah. Al-Jawharī said: and one may say in the singular shaʿārah.

The Bazzār is the compiler of the Musnad, with an rāʾ at its end.

The laḥd of the grave — with fatḥ of the lām and ḍamm of it — are two well-known variant readings; the fatḥ is the more eloquent. It is a niche in its qiblī side into which the deceased is placed. One says: "laḥadtu al-mayyita" and "alḥadtuhu" (I made a laḥd for the deceased).

Abū Hurayrah — his name is ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ṣakhr according to the most correct of some thirty opinions. He was nicknamed Abū Hurayrah after a kitten (huraynah) he had in his youth, and he was the first to be so nicknamed.

"Ādhananī bil-ḥarb" means "he informed me of war," and its meaning is "he manifested his enmity toward me."

Abū Ḥanīfah is al-Nuʿmān ibn Thābit ibn Zūṭī — the Imām al-Shāfiʿī [i.e., the founder of the Ḥanafī school, so named for his lineage].

Abū ʿAbd Allāh Muḥammad ibn Idrīs ibn al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿUthmān ibn Shāfiʿ ibn al-Sāʾib ibn ʿUbayd ibn ʿAbd Yazīd ibn Yazīd ibn Hāshim ibn al-Muṭṭalib ibn ʿAbd Manāf ibn Quṣayy [this is the full genealogy of Imām al-Shāfiʿī].

Al-thalb — with fatḥ of the thāʾ (the dotted thāʾ) and sukūn of the lām — is "defect" or "blemish."

Ḥanafāʾ is the plural of ḥanīf, meaning "upright" or, it is said, "one who inclines to the truth and turns away from falsehood."

Al-Marʿashī — with fatḥ of the mīm, sukūn of the rāʾ, and fatḥ of the ʿayn (the unpointed ʿayn) — is an attribution.

Al-Tustarī — with ḍamm of the first tāʾ, fatḥ of the second, and sukūn of the sīn (the unpointed sīn) — is attributed to Tustar, the well-known city.

The Imām al-Muḥāsibī — with ḍamm of the mīm. Al-Samʿānī said: he was so called because he used to reckon with himself (yuḥāsibu nafsahu), and he was one of those who combined knowledge of the outward and the inward.

"ʿArf al-jannah" — with fatḥ of the ʿayn, sukūn of the rāʾ, and with a fāʾ — is its fragrance.

"Falyatabawwaʾ maqʿadahu min al-nār" — i.e., "let him take up his seat in the Fire"; or it is said, "let him prepare it"; or it is said, it is a supplication; or it is said, it is a declarative statement.

Al-dalālah — with fatḥ of the dāl and kasr of it — and one says "dalwalah" with ḍamm of the dāl and lām — [meaning: to be left unburied, exposed].

Al-ṭawiyyah — with fatḥ of the ṭāʾ and kasr of the wāw — the linguists say it is "the inner conscience" (al-ḍamīr).

Al-tarāqī is the plural of turquwah, which is the bone between the hollow of the throat and the shoulder.

"They sit in circles (ḥilaqan)" — one says with fatḥ of the ḥāʾ and kasr of it; two variant readings.

Ibn Mājah is Abū ʿAbd Allāh Muḥammad ibn Yazīd.

Abū al-Dardāʾ — his name is ʿUwaymir, and it is said ʿĀmir.

"Yaḥnū ʿalā al-ṭālib" — i.e., he inclines toward him with compassion and tenderness.

Ayyūb al-Sakhtiyānī — with fatḥ of the sīn and kasr of the tāʾ. Abū ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-Barr said: Ayyūb used to sell hides in Baṣrah, and for this reason he was called al-Sakhtiyānī.

[ ... ]

Al-barāʿah is the verbal noun of "baraʿa al-rajul" and "bariʿa" — with fatḥ of the rāʾ and ḍamm of it — when he surpasses his companions.

"Ḥalqat al-ʿilm" and the like — with sukūn of the lām — this is the eloquent and well-known form; one may also say it with fatḥ of the lām in a rare dialect, as related by Thaʿlab, al-Jawharī, and others.

Al-rifʿah — with ḍamm of the rāʾ and kasr of it — two variant readings.

"Qiʿdat al-mutaʿallimīn" — with kasr of the qāf.

Al-maʿshar is a group whose affair is one.

His saying: "and they examine it (yatafaqqadūnahā) by day" — i.e., they act upon what is in it.

Abū Sulaymān al-Khaṭṭābī is attributed to one of his forefathers named al-Khaṭṭāb. The name of Abū Sulaymān is Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm ibn al-Khaṭṭāb; and it is said his name was Aḥmad.

Al-Zuhrī is Abū Bakr Muḥammad ibn Muslim ibn ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shihāb ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Zuhrah ibn Kilāb ibn Murrah ibn Kaʿb.

Al-Baṣrī — with fatḥ of the bāʾ and kasr of it.

Al-Shaʿbī — with fatḥ of the shīn — his name is ʿĀmir ibn Sharāḥīl, with fatḥ of the shīn.

Tamīm al-Dārī is attributed to Dārin, a place on the coast; and it is said Tamīm al-Dayrī, attributed to a monastery (dayr) in which he used to worship; and other opinions are mentioned. I have already clarified the disagreement concerning this at the beginning of my commentary on Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim.

Sulaym ibn ʿItrah — with kasr of the ʿayn (the unpointed ʿayn) and sukūn of the tāʾ (the dotted tāʾ above).

Al-Dūraqī — with an unpointed dāl, fatḥa, then a sukūn wāw, then a fatḥa rāʾ, then a qāf, then the yāʾ of attribution. It is said this is an attribution to the tall conical caps called al-dūraqiyyah; and it is said that his father was a devotee (nāsik), i.e., a worshipper, and in that time devotees were called dūraqī; and it is said it is an attribution to Dūraq, a town in Persia, or other places.

Manṣūr ibn Zādān — with zāy and the dotted dhāl.

His saying: "yaḥtabī" — i.e., he erects his shins and wraps his hands or garment around the meeting point of his shins and thighs. "Al-ḥabwah" — with ḍamm of the ḥāʾ and kasr of it, two variants — is that very action.

Al-hadharamah — with the dotted dhāl — is the rapidity of speech that is indistinct.

Al-Ghazālī is Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad — and thus it is said with tashdīd of the zāy. It is related from him that he rejected this and said: "I am only al-Ghazālī with takhfīf of the zāy," attributed to a village of Ṭūs called Ghazālah.

Ṭalḥah ibn Muṣarrif — with ḍamm of the mīm, fatḥ of the ṣād, and kasr of the rāʾ; and it is said the fatḥ of the rāʾ is permissible, but it is nothing.

Abū al-Aḥwaṣ — with the unpointed ḥāʾ and ṣād — his name is ʿAwf ibn Mālik al-Jushamī, with ḍamm of the jīm and fatḥ of the dotted shīn, attributed to Jusham, the ancestor of the tribe.

Al-Fusṭāṭ — it has six variant forms: "Fusṭāt" with tāʾ in place of ṭāʾ, "Fusāṭ" with tashdīd of the sīn and the fāʾ...

chapters.title_en: Section 31 — Clarification of Problematic Words and Names in the Book
chapters.arabic_text:
فيهن مضمومة ومكسورة والمراد به الخيمة والمنزل
# * الدوي بفتح الدال وكسر الواو وتشديد الياء صوت لا يفهم
# * النخعي بفتح النون والخاء منسوب الى النخعي جد قبيلة
# * حلب شاة بفتح اللام ويجوز اسكانها في لغة قليلة
# * الرقاشي بفتح الراء وتخفيف القاف
# * القذاة كالعود وفتات الخرق ونحوها مما يكنس المسجد منه
# * سليمان بن يسار بالمثناة ثم السين المهملة
# 
# * أبو أسيد بضم الهمزة وفتح السين اسمه مالك بن ربيعة شهد بدرا
# * تنطحني بكسر الطاء وفتحها
# * منتشر جدا بكسر الجيم وهو مصدر
# * الأشنان بضم الهمزة وكسرها لغتان ذكرهما أبو عبيدة وهمزة أشنان: أصلية.
# * وابن الجواليقي هو فارسي معرب وهو بالعربية المحضة حرض
# * كراسي أضراسه يجوز فيه التشديد والتخفيف
# * والروياني بضم الراء وإسكان الواو منسوب إلى رويان
# * قوله على حسب حاله هو بفتح السين اي على قدر طاقته
# * الحمام معروف وهو مذكر عند أهل اللغة
# 
# * الحشوش مواضع العذرة والبول المتخذة له واحدها حش بفتح الحاء وضمها

لغتان
# * حجر الانسان بفتح الحاء وكسرها
# * الجنازة بكسر الجيم وفتحها من جنز إذا ستر
# * بهز بن حكيم هو بفتح الباء واسكان الهاء وبالزاي
# * زرارة بضم الزاي
# * أحمد بن أبي الحواري بفتح الحاء وكسر الراء ومنهم من يفتح الراء وكان

شيخنا أبو البقاء خالد النابلسي رحمه الله يحكيه وربما اختاره وكان علامة

وقته في هذا الفن مع كمال تحقيقة فيه واسم أبي
# * الحواري عبد الله بن ميمون بن عباس بن الحرث
# * الجرعي بضم الجيم والراء
# * أبو الجوزاء بفتح الجيم وبالزاي اسمه أوس بن عبد الله وقيل أوس بن خالد
# * حبتر بحاء مهملة مفتوحة ثم باء موحدة ساكنة ثم تاء مثناة من فوق مفتوحة

ثم  راء الرجل الصالح هو القائم بحقوق الله تعالى وحقوق العباد كذا قاله

الزجاج وصاحب المطالع وغيرهما
# 
# * أبو ذر اسمه جندب وقيل برير بضم الموحدة وتكرير الراء
# * اجترحوا السيئات اكتسبوها
# * العار بكسر الشين العلامة
# 
# * الشراك بكسر الشين هو السير الرقيق الذي يكون في النعل ظهر القدم
# * أم سلمة اسمها هند وقيل رملة وليس بشئ
# * عبد الله بن مغفل بضم الميم وفتح الغين المعجمة والفاء
# 
# * اللغط بفتح الغين وإسكانها لغتان هو اختلاط الأصوات
# * المعوذتان بكسر الواو
# * الأوزاعي اسمه عبد الرحمن بن عمر إمام الشام في عصره منسوب الى موضع

بباب الفراديس من دمشق يقال له الأوزاع وقيل إلى قبيلة وقيل غير ذلك
# * عرزب بعين مهملة مفتوحة ثم راء ساكنة ثم زاي مفتوحة ثم باء موحدة
# * بريدة بن الحصيب بضم الحاء وفتح الصاد المهملتين
# * فضالة بفتح الفاء
# 
# * لله أشد أذنا بفتح الهمزة والذال أي استماعا
# * القينة بفتح القاف المغنية
# * طوبى أي خير لهم كذا قاله أهل اللغة
# * الأعمش سليمان بن مهران
# * أبو العالية بالعين المهملة اسمه رفيع بضم الراء
# * أبو لبابة الصحابي بضم اللام اسمه بشير وقيل رفاعة بن عبد المنذر
# * الغشمة الظلمة
# * قوله عيناه تذرفان أي ينصب دمعهما وهو بفتح التاء المثناة من فوق وكسر

الراء
# * فما خطبكم أي شأنكم
# * الأيام المعدودات أيام التشريق الثلاثة بعد يوم النحر
# 
# تشميت العاطس هو بالشين وبالسين القفال المذكور هنا المروزي عبد الله بن

أحمد يقرن بضم الراء على اللغة الفصيحة وفي لغة بكسرها
# * البغوي منسوب الى بغ مدينة بين هراة ومرو ويقال لها أيضا بغشور واسمه

الحسين بن مسعود
# * الآصال جمع أصيل وهو آخر النهار وقيل ما بين العصر وغروب الشمس
# * زبيد بن الحرث بضم الزاي وبعدها موحدة مفتوحة
# * سبوح قدوس بضم أولهما وبالفتح لغتان مشهورتان
# * أبو قلابة بكسر القاف وفتح اللام وتخفيفها وبالياء الموحدة اسمة عبد

الله بن زيد
# 
# * يحيى بن وثاب بثاء مثلثة مشددة
# * معان بن رفاعة بضم الميم والعين وآخره نون
# * الشخير بكسر الشين والخاء مشددة
# * الحكم بن عتيبة هو بتاء مثناة  من فوق ثم مثناة من تحت ثم موحدة
# * المحيى والممات الحياة والموت
# * أوزعهم إلا ألههم
# * حمدأ يوافي نعمة اي يصل إليها فيحصلها
# * ويكافئ مزيده هو بهمزة آخر يكافئ ومعناه يقوم بشكر ما زادنا من النعم
# * مجالد الراوي عن الشعبي بالجيم وكسر اللام
# * الصيمري بفتح الصاد المهملة والميم وقيل بضم الميم وهو غريب
# 
# وقد بسطت بيانه في تهذيب الأسماء واللغات فهذه أحرف وجيزة في ضبط مشكل ما

وقع في هذا الكتاب وما بقي منها تركته لظهوره وما ذكرته من الظاهر قصدت

بيانه لمن لا يخالط العلماء، فإنه ينتفع به إن شاء الله تعالى.
# * * *
# هذا آخر ما تيسر مهه هذا الكتاب، وهو نبذة مختصرة بالنسبة إلى آداب

القراء.
# ولكن حملني على اختصاره ما ذكرته في أول الكتاب.
# وأنا أسأل الله العظيم أن ينفع به النفع العميم، لي ولأحبابي، وكل ناظر
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ض ب ط (ḍād-bā-ṭā)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to bind firmly, to restrain, to preserve precisely" — hence ḍabṭ (ضبط) as exact vocalization and textual control.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In scholarly transmission, ḍabṭ denotes the meticulous fixing of pronunciation and orthography to prevent corruption of sacred texts.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is physical binding (e.g., tying a beast); metaphorically applied to the "binding" of words through voweling and diacritics.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Phonetic Variants (al-Lughāt) — When multiple voweling patterns are attested for a single word, each is grammatically valid if transmitted from authoritative Arab usage; the translator must preserve the author's enumeration without preferring one over the other.
chapters.translation:
I say: Among them are words with ḍammah (u-vowel) and kasrah (i-vowel), and what is intended by "them" is the tent and the dwelling.

- *Al-Dawī (الدوي) — with fatḥah on the dāl, kasrah on the wāw, and tashdīd on the yāʾ — is a sound that is not understood.
- *Al-Nakhaʿī (النخعي) — with fatḥah on the nūn and khāʾ — is attributed to Nakhaʿ, the ancestor of a tribe.
- *Ḥalaba shātan (حلب شاة) — with fatḥah on the lām, and it is permissible to give it sukūn in a rare dialect.
- *Al-Riqāshī (الرقاشي) — with fatḥah on the rāʾ and takhfīf (no tashdīd) on the qāf.
- *Al-Qadhāh (القذاة) — like a piece of wood, or a fragment of cloth, or similar things that the mosque is swept clean of.
- *Sulaymān ibn Yasār (سليمان بن يسار) — with tāʾ mathnāh (i.e., the letter tāʾ with two dots above) then sīn without dots.

- *Abū Usayd (أبو أسيد) — with ḍammah on the hamzah and fatḥah on the sīn; his name is Mālik ibn Rabīʿah, and he witnessed the Battle of Badr.
- *Tanṭaḥunī (تنطحني) — with kasrah on the ṭāʾ and also with fatḥah on it.
- *Muntashir jiddan (منتشر جدا) — with kasrah on the jīm, and it is a verbal noun (maṣdar).
- *Al-Ushnān (الأشنان) — with ḍammah on the hamzah and also with kasrah on it; these are two dialects, both mentioned by Abū ʿUbaydah. The hamzah of "ushnān" is original (not a conjunctive hamzah).
- *And Ibn al-Jawālīqī — it is a Persian word that has been Arabized; in pure Arabic it is "ḥuraḍ" (حرض).
- *Karāsī adrāsihi (كراسي أضراسه) — it is permissible to pronounce it with tashdīd and with takhfīf (i.e., both "karāsī" and "karāsī" with or without doubling).
- *Al-Rūyānī (الروياني) — with ḍammah on the rāʾ and sukūn on the wāw, attributed to Rūyān.
- *His saying "alā ḥasbi ḥālihi" (على حسب حاله) — it is with fatḥah on the sīn, meaning "according to his capacity."
- *Al-Ḥammām (الحمام) — the well-known bathhouse; it is masculine according to the people of language.

- *Al-Ḥushūsh (الحشوش) — places designated for excrement and urine; its singular is "ḥashsh" (حش) — with fatḥah on the ḥāʾ and also with ḍammah on it; these are two dialects.
- *Ḥajar al-insān (حجر الانسان) — with fatḥah on the ḥāʾ and also with kasrah on it.
- *Al-Janāzah (الجنازة) — with kasrah on the jīm and also with fatḥah on it; derived from "janaza" (جنز) meaning "to cover."
- *Bahz ibn Ḥakīm (بهز بن حكيم) — with fatḥah on the bāʾ, sukūn on the hāʾ, and with zāy.
- *Zurārah (زرارة) — with ḍammah on the zāy.
- *Aḥmad ibn Abī al-Ḥawārī (أحمد بن أبي الحواري) — with fatḥah on the ḥāʾ and kasrah on the rāʾ; some open the rāʾ. Our teacher Abū al-Baqāʾ Khālid al-Nābulusī — may Allah have mercy on him — used to relate this variant and sometimes preferred it; he was the foremost scholar of his time in this art, with complete mastery of it. The name of Abū al-Ḥawārī is ʿAbdullāh ibn Maymūn ibn ʿAbbās ibn al-Ḥārith.
- *Al-Jurʿī (الجرعي) — with ḍammah on the jīm and the rāʾ.
- *Abū al-Jawzāʾ (أبو الجوزاء) — with fatḥah on the jīm and with zāy; his name is Aws ibn ʿAbdullāh, and it is also said Aws ibn Khālid.
- *Ḥabtar (حبتر) — with an unpointed ḥāʾ opened, then a bāʾ with one dot and sukūn, then a tāʾ with two dots from above opened, then a rāʾ. [It refers to] the righteous man — he is the one who upholds the rights of Allah the Exalted and the rights of the servants. Thus said al-Zajjāj, the author of al-Maṭāliʿ, and others.

- *Abū Dharr (أبو ذر) — his name is Jundab, and it is also said Burayr — with ḍammah on the bāʾ and repetition of the rāʾ.
- *Ijtaraḥū al-sayyiʾāt (اجترحوا السيئات) — meaning they earned/committed them.
- *Al-ʿār (العار) — with kasrah on the shīn (i.e., al-ʿishār) — meaning the mark/sign.

- *Al-Shirāk (الشراك) — with kasrah on the shīn — is the thin strap that is on the top of the foot in the sandal.
- *Umm Salamah (أم سلمة) — her name is Hind, and it is also said Ramlah, but that is nothing (i.e., not sound).
- *ʿAbdullāh ibn Mughaffal (عبد الله بن مغفل) — with ḍammah on the mīm, fatḥah on the ghayn muʿjamah (i.e., with a dot above), and the fāʾ.

- *Al-Laghaṭ (اللغط) — with fatḥah on the ghayn and also with sukūn on it; these are two dialects. It is the mixing/confusion of voices.
- *Al-Muʿawwidhatān (المعوذتان) — with kasrah on the wāw.
- *Al-Awzāʿī (الأوزاعي) — his name is ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAmr, the Imām of Syria in his time; attributed to a place at the gate of al-Farādīs in Damascus called al-Awzāʿ; and it is also said [attributed] to a tribe, and other opinions exist.
- *ʿArzab (عرزب) — with an unpointed ʿayn opened, then a rāʾ with sukūn, then a zāy opened, then a bāʾ with one dot.
- *Buraydah ibn al-Ḥuṣayb (بريدة بن الحصيب) — with ḍammah on the ḥāʾ and fatḥah on the ṣād, both unpointed.
- *Fuḍālah (فضالة) — with fatḥah on the fāʾ.

- *"Lillāhi ashaddu adhanan" (لله أشد أذنا) — with fatḥah on the hamzah and the dhāl, i.e., more intense listening.
- *Al-Qaynah (القينة) — with fatḥah on the qāf — the singing slave-girl.
- *Ṭūbā (طوبى) — meaning "goodness for them"; thus said the people of language.
- *Al-Aʿmash (الأعمش) — Sulaymān ibn Mahrān.
- *Abū al-ʿĀliyah (أبو العالية) — with the unpointed ʿayn; his name is Rufayʿ — with ḍammah on the rāʾ.
- *Abū Lubābah al-Ṣaḥābī (أبو لبابة الصحابي) — with ḍammah on the lām; his name is Bashīr, and it is also said Rifāʿah ibn ʿAbd al-Mundhir.
- *Al-Ghashmah (الغشمة) — the darkness.
- *His saying "ʿaynāhu tadhrifāni" (عيناه تذرفان) — meaning his tears flow; it is with fatḥah on the tāʾ mathnāh (i.e., the tāʾ with two dots from above) and kasrah on the rāʾ.
- *"Fa-mā khaṭbukum" (فما خطبكم) — meaning "what is your affair/matter."
- *Al-Ayyām al-Maʿdūdāt (الأيام المعدودات) — the three days of Tashrīq following the Day of Sacrifice (al-Naḥr).

- *Tashmīt al-ʿāṭis (تشميت العاطس) — it is with shīn and also with sīn. The al-Qaffāl mentioned here, al-Marwazī, ʿAbdullāh ibn Aḥmad — "yuqran" (يقرن) with ḍammah on the rāʾ in the eloquent dialect, and in another dialect with kasrah on it.
- *Al-Baghawī (البغوي) — attributed to Bagh, a city between Herāt and Marw, also called Baghshūr; his name is al-Ḥusayn ibn Masʿūd.
- *Al-Āṣāl (الآصال) — plural of "aṣīl" (أصيل), which is the end of the day; and it is said [it is] between the ʿAṣr prayer and sunset.
- *Zubayd ibn al-Ḥārith (زبيد بن الحرث) — with ḍammah on the zāy, followed by an opened bāʾ with one dot.
- *Subbūḥ Quddūs (سبوح قدوس) — with ḍammah on the first letter of each, and with fatḥah — two well-known dialects.
- *Abū Qilābah (أبو قلابة) — with kasrah on the qāf, fatḥah on the lām with takhfīf (no tashdīd), and with yāʾ with one dot (i.e., the second element is "qilābah" with yāʾ); his name is ʿAbdullāh ibn Zayd.

- *Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb (يحيى بن وثاب) — with a thāʾ with three dots, mushaddad (doubled).
- *Muʿān ibn Rifāʿah (معان بن رفاعة) — with ḍammah on the mīm and ʿayn, and its final letter is nūn.
- *Al-Shakhīr (الشخير) — with kasrah on the shīn and khāʾ, with tashdīd on the khāʾ.
- *Al-Ḥakam ibn ʿUtaybah (الحكم بن عتيبة) — it is with tāʾ mathnāh from above (i.e., tāʾ with two dots), then tāʾ mathnāh from below (i.e., yāʾ with two dots), then bāʾ with one dot.
- *Al-Muḥyī wa al-Mumāt (المحيى والممات) — life and death.
- *Awziʿhum (أوزعهم) — meaning "make me grateful" (alhimhum).
- *Ḥamdan yuwāfī niʿmah (حمدأ يوافي نعمة) — meaning it reaches it and thus obtains it.
- *Wa yukāfiʾu mazīdah (ويكافئ مزيده) — it is with a hamzah at the end, "yukāfiʾ" (يكافئ), and its meaning is: he undertakes to give thanks for the additional blessings Allah has given us.
- *Mujālid (مجالد) — the narrator from al-Shaʿbī — with jīm and kasrah on the lām.
- *Al-Ṣaymarī (الصيمري) — with fatḥah on the unpointed ṣād and the mīm; and it is said with ḍammah on the mīm, but that is odd (gharīb).

I have already expanded its explanation in Tahdhīb al-Asmāʾ wa al-Lughāt. These are concise notes on the precise vocalization of what is problematic in this book. What remains of them I have left out due to its obviousness. And what I have mentioned of the apparent, I intended to clarify for the one who does not mix with scholars, for he will benefit from it, Allah willing.

* * *

This is the end of what was facilitated of this book. It is a brief excerpt relative to the etiquette of Qurʾān readers. But what compelled me to abbreviate it is what I mentioned at the beginning of the book. And I ask Allah the Magnificent to grant through it abundant benefit — for me, for my beloved ones, and for every reader/observer.

chapters.title_en: Section 32 — Concluding Supplications, Appended Benefits, and Closing Remarks
chapters.arabic_text: فيه وسائر المسلمين في الدارين. # والحمد الله رب العالمين حمدا يوافي نعمه ويكافي مزيده، وصلاته وسلامه الأكملان على سيدنا محمد، وعلى آل محمد، وأصحابه أجمعين والحمد الله رب العالمين. # اه. إلى هنا تم كتاب التبيان. # | الفوائد المزيدة على الكتاب | | لطيفة # # قال ابن الجوزي في كتاب " مناقب الامام أحمد بن حنبل " ص 434 في الباب الحادي والتسعين في ذكر المنامات التي رآها أحمد بن حنبل رضي الله تعالى عنه: أخبرنا عبد الملك بن أبي القاسم، قال: أنا عبد الله بن محمد الانصاري، قال: أنا محمد بن عبد الجليل بن أحمد، قال: أنا محمد بن أحمد بن إبراهيم، وأخبرنا ابن ناصر، قال: أنبأنا أبو علي الحسن بن أحمد، قال: أنا أبو محمد الخلال، قال: أنا عبيد الله بن عبد الرحمن الزهري، قالا: حدثنا أحمد بن محمد بن معثم، قال: سمعت عبد العزيز بن أحمد النهاوندي قال: سمعت عبد الله بن أحمد بن حنبل قال: سمعت أبي يقول: * رأيت رب العزة في المنام فقلت: يا رب ما أفضل ما تقرب به المتقربون إليك؟ * فقال: كلامي يا أحمد # * قال فقلت: يا رب بفهم أو بغير فهم؟ # # * قال: بفهم وبغير فهم. اه. # أنظر مناقب الامام أحمد، مطبعة دار الافاق الجديدة ط الثانية 1977 م. | | لطيفة # # عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أنه قال: ثمان أيات نزلت في سورة النساء خير لهذه الامة مما طلعت عليه الشمس: # * 1 -: (يريد الله ليبين لكم ويهديكم سنن الذين من قبلكم ويتوب عليكم) . # * 2 -: (والله يريد أن يتوب عليكم ويريد الذين يتبعون الشهوات أن تميلوا ميلا عظيما) . # ، 3 -: (يريد الله أن يخفف عنكم وخلق الانسان ضعيفا) . # * 4 -: (إن تجتنبوا كبائر ما تنهون عنه نكفر عنكم سيئاتكم وندخلكم مدخلا كريما) . # * 5 -: (إن الله لا يظلم مثقال ذرة وإن تك حسنة يضاعفها ويؤت من لدنه أجرا عظيما) . # * 6 -: (ومن يعمل سوءا أو يظلم نفسه ثم يستغفر الله يجد الله غفورا رحيما) . # * 7 -: (إن الله لا يغفر أن يشرك به ويغفر ما دون ذلك لمن يشاء) . # * 8 -: (والذين ءامنوا بالله ورسله، ولم يفرقوا بين أحد منهم # # أولئك سوف يؤتيهم أجورهم وكان الله غفورا رحيما) . # اه الاتقان 2 / 206 | لطيفة # * 1 -: إن أعظم آية في القرآن، (الله لا إله إلا هو الحي القيوم) . # * 2 -: وأعدل آية في القرآن، (إن الله يأمر بالعدل والاحسان وإيتائ ذى القربى) الاية ... * 3 -: وأخوف آية في القرآن، (فمن يعمل مثقال ذرة خيرا يره (7) ومن يعمل مثقال ذرة شرا يره) . # * 4 -: وأرجي آية في القرآن، (قل يعبادي الذين أسرفوا على أنفسهم لا تقنطوا من رحمة الله) الاية ... وقيل: (ولسوف يعطيك ربك فترضى) . # * 5 -: وأحزن آية في القرآن، (من يعمل سوءا يجزيه) . # * 6 -: وأشد آية في القرآن، - أي على أهل النار - (فذوقوا فلن نزيد كم إلا عذابا) . # * 7 -: وعن علي كرم الله وجهه: أحب آية إلى في القرآن، (إن الله لا يغفرأن يشرك به ويغفر ما دون ذلك لمن يشاء) . # * 8 -: وأفضل آية في القرآن، (وما أصابكم من مصيبة فبما كسبت أيديكم ويعفوا عن كثير) . # اه الاتقان 2 / 205 # | كلمة الختام # لقد تم - والحمد الله تعالى - تنقيح الطبعة الثالثة لكتاب التبيان، وإبرازها في ثوبها الجديد، وطباعتها الانيقة في المدينة المنورة، على ساكنها أفضل التحية، وأطيب الصلاة، وأتم التسليم، أيام هجرتي في أوائل الحرم في 1414 ه. # فالله أسأل أن ينظمني في سلك حملة القرآن، الذين يحلون حلاله، ويحرمون حرامه، ويرعون حدوده، ويجيدون تلاوته، وأن يميتني على حبهم، وأن يحشرني في زمرتهم وتحت لوائهم فأهل القرآن أهل الله، وسدنة كتابه، وأن يتقبل مني ما قدمت من عمل، وأن يمنحني حسن الختام عند انتهاء الاجل # نزيل المدينة المنورة # الفقير إليه تعالى # محمد محمود الحجار
chapters.anchors:
- Root: د-ع-و (da-ʿa-wa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Invocation, supplication, calling upon; the act of beseeching with humility.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Duʿā as the essence of worship (ʿibādah), the creature's acknowledgment of need before the Creator.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) in the sense of direct address; metaphorical (majāz) when referring to the Quran's "call" to guidance.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — The phrase "وسائر المسلمين في الدارين" is an appositive to the preceding supplication, extending the prayer's scope to all Muslims in both abodes.
chapters.translation:
And upon him, and upon all Muslims, in both abodes [this world and the Hereafter].

And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds — a praise that corresponds to His blessings and suffices for His increase — and His prayers and peace, the most complete of them, be upon our Master Muḥammad, and upon the family of Muḥammad, and upon all his Companions. And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds. End. Here concludes the Book of al-Tibyān.

---

| ADDITIONAL BENEFITS APPENDED TO THE BOOK |

| A Subtle Point (Laṭīfah) |

Ibn al-Jawzī said in his book "Manāqib al-Imām Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal" (p. 434), in Chapter Ninety-One, concerning the dreams seen by Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal (may Allah be pleased with him): ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Abī al-Qāsim informed us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad al-Anṣārī told us, saying: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jalīl ibn Aḥmad told us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Ibrāhīm told us — and Ibn Nāṣir also informed us, saying: Abū ʿAlī al-Ḥasan ibn Aḥmad told us, saying: Abū Muḥammad al-Khallāl told us, saying: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Zuhrī told us — both chains said: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Maʿtham narrated to us, saying: I heard ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Aḥmad al-Nahāwandī say: I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal say: I heard my father say: *I saw the Lord of Might in a dream, and I said: "O my Lord, what is the most excellent thing by which those who draw near draw near to You?"* He said: *"My Speech (Kalāmī), O Aḥmad."* *I said: "O my Lord, with understanding (bi-fahm) or without understanding?"* *He said: "With understanding and without understanding."* End. See Manāqib al-Imām Aḥmad, Dār al-Āfāq al-Jadīdah Press, 2nd edition, 1977 CE.

---

| A Subtle Point (Laṭīfah) |

On the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them both) that he said: Eight verses revealed in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ are better for this nation than all that the sun has risen upon:
1. {«يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ لِيُبَيِّنَ لَكُمْ وَيَهْدِيَكُمْ سُنَنَ الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ وَيَتُوبَ عَلَيْكُمْ»} (Allah desires to make clear to you and guide you to the ways of those before you and to accept your repentance) [4:26].
2. {«وَاللَّهُ يُرِيدُ أَن يَتُوبَ عَلَيْكُمْ وَيُرِيدُ الَّذِينَ يَتَّبِعُونَ الشَّهَوَاتِ أَن تَمِيلُوا مَيْلًا عَظِيمًا»} (And Allah desires to accept your repentance, but those who follow lusts desire that you deviate with great deviation) [4:27].
3. {«يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ أَن يُخَفِّفَ عَنكُمْ وَخُلِقَ الْإِنسَانُ ضَعِيفًا»} (Allah desires to lighten your burden, for man was created weak) [4:28].
4. {«إِن تَجْتَنِبُوا كَبَائِرَ مَا تُنْهَوْنَ عَنْهُ نُكَفِّرْ عَنكُمْ سَيِّئَاتِكُمْ وَنُدْخِلْكُم مُّدْخَلًا كَرِيمًا»} (If you avoid the great sins you are forbidden, We will expiate your evil deeds and admit you to a noble entrance) [4:31].
5. {«إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَظْلِمُ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ وَإِن تَكُ حَسَنَةً يُضَاعِفْهَا وَيُؤْتِ مِن لَّدُنْهُ أَجْرًا عَظِيمًا»} (Indeed, Allah does not wrong even the weight of an atom; and if there is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward) [4:40].
6. {«وَمَن يَعْمَلْ سُوءًا أَوْ يَظْلِمْ نَفْسَهُ ثُمَّ يَسْتَغْفِرِ اللَّهَ يَجِدِ اللَّهَ غَفُورًا رَّحِيمًا»} (And whoever does evil or wrongs himself, then seeks Allah's forgiveness, will find Allah Forgiving, Merciful) [4:110].
7. {«إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَغْفِرُ أَن يُشْرَكَ بِهِ وَيَغْفِرُ مَا دُونَ ذَٰلِكَ لِمَن يَشَاءُ»} (Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but forgives what is less than that for whom He wills) [4:48].
8. {«وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرُسُلِهِ وَلَمْ يُفَرِّقُوا بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ مِّنْهُمْ أُولَٰئِكَ سَوْفَ يُؤْتِيهِمْ أُجُورَهُمْ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ غَفُورًا رَّحِيمًا»} (And those who believe in Allah and His messengers and do not differentiate between any of them — those He will give their rewards, and Allah is Forgiving, Merciful) [4:152].
End. [From] al-Itqān, 2/206.

---

| A Subtle Point (Laṭīfah) |

1. The greatest verse in the Quran: {«اللَّهُ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ»} (Allah — there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining) [2:255].
2. The most just verse in the Quran: {«إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَأْمُرُ بِالْعَدْلِ وَالْإِحْسَانِ وَإِيتَاءِ ذِي الْقُرْبَىٰ»} (Indeed, Allah commands justice, excellence, and giving to near relatives) [16:90] — to the end of the verse.
3. The most fear-inducing verse in the Quran: {«فَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَيْرًا يَرَهُ (7) وَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ شَرًّا يَرَهُ»} (So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it) [99:7-8].
4. The most hope-inspiring verse in the Quran: {«قُلْ يَا عِبَادِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا عَلَىٰ أَنفُسِهِمْ لَا تَقْنَطُوا مِن رَّحْمَةِ اللَّهِ»} (Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of Allah's mercy) [39:53] — to the end of the verse. And it is also said: {«وَلَسَوْفَ يُعْطِيكَ رَبُّكَ فَتَرْضَىٰ»} (And your Lord will give you, and you will be satisfied) [93:5].
5. The most sorrowful verse in the Quran: {«مَن يَعْمَلْ سُوءًا يُجْزَ بِهِ»} (Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it) [4:123].
6. The most severe verse in the Quran — that is, upon the people of the Fire: {«فَذُوقُوا فَلَن نَّزِيدَكُمْ إِلَّا عَذَابًا»} (So taste — for We will not increase you except in punishment) [78:30].
7. And on the authority of ʿAlī (may Allah honor his face): The most beloved verse to me in the Quran: {«إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَغْفِرُ أَن يُشْرَكَ بِهِ وَيَغْفِرُ مَا دُونَ ذَٰلِكَ لِمَن يَشَاءُ»} (Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but forgives what is less than that for whom He wills) [4:48].
8. And the most virtuous verse in the Quran: {«وَمَا أَصَابَكُم مِّن مُّصِيبَةٍ فَبِمَا كَسَبَتْ أَيْدِيكُمْ وَيَعْفُو عَن كَثِيرٍ»} (And whatever misfortune strikes you is due to what your hands have earned, and He pardons much) [42:30].
End. [From] al-Itqān, 2/205.

---

| THE CLOSING WORD |

Indeed — and praise be to Allah, the Exalted — the revision of the third edition of the Book of al-Tibyān has been completed, and it has been brought forth in its new garb, with its elegant printing in al-Madīnah al-Munawwarah — upon its dweller be the finest greeting, the purest prayers, and the most complete salutations — during the days of my emigration (hijrah) in the early days of the Sacred Month (al-Ḥaram) in the year 1414 AH (1993 CE).

I ask Allah to enroll me in the ranks of the bearers of the Quran — those who deem lawful its lawful, deem unlawful its unlawful, observe its limits, and perfect its recitation — and to cause me to die upon love of them, and to gather me in their company and beneath their banner. For the people of the Quran are the people of Allah and the custodians of His Book. And I ask Him to accept from me the work I have presented, and to grant me a good end (ḥusn al-khātimah) at the termination of my appointed term.

— Resident of al-Madīnah al-Munawwarah,
The poor one in need of Him, the Exalted,
Muḥammad Maḥmūd al-Ḥajjār.
